difficulty:0.en: The power went out at 2 a.m., and I stood behind the counter with only a small torch. The real *difficulty* was not the dark — it was reading the handwritten price list the Manager had taped to the shelf years ago. Tang appeared from the back room holding a second torch and grinning. 'Two lights are better than one,' he said.
difficulty:0.cnHint: 停电后，我发现阅读店长那张手写价目表才是最大的____。
difficulty:0.hook: Then a regular walked in, carrying something none of us expected.
difficulty:0.line: 'The *difficulty* is not the dark — it is this terrible handwriting.'

full:0.en: Every shelf was *full* when my shift started, but by 3 a.m. the instant-noodle section looked like a place where a storm had passed. The power cut had sent half the street down to us for comfort food. Tang counted the last cup on the shelf and sighed softly. I started writing a restock note by torchlight.
full:0.cnHint: 停电之夜，货架上的方便面区很快就被买____了。
full:0.hook: One customer came back three minutes later and asked for something we had never stocked.
full:0.line: 'The shelf was *full* an hour ago — people really love noodles in the dark.'

range:0.en: Tang lit four candles along the counter, giving us a warm *range* of soft light that reached from the door to the back fridges. It was not much, but it was enough to see faces. Customers drifted in, looked surprised by the candles, then smiled. For an hour, the store felt less like a shop and more like a small camp.
range:0.cnHint: 蜡烛的光____从门口一直延伸到冷藏柜。
range:0.hook: The last person to walk in that hour had been standing outside for a very long time.
range:0.line: 'This *range* of candlelight is actually quite lovely, don't you think?'

region:0.en: The Manager called at 2:30 a.m. to say the whole *region* around our block had lost power and the repair team would not arrive before dawn. 'Stay open,' she said, sounding very calm. Tang hung up the phone for me and wrote 'OPEN — candles inside' on a piece of card and taped it to the glass door.
region:0.cnHint: 店长来电说我们所在的整个____都停电了，天亮前无法修复。
region:0.hook: Thirty seconds later, someone tried to open the door from the wrong side.
region:0.line: 'The whole *region* is dark, so we may be the only light on the street tonight.'

material:0.en: Tang dug a box of emergency candles from the stock room and held one up. 'This *material* is old,' he said, sniffing the wax, 'but it will burn.' He was right. We lined eight candles along the counter, and the store glowed like something out of an old painting. Customers stopped at the window just to look.
material:0.cnHint: 阿糖检查了应急蜡烛，说这种____虽然旧，但还能用。
material:0.hook: One woman pressed her face against the glass for almost a full minute before coming in.
material:0.line: 'The *material* is a bit old, but old wax burns just as well as new wax.'

pressure:0.en: A long line formed at the counter because the card reader was down and people were counting out coins by candlelight. I felt the *pressure* build in my chest with every slow transaction. Tang leaned over quietly and said, 'Breathe. They waited this long — they can wait a little more.' The line laughed softly, and somehow that helped.
pressure:0.cnHint: 读卡器坏掉后，顾客排起长队，我感到____越来越大。
pressure:0.hook: The very last person in line put a single coin on the counter and made a strange request.
pressure:0.line: 'I can see the *pressure* on your face — just breathe, we are all fine here.'

thus:0.en: The fridge lights were dead, *thus* the cold drinks section was just a dark glass wall. I taped a small note that said 'cold inside — trust us.' Tang found it funny. 'Honest advertising,' he said. Three customers opened the fridge anyway, as if the note might be lying, and each one looked pleasantly surprised to find everything still cool.
thus:0.cnHint: 冰箱灯灭了，____饮料区变成了一面黑玻璃墙。
thus:0.hook: The fourth customer opened the fridge and stood there for a very long time without taking anything.
thus:0.line: 'Power is out, and *thus* we are operating on trust and torchlight tonight.'

tool:0.en: My phone was the only *tool* I had to check prices after the register screen went dark. Tang watched me squinting at the inventory app and handed me a pen and a torn paper bag. 'Old tools work too,' he said simply. I spent the next hour writing prices by hand, and honestly, it felt surprisingly satisfying.
tool:0.cnHint: 收银屏幕黑掉后，我的手机成了查询价格的唯一____。
tool:0.hook: At 4 a.m., a customer walked in who somehow already knew every price in the store.
tool:0.line: 'Your phone is a fine *tool*, but a pen never runs out of battery.'

international:0.en: The power cut left us with only candles and a small radio. Tang tuned it to an *international* station — distant voices in three languages filled the dark store like friendly ghosts. The Manager translated the weather report badly on purpose, just to make us laugh.
international:0.cnHint: 停电时，收音机里传来____电台的声音，店长故意翻译错了天气预报，逗大家开心。
international:0.hook: But one voice on the radio said something that made Tang go very still.
international:0.line: 'This *international* station plays all night — good company when the lights go out.'

manage:0.en: Every shelf went dark at once. I grabbed a torch and tried to restock the rice bags by feel. It took three tries, but I did *manage* to finish before the backup light came on. The Manager looked almost impressed — almost.
manage:0.cnHint: 停电后我摸黑补货，好不容易才____完成了任务，店长差点夸了我。
manage:0.hook: Then I noticed one bag had been placed in completely the wrong aisle.
manage:0.line: 'You *managed* to restock in the dark? I could not even find my own shoes.'

outside:0.en: When the power died, the street went black too. A regular — a quiet man who buys green tea every night — pressed his face to the glass and stared at the *outside* as if seeing it for the first time. Then he turned and smiled at me. 'Nice in here,' he said.
outside:0.cnHint: 停电后，一位常客望着玻璃门____的黑暗，转身对我说里面更好。
outside:0.hook: He had never once told me his name in three weeks.
outside:0.line: 'The *outside* is all dark tonight — I think I will stay a little longer.'

fun:0.en: Tang discovered that our price-tag scanner made a funny beep in the silence. She started tapping it like a drum. I joined in with an empty bottle. For five whole minutes the powerless store was full of strange music and *fun*, until the Manager walked in from the back room.
fun:0.cnHint: 停电时阿糖把扫码枪当鼓敲，我们在黑暗中找到了____，直到店长出现。
fun:0.hook: The Manager stared for a long moment, then quietly picked up a tin can.
fun:0.line: 'A little *fun* in the dark never hurt anyone — keep the beat going.'

reality:0.en: I had imagined a blackout would feel dramatic. The *reality* was quieter: one candle on the counter, a sleepy cat outside the window, and Tang humming to herself while counting change by touch. It was, honestly, rather pleasant.
reality:0.cnHint: 我以为停电会很刺激，但____是一切都安静得出奇，阿糖哼着歌数着零钱。
reality:0.hook: Then someone knocked hard on the locked door and called Tang's name.
reality:0.line: 'You expected drama? The *reality* of a blackout is mostly just sitting around.'

beyond:0.en: The candle threw soft shadows across every corner. I could see the snack aisle clearly, but the area *beyond* the freezers was pure darkness. Tang said something lived back there. She was joking. She was probably joking.
beyond:0.cnHint: 烛光照亮了零食区，但冰柜____的地方漆黑一片，阿糖说那里住着什么东西。
beyond:0.hook: Something in that darkness knocked over a bottle — all on its own.
beyond:0.line: 'Do not walk *beyond* the freezers tonight — I mean it, trust me on this.'

completely:0.en: The backup battery gave out and the store went *completely* silent. No hum of fridges, no buzz of lights — just the sound of rain beginning outside. Tang and I sat on the counter and listened. Neither of us felt like talking, and that was fine.
completely:0.cnHint: 备用电源耗尽后，店里____安静了下来，我和阿糖坐着听雨，什么都没说。
completely:0.hook: Then Tang said, very quietly, 'I used to be afraid of this kind of silence.'
completely:0.line: 'It is *completely* quiet now — even the fridges have given up for the night.'

advise:0.en: A woman came in carrying a dripping umbrella and a worried look. She asked me which candle would burn longest. I had no idea, so I went to find Tang. Tang did not hesitate: she picked one, handed it over, and said the exact words I needed. I decided to *advise* customers less and learn from Tang more.
advise:0.cnHint: 一位顾客问哪根蜡烛燃得最久，阿糖毫不犹豫地给出答案，我决定多向她____学习。
advise:0.hook: The woman glanced back once before stepping into the rain, as if she wanted to say something else.
advise:0.line: 'I *advise* you to take the tall white one — it lasts through the whole night.'

describe:0.en: The power went out at midnight. I lit two candles and tried to *describe* the store to a lost delivery man over the phone — 'small, yellow sign, red door, one step up.' Tang laughed from behind the chip rack. 'You forgot the cat,' she said. There was indeed a cat. I had not noticed it until that moment.
describe:0.cnHint: 停电后我试着向一个迷路的外卖员____这家店的位置，同事唐提醒我忘说了一只猫。
describe:0.hook: The cat was sitting on the manager's chair, and it clearly knew the code to the back room.
describe:0.line: 'Can you *describe* the street sign — is it round or square?'

rest:0.en: After the power cut, Tang and I shared a bench behind the counter. 'Take a *rest*,' she said. 'Nothing will happen for twenty minutes.' She was right. For exactly nineteen minutes the street was quiet and the candles burned without moving. On the twentieth minute, someone knocked on the glass with one finger, very slowly.
rest:0.cnHint: 停电后唐让我____一会儿，说二十分钟内不会有事，结果第二十分钟时有人敲了玻璃。
rest:0.hook: Nobody was standing outside when I looked up.
rest:0.line: 'Sit down and take a *rest* — the backup light will kick in soon.'

employer:0.en: A man in a damp coat came in during the blackout and asked to charge his phone. While it charged, he told me his *employer* had locked the office and gone home without warning. He smiled as he said it, which was strange. He left before his phone hit fifty percent, and he did not take the phone.
employer:0.cnHint: 一个男人停电时进来借电，说他的____把办公室锁了就走，他留下了手机却人先离开了。
employer:0.hook: The phone lit up with a call from a contact saved only as 'Do Not Answer.'
employer:0.line: 'My *employer* closed the whole building without telling anyone — can I stay a moment?'

owner:0.en: The candles threw long shadows. An older woman came in and walked straight to the back shelf, picked up a jar of salted plums, and held it to the light. 'My daughter is the *owner* of the shop next door,' she said to no one in particular. She put the jar back, bought nothing, and left a small folded note on the counter.
owner:0.cnHint: 一位老太太进来，自言自语地说她女儿是隔壁店的____，然后在柜台上留下了一张折好的纸条。
owner:0.hook: The note had tomorrow's date written on it, and nothing else.
owner:0.line: 'Tell the *owner* of this store the back window has a crack — I noticed it last week.'

gender:0.en: I was filling out a new customer log the Manager left for me. One column said *gender*. Tang looked over my shoulder and snorted. 'He never fills that in himself,' she said. 'Just leave it blank.' I left it blank for every row. The Manager arrived at dawn, checked the log, and said nothing — but he crossed out the whole column with one clean line.
gender:0.cnHint: 我在填写顾客登记表时遇到了____一栏，唐说店长自己从不填，店长来后直接把那一列划掉了。
gender:0.hook: The column he crossed out was not the gender column.
gender:0.line: 'The old form had a *gender* box — the new one doesn't, and I think that's better.'

website:0.en: During the blackout a teenager sat on the front step with a pocket light, muttering. I asked if he was okay. 'My order says delivered but it's not here,' he said. 'The *website* shows a photo of someone else's door.' Tang handed him a warm can from under the counter. He stayed on the step for an hour, refreshing something.
website:0.cnHint: 停电时一个少年在门口抱怨外卖____显示已送达，但送到了别人家门口，唐给了他一罐热饮。
website:0.hook: The photo on the website showed our store's red door, not his.
website:0.line: 'The *website* keeps crashing — I can't even check where my order went.'

emotional:0.en: Tang warned me about a regular named Lin from the store across the street. 'He gets *emotional* about shelf arrangements,' she said, as if that explained everything. At 2 a.m., by candlelight, Lin walked in, stared at our snack wall for a long time, then quietly rearranged six items into a pattern I did not understand, nodded, and left.
emotional:0.cnHint: 唐提醒我说林对货架摆放很____，凌晨两点他果然进来，在烛光下默默调整了六样商品。
emotional:0.hook: The pattern Lin made matched the layout of his own store exactly.
emotional:0.line: 'Don't get *emotional* about it — he does this every time the power goes out.'

training:0.en: The Manager had left a printed sheet on the counter: 'Night-shift *training* notes — read before the power comes back.' I read it by candle. Point one said: 'Do not wake the cat.' Point two said: 'Tang knows where the torch is. She will not tell you. Ask nicely.' There were eleven more points. Point thirteen was left blank.
training:0.cnHint: 店长留下了一份夜班____资料，第一条是不要吵醒猫，第二条说唐知道手电筒在哪但不会主动告诉我。
training:0.hook: Point thirteen had been blank on every copy — Tang had seen three.
training:0.line: 'This is your *training* sheet — the Manager updates it every few months, usually after something goes wrong.'

consume:0.en: The power cut killed every light in the store. I grabbed a torch and checked the fridges. The cooling units were off, and the ice cream was already soft. 'We'll *consume* all of this before it melts,' I told myself, opening the first tub with quiet determination.
consume:0.cnHint: 停电后，店员决定在冰淇淋融化前把它们全部____掉。
consume:0.hook: But the last tub had someone's name written on the lid.
consume:0.line: 'We have to *consume* the ice cream now, or it's all wasted.'

desire:0.en: Tang lit three candles and set them on the counter. The warm glow made the small store feel like a cosy cave. A regular customer stood at the door, rain dripping from his coat. His eyes moved to the hot food shelf. I could see the *desire* in his face before he even spoke.
desire:0.cnHint: 停电的夜晚，一位常客望着热食货架，眼神里满是____。
desire:0.hook: He asked for something we stopped selling six months ago.
desire:0.line: 'I *desire* nothing more than a hot meal on a night like this.'

meal:0.en: The power had been gone for an hour. Tang found a small gas cooker in the back room and heated up a pot of soup. The smell drifted into the dark store. A tired woman came in, sat on a low stool, and finished every drop. It was her only *meal* of the day.
meal:0.cnHint: 停电夜里，一位疲惫的女士在店里吃了当天唯一的一____。
meal:0.hook: She left a folded note under the empty bowl.
meal:0.line: 'This simple *meal* is honestly the best thing I have had all week.'

vegetable:0.en: With the fridges off, I moved stock to a cool corner near the back door. Tang helped me sort through the shelves by torchlight. We found a forgotten bag of *vegetable* behind a row of noodles — spinach, still fresh and bright green. Someone had paid for it and never picked it up.
vegetable:0.cnHint: 停电时，店员在货架后面发现了一袋被遗忘的____。
vegetable:0.hook: The receipt inside the bag was dated three weeks ago.
vegetable:0.line: 'This *vegetable* is still good — someone is going to be very happy tonight.'

adopt:0.en: The Manager arrived just after midnight with a battery lamp. He looked around the dark store, nodded once, and walked to the whiteboard. 'We *adopt* a simple rule tonight,' he said in a calm voice. 'Anything that will spoil by morning, we give away free.' Tang and I exchanged a surprised look.
adopt:0.cnHint: 停电后，店长宣布____一条新规定，让两人都感到意外。
adopt:0.hook: The first person to hear the news was already waiting outside.
adopt:0.line: 'From tonight we *adopt* a new rule — nothing goes to waste here.'

miss:0.en: A young woman ran in just before one in the morning, shaking water from her umbrella. She looked at the dark fridges and let out a long breath. 'Did I *miss* the last hot drink?' she asked quietly. Tang was already filling a paper cup from the gas cooker. She smiled with great relief.
miss:0.cnHint: 一位年轻女士冲进店里，担心自己____了最后一杯热饮。
miss:0.hook: She came back ten minutes later with an extra umbrella for Tang.
miss:0.line: 'Please tell me I did not *miss* the last hot drink you have.'

yourself:0.en: Around two in the morning the store felt oddly peaceful. Tang was dozing behind the counter. The Manager had gone to check the fuse box. A regular customer, an older man, poured himself some hot water and told me, 'You should look after *yourself* on nights like this — eat something, sit down.'
yourself:0.cnHint: 深夜，一位常客好心提醒店员要照顾好____。
yourself:0.hook: He then pulled a small wrapped box from his coat pocket.
yourself:0.line: 'You cannot help others if you do not take care of *yourself* first.'

century:0.en: The old man settled onto a stool near the candles. He said the street corner had held a small shop for nearly a *century* — different owners, different names, but always open through storms. He tapped the wooden counter gently. 'This store has seen worse nights than this,' he said with a slow smile.
century:0.cnHint: 老人说这个街角的小店已经开了将近一个____，见过更糟糕的夜晚。
century:0.hook: Then he mentioned a name none of us had ever heard before.
century:0.line: 'This corner has had a shop for almost a *century* — it will survive tonight.'

responsibility:0.en: The lights went out at midnight. Every candle in the store was lit within seconds. The Manager called from the back room: 'This is your *responsibility* now — keep the customers calm and the shelves safe.' I nodded, suddenly feeling the weight of the whole quiet street on my shoulders.
responsibility:0.cnHint: 停电了，店长告诉我，安抚顾客、保护货架是我的____。
responsibility:0.hook: Then someone knocked hard on the locked back door.
responsibility:0.line: 'Keeping this store running tonight is your *responsibility*, not mine.'

soon:0.en: The power cut hit without warning. I found one torch under the counter and switched it on. 'Don't worry,' I told the old man buying instant noodles, '*soon* the lights will be back.' He smiled, paid in coins by torchlight, and shuffled toward the door without another word.
soon:0.cnHint: 我告诉买泡面的老爷爷，灯____就会亮了。
soon:0.hook: But the old man paused and looked back at me strangely.
soon:0.line: '*Soon* the whole block will be dark — you should know that.'

center:0.en: When the power died, everyone in the store drifted toward the cold drinks fridge — its tiny backup light made it the *center* of the room. A small girl pressed her face against the glass and laughed at her own reflection. For a moment the darkness felt almost cheerful.
center:0.cnHint: 停电后，冷饮柜的备用灯让它成了整个店的____。
center:0.hook: Then the backup light flickered and went out too.
center:0.line: 'The fridge is the *center* of everyone's attention right now, clerk.'

arrive:0.en: I was counting candles when Tang rushed in from the staff room. 'Did the emergency kit *arrive* last week?' she asked, already pulling open every low cabinet. I had no idea — I had only started three nights ago. We found nothing but a broken torch and two expired batteries.
arrive:0.cnHint: 阿糖问我，上周订的应急包有没有____。
arrive:0.hook: Tang went very still and whispered something under her breath.
arrive:0.line: 'Tell me the backup batteries *arrive* before my shift ends, please.'

boost:0.en: The darkness made customers nervous, so I lined up six scented candles along the counter and put soft music on my phone. The warm glow gave everyone a small *boost*. Even Lin, who had come in only to complain about the price of coffee, stopped frowning and bought a second cup.
boost:0.cnHint: 我点上蜡烛、放上轻音乐，给大家的心情带来了一点____。
boost:0.hook: Lin left a coin on the counter and said nothing at all.
boost:0.line: 'A few candles really give the whole mood a *boost*, you know.'

conflict:0.en: Lin arrived just as Tang was handing out the last free bottle of water. They reached for the same torch at the same moment. Their eyes met. Old feelings seemed to *conflict* beneath the surface — two people with a long, quiet history the darkness had suddenly made visible. I stepped between them carefully.
conflict:0.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林和阿糖同时抓住手电筒，两人之间积压的情绪似乎开始____。
conflict:0.hook: Neither of them looked at me, only at each other.
conflict:0.line: 'Our schedules *conflict* again — someone planned this on purpose.'

demand:0.en: A tired woman in a raincoat pushed through the door and *demanded* a working phone charger, a warm meal, and a receipt for both. The power was still out. I offered her a candle, a steamed bun from the hot case, and my best handwritten receipt. She stared at it, then actually laughed.
demand:0.cnHint: 一位雨衣女士进门就____充电器和热食。
demand:0.hook: She folded the handwritten receipt and tucked it into her pocket.
demand:0.line: 'I *demand* at least one working outlet in a twenty-four-hour store.'

emotion:0.en: By two in the morning the store held five strangers sharing one box of crackers by candlelight. Nobody spoke much. The soft flames brought out every small *emotion* — relief, tiredness, a shy kind of warmth. Tang caught my eye across the counter and gave me a slow, approving nod.
emotion:0.cnHint: 烛光下，五个陌生人共享饼干，每个人脸上都流露出细腻的____。
emotion:0.hook: Then the lights snapped back on, and the moment was gone.
emotion:0.line: 'There is so much *emotion* in this little store tonight, clerk.'

management:0.en: The lights cut out at midnight. I found a torch under the counter and checked the fuse box, just as the Manager had shown me. A note taped to the box read: 'Follow the *management* plan on the back wall.' I turned the torch toward the wall and read step one.
management:0.cnHint: 停电后，我按照店里的____方案找到了应急指南。
management:0.hook: Step three on the plan had been crossed out by hand.
management:0.line: 'The *management* plan is clear — check the fuse first, then call me.'

perfect:0.en: With the power gone, the store felt oddly peaceful. The candles I lit on the counter made every tin and packet glow softly. Tang laughed quietly and said it was *perfect* for a slow night — better than the harsh white lights above. I had to agree.
perfect:0.cnHint: 停电后烛光让小店看起来____极了，同事也忍不住夸了一句。
perfect:0.hook: Then a shadow appeared on the other side of the glass door.
perfect:0.line: 'Honestly, this soft light is *perfect* — we should do this every week.'

along:0.en: I carried a small candle and walked *along* the narrow aisle between the shelves, checking that nothing had fallen in the sudden dark. Tins of soup, bags of chips, rows of instant noodles — all still standing. Halfway down, I heard a soft knock from the back room.
along:0.cnHint: 我拿着蜡烛____货架走了一圈，检查有没有东西倒下。
along:0.hook: The back room door was supposed to be locked all night.
along:0.line: 'Come *along*, I will show you where the spare torches are kept.'

harm:0.en: The power cut stretched past one in the morning. A regular customer, an older man who bought warm milk every night, stood at the door looking worried. 'Will the cold *harm* the milk in your fridge?' he asked. I assured him the sealed units stayed cold for hours yet.
harm:0.cnHint: 一位常客担心停电会____冰箱里的牛奶，专门来问我。
harm:0.hook: He then mentioned he had not come for the milk tonight.
harm:0.line: 'I just want to be sure the cold will not *harm* anything in there.'

increasingly:0.en: As the outage went on, the street outside grew *increasingly* quiet. Cars stopped passing. The only sound was the hum of the battery-powered clock above the door. Tang sat behind the counter, staring at his phone screen — the last little square of light in the whole block.
increasingly:0.cnHint: 随着停电时间延长，街道变得____安静，同事的手机成了唯一的光源。
increasingly:0.hook: His phone screen suddenly showed an incoming call from an unknown number.
increasingly:0.line: 'It is getting *increasingly* strange out there — nobody has walked by for twenty minutes.'

opinion:0.en: Lin stepped in just after two, shaking rain off her jacket. She looked around at the candles and the dark shelves and gave a short laugh. 'In my *opinion*,' she said, 'a store without power is still a store.' She grabbed a basket and started shopping by torchlight as if nothing were odd.
opinion:0.cnHint: 竞争对手在停电时进来买东西，还发表了自己对小店的____。
opinion:0.hook: She put something on the counter that was not for sale.
opinion:0.line: 'In my *opinion*, candles actually make this place feel more welcoming.'

previous:0.en: I checked the logbook for the night shift. The *previous* clerk had written a single line at the bottom of last week's entry: 'If power fails, spare keys are in the blue tin, top shelf.' I climbed up, found the tin, and inside it was a hand-drawn map of the store.
previous:0.cnHint: 我在工作日志里找到了____夜班店员留下的停电应急提示。
previous:0.hook: The map showed a room I had never noticed before.
previous:0.line: 'The *previous* clerk left good notes — we should all do the same.'

aim:0.en: My *aim* for the night had been simple: stay awake, keep the shelves tidy, greet anyone who came in. The power cut turned all of that into a small adventure. By three in the morning I had fixed the fuse, sold six candles, and learned the name of every regular on the street.
aim:0.cnHint: 我这个夜班的____原本很简单，没想到停电让一切变成了小冒险。
aim:0.hook: The last customer of the night left behind a folded note for me.
aim:0.line: 'My *aim* is to have this place ready before the Manager arrives at six.'

model:0.en: The power cut left the store lit only by a single candle. The Manager pulled a small plastic *model* of the store from under the counter — every shelf, every fridge, perfectly tiny — and set it between the candles like a shrine. 'I built it myself,' he said quietly.
model:0.cnHint: 停电后，店长从柜台下拿出一个小小的____，摆在烛光中。
model:0.hook: Why does the model have a tiny figure behind the counter?
model:0.line: 'This *model* shows exactly how the store should look at midnight.'

spot:0.en: Without the overhead lights, the store felt like a cave. I was restacking crisps by torchlight when I *spotted* a small boy sitting on the floor behind the magazine rack, reading by the glow of his phone. He had been there for at least an hour.
spot:0.cnHint: 停电后，我用手电筒整理货架时，____ 到一个小男孩藏在杂志架后面。
spot:0.hook: The boy looked up and put one finger to his lips.
spot:0.line: 'I can *spot* a hiding customer anywhere in this store.'

achievement:0.en: Tang arrived for the late shift carrying a paper certificate. 'Regional maths competition,' she said, holding it under my torch beam. 'Third place.' She slid it carefully behind the counter. For Tang, finishing that exam after three all-night shifts here was a real *achievement*.
achievement:0.cnHint: 停电的夜里，唐拿出一张证书，这个____对她来说来之不易。
achievement:0.hook: Her hands were shaking slightly as she put it away.
achievement:0.line: 'Winning third place is a real *achievement* after working every night this week.'

enter:0.en: The door sensor beeped even though the power was out. We both froze. Then Lin pushed the door open slowly and stepped inside, dripping wet from the rain. 'The sensor runs on battery,' the Manager explained. Everyone watched Lin *enter* and shake water from her umbrella onto the clean floor.
enter:0.cnHint: 停电的夜里，门铃突然响起，林____了店里，把大家都吓了一跳。
enter:0.hook: Lin was supposed to be on the other side of town tonight.
enter:0.line: 'Please *enter* quietly — the Manager is asleep in the back room.'

eye:0.en: The candles made soft shadows jump across the shelves. I noticed the Manager kept one *eye* on the old security monitor, which ran on a backup battery and showed a grey, fuzzy picture of the street outside. He never explained what he was watching for.
eye:0.cnHint: 烛光中，店长一直用____ 盯着备用电源驱动的监控屏幕。
eye:0.hook: Something moved on the screen, and the Manager sat up straight.
eye:0.line: 'Keep an *eye* on the door — someone has been circling the block.'

shift:0.en: At two in the morning the power came back with a loud click. The lights felt brutally bright after so long in candlelight. Tang blinked and said the sudden *shift* from warm dark to cold white felt like being born again. Then she went straight back to mopping the floor.
shift:0.cnHint: 电力恢复时，光线突然大变，这种____让唐感慨了一句。
shift:0.hook: She stopped mopping and stared at the freezer door.
shift:0.line: 'That *shift* from darkness to light is something I will remember.'

agree:0.en: Lin wanted to leave early; the rain had stopped and she had a long walk home. The Manager looked at me. I looked at Tang. We all knew Lin had covered an extra hour last Sunday without complaint. The Manager sighed. 'Fine,' he said. We all seemed to *agree* without saying another word.
agree:0.cnHint: 林想提前离开，我们几个人交换了一个眼神，默默____了她的请求。
agree:0.hook: Lin paused at the door and glanced back at the security monitor.
agree:0.line: 'I *agree* that she has earned the right to leave early tonight.'

aware:0.en: Just before my shift ended I found a wallet on the floor near the magazine rack — the same spot where I had seen the small boy earlier. I slipped it onto the counter. I was suddenly *aware* that every quiet customer in this store carries a story I know nothing about.
aware:0.cnHint: 快下班时我在地上发现了一个钱包，意识到，我对每位顾客其实一无所知，并不____他们的故事。
aware:0.hook: Inside the wallet was a folded maths competition ticket.
aware:0.line: 'I was not *aware* that he had been sitting there for so long.'

land:0.en: The power cut turned the store into a quiet cave. The Manager lit a candle and set it on the counter. An old man shuffled in, holding a worn map. 'Every piece of *land* on this map,' he said softly, 'I have walked.' He bought nothing. He only smiled.
land:0.cnHint: 停电后，一位老人拿着地图走进来，说他走遍了地图上每一片____。
land:0.hook: But the map showed a town that no longer exists.
land:0.line: 'Every piece of *land* on this map, I have walked.'

promote:0.en: Tang found a dusty box behind the shelves during the blackout. Inside were old flyers. 'The Manager used to *promote* the store with handwritten notes,' Tang whispered, holding one up to the candle. The note was addressed to someone named after a flower. Nobody knew who she was.
promote:0.cnHint: 停电时，唐在货架后发现了旧传单，原来店长曾用手写便条来____这家店。
promote:0.hook: The handwriting on the last flyer was shaking badly.
promote:0.line: 'The Manager used to *promote* the store with handwritten notes,' Tang whispered.

purchase:0.en: A young woman came in just after the lights died. She moved through the dark aisles by memory, picking up the same three things every time. I rang up her *purchase* by torchlight. She paused at the door and said, 'Same as always.' Then she was gone before I could ask her name.
purchase:0.cnHint: 停电后，一位年轻女士凭记忆挑好商品，我在手电筒下结算了她的____。
purchase:0.hook: Her receipt showed she had shopped here every night for two years.
purchase:0.line: 'Please ring up my *purchase* quickly, I have somewhere to be.'

rely:0.en: The power stayed off for an hour. I started to panic, but Tang stayed calm. 'We *rely* on the candles the Manager keeps in the back,' she said, already lighting a row of them. The store glowed warm and gold. Three more customers came in just to stand in the light.
rely:0.cnHint: 停电时我很慌，但唐很镇定，说我们可以____店长备在后面的蜡烛。
rely:0.hook: One of the three customers had not spoken to anyone in a week.
rely:0.line: 'We *rely* on the candles the Manager keeps in the back,' Tang said.

connect:0.en: The blackout cut the Wi-Fi, so the card reader went dark. A delivery man stood at the counter looking lost. 'How do I *connect* to anyone now?' he said, half joking, waving his dead phone. I offered him a cup of hot tea instead. He sat down and did not leave for thirty minutes.
connect:0.cnHint: 停电导致读卡机失灵，一名快递员问没有网络怎么____外界，我请他喝了杯热茶。
connect:0.hook: He mentioned he was waiting for a call that might change everything.
connect:0.line: 'How do I *connect* to anyone now?' he said, waving his dead phone.

indicate:0.en: Lin from the rival store across the street appeared in our doorway during the outage. She held up two fingers. I had no idea what that meant. The Manager looked up from his candle and nodded once. 'That number *indicates* how many boxes of batteries she needs,' he said quietly. They had a system. I was stunned.
indicate:0.cnHint: 停电时，对面店的林走进来比了个手势，店长说那个数字____她需要的电池数量。
indicate:0.hook: So Lin and the Manager had been sharing supplies for years.
indicate:0.line: 'That number *indicates* how many boxes she needs,' the Manager said.

period:0.en: During the dark *period* after the power failed, the store felt different. Softer. Two neighbours who never spoke sat side by side on the step outside, sharing a bag of crackers from our shelf. I watched from the window. The Manager appeared beside me. 'This happens every blackout,' he said, almost proud.
period:0.cnHint: 在停电后的这段____里，两位平时不说话的邻居坐在一起分享饼干。
period:0.hook: One of them had once filed a complaint about the other.
period:0.line: 'During a *period* like this, people remember each other,' the Manager said.

picture:0.en: I found an old photo album under the counter while searching for a torch. Every page held a *picture* of a different regular, each one smiling beside a handwritten date. Some faces I already recognised. Tang leaned over my shoulder. 'The Manager takes one every New Year,' she said. 'You will be next.'
picture:0.cnHint: 我在柜台下发现了一本相册，每页都有一张老顾客的____，唐说我下一个就轮到我了。
picture:0.hook: One picture had a date from thirty years ago, and the face was the Manager's.
picture:0.line: 'Every *picture* in that album has a story,' Tang said softly.

return:0.en: The power cut at midnight. Every shelf went dark. I found a torch under the counter and lit the way for customers to the exit. Ten minutes later, when the lights came back on, I expected quiet — but the Manager appeared at the door, arms full of candles, ready for the *return* of the next blackout.
return:0.cnHint: 停电后灯光恢复，店长却带着蜡烛____，准备应对下一次停电。
return:0.hook: Why did the Manager look relieved, not surprised?
return:0.line: 'The *return* of power means nothing if we are not ready.'

remove:0.en: Shelves of canned soup glowed faintly in the emergency light. Tang knocked one over, and it rolled behind the drinks fridge. We both tried to *remove* the heavy fridge from the wall, scraping it inch by inch across the floor, until the can finally rolled free — along with a folded note nobody had put there.
remove:0.cnHint: 停电时，我们努力____冰箱，找到了一个神秘的纸条。
remove:0.hook: The note had tonight's date written on it.
remove:0.line: 'Help me *remove* this fridge — there is something behind it.'

colleague:0.en: The emergency light threw long shadows across the snack aisle. I had worked three nights alone, so I was glad when Tang arrived early. 'You are my only *colleague* on this shift,' I said, handing over a warm cup of instant noodles. Tang smiled, then glanced at the back room with an odd, careful look.
colleague:0.cnHint: 停电的夜晚，我把热泡面递给我的____，却发现他一直盯着后室。
colleague:0.hook: Tang had never once looked at that back room before.
colleague:0.line: 'A good *colleague* always arrives before the storm.'

normal:0.en: At two in the morning the lights died and the fridge hum stopped. Customers pulled out their phones for light and laughed nervously. After fifteen minutes everything came back on, and the Manager said it was all *normal* — a simple overload. But I noticed he had already moved the safe to a different shelf.
normal:0.cnHint: 店长说停电完全____，但我发现他悄悄移动了保险箱。
normal:0.hook: You do not move a safe for a normal overload.
normal:0.line: 'This is all perfectly *normal*, so please do not worry.'

succeed:0.en: Lin arrived just as the backup generator sputtered and died. We needed to restart it, but the button was stiff and the handbook was missing. Lin tried twice and failed. On the third try I leaned all my weight on the switch and felt it click — I had managed to *succeed*, and cold white light filled the store again.
succeed:0.cnHint: 备用发电机坏了，我终于____重启了它，灯光重新亮起。
succeed:0.hook: Lin stared at the restarted generator as if it frightened her.
succeed:0.line: 'I knew you would *succeed* — you always do on the third try.'

image:0.en: The power returned slowly, screen by screen. The security monitor was last to wake up. When it did, it showed a frozen *image* from thirty minutes earlier — a figure standing in the snack aisle who was not me, not Tang, and not any customer I had served that night.
image:0.cnHint: 监控恢复后，屏幕上出现了一个陌生人的____，那时店里应该只有我们。
image:0.hook: The timestamp on the image read 01:47 — I was alone then.
image:0.line: 'Look at this *image* — who is standing in aisle three?'

ourselves:0.en: The torch batteries died ten minutes into the blackout. Tang and I stood in total darkness among the crisp packets and phone chargers. 'We only have *ourselves* to rely on now,' Tang said quietly. We linked arms and felt along the shelves until we reached the counter and found the spare batteries taped underneath.
ourselves:0.cnHint: 停电后手电筒没电了，我们只能靠____摸黑找到备用电池。
ourselves:0.hook: The batteries we found were still warm, as if someone had just held them.
ourselves:0.line: 'We only have *ourselves* now, so let us be careful.'

catch:0.en: A gust of wind pushed the door open just as the lights failed. Papers flew off the counter in every direction. I lunged across the floor, arms wide, trying to *catch* the inventory sheet before it disappeared under the fridge. I missed — but Tang snatched it from the air with one easy hand.
catch:0.cnHint: 停电时风把文件吹跑，我没能____住它，唐却轻松接住了。
catch:0.hook: Tang had been standing too far away to reach it that fast.
catch:0.line: 'Next time, I will *catch* it before it even leaves the desk.'

relate:0.en: The power cut turned the store dark in an instant. The Manager lit a candle and sat on the counter. 'Let me *relate* something funny,' he said, and began telling us about the night a cat knocked every snack off shelf three. Lin and I leaned in close.
relate:0.cnHint: 停电后店长点起蜡烛，开始____一个关于猫的趣事。
relate:0.hook: But his smile faded before the story ended.
relate:0.line: 'Let me *relate* what really happened that night.'

attitude:0.en: Tang folded his arms and stared at the flickering candle with a calm, easy *attitude*, as if power cuts happened every hour. I was sweating and checking the register. He just shrugged. 'Darkness is fine,' he said softly. His cool manner made me feel a little better, honestly.
attitude:0.cnHint: 停电时，同事展现出一种从容的____，让叙述者稍感安心。
attitude:0.hook: Then Tang whispered something no one else was meant to hear.
attitude:0.line: 'Your *attitude* toward the dark says a lot about you.'

fill:0.en: The candle threw warm gold light across the shelves. I grabbed a torch and started checking the drink fridges. The Manager handed me a clipboard. 'Write down every item we need to *fill* back up before morning,' he said. The list grew longer with each dark aisle I walked down.
fill:0.cnHint: 停电后，店长让叙述者记下所有需要____的商品。
fill:0.hook: One shelf had been emptied by someone we never saw come in.
fill:0.line: 'We need to *fill* the cold shelf before sunrise, no excuses.'

ignore:0.en: A regular customer pushed open the door, saw the candles, and walked straight to the snack wall as usual. She seemed to *ignore* the darkness completely, picking up a small bag of crackers by feel alone. I called out, 'Can I help?' She did not even turn around.
ignore:0.cnHint: 停电时，一位常客似乎完全____了黑暗，径直去拿零食。
ignore:0.hook: She paid in exact coins, then vanished before I could see her face.
ignore:0.line: 'I choose to *ignore* the dark — it helps nothing to fear it.'

necessary:0.en: Lin arrived for her shift early, carrying a small bag. She unpacked four candles, a torch, and a first-aid kit onto the counter. 'I thought these might be *necessary*,' she said simply, without making a big deal of it. The Manager looked surprised. I was grateful. Lin always thought one step ahead.
necessary:0.cnHint: 停电时，林带来了一些她认为____的物品，让大家刮目相看。
necessary:0.hook: But the last item in her bag was harder to explain.
necessary:0.line: 'I knew a torch would be *necessary*, so I brought two.'

definitely:0.en: The emergency light above the door blinked twice, then stayed on. 'That is *definitely* not supposed to do that,' Tang said, pointing up at it. We all stared. The Manager climbed onto a step-stool and gave the cover a gentle tap. The blinking stopped. Nobody spoke for a moment.
definitely:0.cnHint: 应急灯突然闪烁，同事说这____不正常。
definitely:0.hook: When the Manager stepped down, his expression was oddly serious.
definitely:0.line: 'That light will *definitely* cause problems again before morning.'

forget:0.en: In all the rush of finding candles and checking fridges, I managed to *forget* the most important thing — the back-door lock. At midnight, the Manager walked past and froze. 'Did anyone check that?' he asked quietly. The door was wide open. Cold air poured into the store.
forget:0.cnHint: 忙乱中，叙述者____了检查后门，导致门大开着。
forget:0.hook: Someone — or something — had already slipped inside.
forget:0.line: 'Please don't *forget* the back door again — ever.'

particularly:0.en: Most shelves were easy to manage by torchlight, but the high back shelf was *particularly* tricky. Everything up there was packed tight and hard to read in the dark. Lin stood on her toes, squinting. 'I cannot see a thing,' she muttered. I held the torch higher. She laughed softly.
particularly:0.cnHint: 停电时大多数货架还好，但后方高架____难以操作。
particularly:0.hook: Then Lin reached up and touched something that should not have been there.
particularly:0.line: 'This top shelf is *particularly* dangerous in the dark, be careful.'

meanwhile:0.en: The lights went out at half past eleven. I found a torch under the counter and lit three candles on the shelf. Customers moved carefully between the shadows. *Meanwhile*, Tang was in the back room counting the coins from the broken machine, humming a small tune as if nothing had happened.
meanwhile:0.cnHint: 停电后，店里一片昏暗，____，同事唐在后室数零钱，十分淡定。
meanwhile:0.hook: Then Tang came out holding something that was not coins.
meanwhile:0.line: '*Meanwhile*, I found something strange back there — come and look.'

damage:0.en: One of the tall drink fridges made a loud crack when the power cut hit. I pressed my hand against the door; it felt warm. The Manager arrived ten minutes later, torch in hand, and walked straight to it. 'Look at this,' he said quietly, running a finger along a dark crack. 'Real *damage*.'
damage:0.cnHint: 停电时冰柜发出巨响，店长检查后发现冰柜出现了____。
damage:0.hook: He then turned and looked directly at me.
damage:0.line: 'This *damage* will cost more than one night's sales.'

police:0.en: A sharp knock came at the glass door just after midnight. Two officers in dark jackets stood outside, torches pointing at the floor. I unlocked the door with hands that were not quite steady. 'We are checking every open shop on the street,' the first *police* officer said, stepping inside.
police:0.cnHint: 午夜刚过，____来到便利店，说要检查这条街上所有营业中的商店。
police:0.hook: The second officer was staring at something on the shelf behind me.
police:0.line: 'The *police* are here — please stay calm and show us the back room.'

race:0.en: The backup generator in the building next door roared to life, but our store was still dark. Tang appeared from the back with a second torch. 'We need to move the cold food to the cooler boxes before it all goes bad,' he said. It felt like a quiet *race* against time, the two of us carrying trays through the dark.
race:0.cnHint: 停电后，我和唐在黑暗中抢时间转移冷藏食品，感觉像在进行一场____。
race:0.hook: Tang suddenly stopped and whispered, 'Did you hear that?'
race:0.line: 'This is a *race* — grab the dairy shelf first, then the meat.'

medical:0.en: A woman came in just before one in the morning, wet from the rain outside. She asked if we kept any basic supplies. I brought out the small first-aid box from under the counter. 'I have some *medical* things here — bandages, some tablets for pain,' I said, setting the box on the counter in the candlelight.
medical:0.cnHint: 一位雨夜来客询问是否有____用品，我从柜台下取出了急救箱。
medical:0.hook: She looked at the box and said she needed far more than that.
medical:0.line: 'Do you have any *medical* supplies — anything at all for a burn?'

wear:0.en: Lin walked in at one-fifteen, calm as ever, a small bag on one shoulder. Even in a blackout she managed to *wear* a look of mild amusement, as though the dark and the candles were there purely for her entertainment. She set two hot drinks on the counter and slid one across to me without a word.
wear:0.cnHint: 林走进昏暗的店里，脸上____着一副轻松愉快的表情，还带来了两杯热饮。
wear:0.hook: The second cup had a folded note tucked under it.
wear:0.line: 'You always *wear* that worried face — here, drink this first.'

climate:0.en: 'Blackouts are going to get more common,' the Manager said, sitting on an upturned crate near the window. 'The whole *climate* of this neighbourhood is changing — new buildings, old wires, too much demand.' He sounded less like a shop manager and more like someone who had been worrying about this for years.
climate:0.cnHint: 店长坐在木箱上感叹，整个街区的____正在改变，停电只会越来越常见。
climate:0.hook: Then he mentioned a name I had never heard before.
climate:0.line: 'The *climate* here has changed — we need a generator before next month.'

head:0.en: Around two in the morning I sat down on the step behind the counter, tired all the way through. Tang appeared and tapped the top of my *head* once with two fingers, lightly, the way you might tap a table to get someone's attention. 'Still awake?' he asked. 'Good. We have a customer.'
head:0.cnHint: 凌晨两点，唐轻敲我的____，提醒我打起精神——店里来客人了。
head:0.hook: The customer was wearing a coat that was completely dry.
head:0.line: 'Lift your *head* — there is someone at the door and they look lost.'

mistake:0.en: The power cut hit at midnight. I reached for the wrong shelf and handed a customer salt crackers instead of sweet ones. 'Sorry, my *mistake*,' I said, cheeks warm. The customer laughed and dropped both packs on the counter, studying them side by side under my phone torch.
mistake:0.cnHint: 停电时，我拿错了货，把咸饼干当成甜饼干递给顾客，连忙道歉。
mistake:0.hook: He chose the salt ones — and came back an hour later for more.
mistake:0.line: 'Don't worry, your *mistake* actually helped me find my new favourite snack.'

staff:0.en: When the lights died, the Manager gathered all three of us by the cold drinks fridge, its little green light still glowing. 'Full *staff* meeting, right now,' he said, sounding almost proud. He handed out phone torches and a handwritten checklist. Tang was already taping a paper sign to the door.
staff:0.cnHint: 停电后，店长把全体____召集在一起，分发手电筒，布置任务。
staff:0.hook: The sign Tang wrote said something none of us expected.
staff:0.line: 'Good — full *staff* present. Now let's keep this store running.'

enhance:0.en: Tang lit three small candles along the front counter and stepped back to look. 'Candles *enhance* the whole atmosphere,' she said seriously. The Manager stared at her. I stared at her. A customer who had just walked in stopped, looked around, and quietly took a photo with his phone.
enhance:0.cnHint: 停电后，阿糖点上蜡烛，说这样能____整体气氛，大家都愣住了。
enhance:0.hook: The photo would cause a very unexpected problem by morning.
enhance:0.line: 'Candles really *enhance* the mood in here tonight, don't you think?'

famous:0.en: By one in the morning, word spread somehow. A steady line formed outside. 'We're *famous*,' Tang whispered, pressing her nose to the glass. The Manager checked his phone with wide eyes. Someone had posted a photo of our candlelit store and called it the most romantic spot on the street.
famous:0.cnHint: 停电的烛光照片在网上传开，便利店一夜之间变得____了。
famous:0.hook: Lin from the rival store across the road was not smiling.
famous:0.line: 'We're *famous* now — better restock the hot drinks fast.'

project:0.en: Lin appeared at the door just after two, carrying a thick folder. 'Community lighting *project*,' she announced, slapping papers on the counter. 'I need every shop on this block to sign.' The Manager read the first page slowly. I watched his eyebrows rise, then fall, then rise again.
project:0.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林带来一份社区照明____的文件，要求街上每家店都签字。
project:0.hook: Page three had a cost that made the Manager go very quiet.
project:0.line: 'This *project* could fix the whole street's power problem for good.'

record:0.en: 'Highest single-night sale in two years,' the Manager murmured, staring at the screen of the little register, which had somehow kept working on battery. 'That's a new *record*.' Tang punched the air. I looked at the almost-empty snack wall and felt a complicated kind of pride.
record:0.cnHint: 停电夜的销售额创下了新____，店长盯着收银机屏幕喃喃自语。
record:0.hook: The one item we sold most of was the thing I almost threw away.
record:0.line: 'A new *record* — on a night with no lights. Not bad at all.'

regular:0.en: Old Mr Chen arrived at three, same as always, for his warm soy milk. He didn't even mention the darkness. '*Regular* customers keep regular hours,' he said simply, settling onto his usual stool with a small candle between us. We sat quietly. Outside, the street was perfectly still.
regular:0.cnHint: 停电深夜，____顾客陈老先生照常出现，买他的热豆浆，毫不在意停电。
regular:0.hook: Then he said he had something important to tell me before dawn.
regular:0.line: 'A *regular* customer shows up no matter what — that's just how it is.'

security:0.en: At four in the morning, a man in a dark jacket tried the back door. Tang grabbed my arm. Then we saw the logo on his sleeve — he was the building's *security* guard, just checking locks during the outage. He waved a torch at us, a little embarrassed, and moved on.
security:0.cnHint: 凌晨四点，有人试图开后门，吓了我们一跳，原来是大楼的____人员在例行检查。
security:0.hook: But Tang said she had seen that jacket somewhere else before.
security:0.line: '*Security* check — sorry for the scare. All good back here.'

whatever:0.en: The lights went out at eleven. The Manager grabbed a torch and said we should keep serving *whatever* customers still came in. I lit the candles on the counter. The small flames made every tin and bottle glow like something from an old painting.
whatever:0.cnHint: 停电后，店长说无论____顾客进来，我们都要继续营业。
whatever:0.hook: Then the door opened, and something rolled across the dark floor.
whatever:0.line: '*Whatever* you need tonight, we still have it.'

predict:0.en: Tang checked the weather app three times before her shift. 'I can *predict* one thing,' she said, stacking the cup noodles. 'The power will cut out before midnight.' I laughed. At eleven fifty-eight, every light in the store went dead.
predict:0.cnHint: 阿糖说她能____停电的时间，我起初不信。
predict:0.hook: She was already holding the torch before I even reached for one.
predict:0.line: 'I can *predict* exactly when the lights will go out.'

road:0.en: Through the dark window I watched the *road* outside. Not a single car. Not a single lamp post working. The whole street had lost power. Only our store, running on the backup box, still made a small square of warm yellow light on the pavement.
road:0.cnHint: 停电后，窗外的____一片漆黑，只有我们小店还亮着。
road:0.hook: A figure at the far end of the road began walking toward us.
road:0.line: 'The whole *road* is dark — only our store has light.'

solution:0.en: The backup power box could not run both the fridge and the register. 'Pick one,' said the Manager. I thought for ten seconds. My *solution* was simple: take cash by hand, keep the fridge on, write every sale in a notebook. The Manager nodded slowly.
solution:0.cnHint: 我想出了一个____，让冰柜和收银都能在停电中运转。
solution:0.hook: The notebook was already half full by one in the morning.
solution:0.line: 'My *solution* keeps the fridge cold and the sales recorded.'

total:0.en: I added up the notebook by torchlight. Thirty-one customers in four dark hours. A *total* of two hundred and forty yuan in loose change and small notes, piled beside the candle. The Manager stared at the pile and said nothing for a long moment.
total:0.cnHint: 我用手电筒统计了停电期间的____销售额，数字让店长沉默了。
total:0.hook: Then he said, 'This is more than last Friday with full power.'
total:0.line: 'The *total* is higher than I expected — count it again.'

fail:0.en: The backup box began to hum louder near two in the morning. 'If it *fails*,' Tang said quietly, 'the ice cream section is finished.' We stood very still, listening. The hum steadied. We both let out a long breath at exactly the same time.
fail:0.cnHint: 备用电源快____了，阿糖担心冷冻区的冰淇淋全部融化。
fail:0.hook: An hour later the hum changed pitch again, lower and slower.
fail:0.line: 'If this box *fails*, we lose everything in the freezer.'

function:0.en: Lin arrived from the rival store down the block, carrying a small battery lamp. 'Ours lost all power,' she said. 'Nothing can *function* over there.' She set her lamp on our counter without asking and began helping Tang restock the shelves by its light.
function:0.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林说对面的店什么都无法____了，就跑来我们这里帮忙。
function:0.hook: She knew where every item on our shelves belonged, which was strange.
function:0.line: 'Nothing can *function* in my store — can I stay here a while?'

method:0.en: The Manager had a *method* for counting cash in the dark: sort by feel, stack by size, rubber-band each bundle. He taught me in under three minutes. My fingers learned the difference between a one-yuan coin and a five-yuan coin without any light at all.
method:0.cnHint: 店长教了我一种在黑暗中清点现金的____，我很快就学会了。
method:0.hook: He said he had learned it somewhere he did not want to name.
method:0.line: 'This *method* works even when you cannot see a single coin.'

review:0.en: The power had been out for twenty minutes. I lit a candle and found Tang sitting behind the counter, open notebook in hand. 'Night shift is perfect for a *review*,' she said, not even looking up. Outside, the street was dark and still. I had no idea she was studying for something so important.
review:0.cnHint: 停电后，阿糖借着烛光在便利店里____她的笔记。
review:0.hook: Her notebook was full of medical terms, not store codes.
review:0.line: 'A quiet night shift is honestly the best time for a *review*.'

ahead:0.en: The candles threw soft shadows across the shelves. Tang pointed her pen at the door. 'We still have the whole night *ahead* of us,' she said cheerfully. I looked at the dark street and the half-empty snack aisle and tried to feel the same way. Somehow, she always made it seem easy.
ahead:0.cnHint: 停电的漫漫长夜还在____，阿糖却显得毫不在意。
ahead:0.hook: Then we heard slow footsteps stop just outside the door.
ahead:0.line: 'Don't worry — we still have the whole night *ahead* of us.'

cheap:0.en: A regular came in just after the power failed, phone torch in hand. He picked up a small battery lamp from the shelf and frowned at the price tag. 'This feels a little *cheap*,' he muttered, shaking it. It flickered. He bought it anyway and shuffled back into the dark street without another word.
cheap:0.cnHint: 停电时，一位常客抱怨货架上的小灯质量____，却还是买走了。
cheap:0.hook: He was back ten minutes later, holding two broken pieces.
cheap:0.line: 'I don't mean the price — I mean it feels *cheap* in my hand.'

critical:0.en: The Manager called during the blackout to check on us. His voice was calm but serious. 'The fridge units are *critical* right now,' he said. 'Keep the doors closed no matter what.' Tang and I looked at each other across the candlelight. Neither of us had thought about the food going bad until that moment.
critical:0.cnHint: 停电期间，店长来电提醒我们，冷柜在这种时候是____的。
critical:0.hook: One fridge door was already open a crack.
critical:0.line: 'Listen — the fridge temperature is *critical* tonight, keep it shut.'

motivate:0.en: An hour into the blackout, I started to feel tired and a little low. Tang noticed and slid a warm canned drink across the counter to me. 'You need something to *motivate* you,' she said with a grin. It was a small thing, but somehow it worked. I stood up straighter and got back to tidying the shelves.
motivate:0.cnHint: 停电让我情绪低落，阿糖用一个小举动来____我打起精神。
motivate:0.hook: She said the Manager had done the same thing for her, once.
motivate:0.line: 'Here, take this — you need something to *motivate* you right now.'

charge:0.en: Around midnight a student rushed in, eyes wide. 'Do you have power? I need to *charge* my phone — my alarm is dead and I have an exam at eight.' Tang lit a second candle and shook her head slowly. The student stared at the unlit sockets on the wall and let out a long, quiet groan.
charge:0.cnHint: 一个学生冲进店里，想在停电的便利店里给手机____。
charge:0.hook: He sat down on the floor and did not leave.
charge:0.line: 'Please, I just need to *charge* my phone for ten minutes!'

complex:0.en: The fuse box was behind the cleaning supplies. The Manager had left a handwritten note about how to reset it, but the steps were long and the words were small. 'This is more *complex* than I expected,' I told Tang, holding the candle closer to the paper. She read it over my shoulder and nodded slowly.
complex:0.cnHint: 停电后，我发现店里的电路恢复步骤比预想的更____。
complex:0.hook: Step four on the note was crossed out and rewritten twice.
complex:0.line: 'I have to be honest — this diagram is way more *complex* than it looks.'

itself:0.en: Just before two in the morning, the lights came back on all at once. The fridge hummed, the radio crackled, and the store seemed to wake up by *itself*. Tang and I stood there blinking in the sudden brightness. Neither of us said anything for a moment. Then she quietly closed her notebook and smiled.
itself:0.cnHint: 快到凌晨两点时，便利店突然____恢复了灯光和电力。
itself:0.hook: The student asleep on the floor had missed the whole thing.
itself:0.line: 'Look — the store just turned *itself* back on. That's kind of magical.'

join:0.en: The power cut turned the store into a cave of shadows. I lit three candles on the counter. Then the old man from next door knocked on the glass door and pointed inside. I waved him in. 'Come *join* us,' I said. He smiled and sat beside Tang on a crate.
join:0.cnHint: 停电了，店里点起蜡烛，一位老邻居敲门想进来____我们。
join:0.hook: He carried a small tin box he refused to put down.
join:0.line: 'Come *join* us — there is plenty of candle light for everyone.'

significant:0.en: Tang and I sorted the shelves by candlelight while the Manager paced behind us. She stopped at the canned-food row and tapped one tin. 'This spot is *significant*,' she said quietly. 'Every big storm, every cut, every strange night — something always happens right here.' Tang and I exchanged a look.
significant:0.cnHint: 店长指着货架上某个位置说，它在每个特殊夜晚都格外____。
significant:0.hook: Neither of us dared ask what had happened there before.
significant:0.line: 'This corner is *significant* — watch it carefully tonight.'

step:0.en: The backup light above the door had died. I moved slowly through the dark aisle, arms out, feeling for the shelf edge. Then I heard a soft *step* behind me — not Tang, not the Manager. Someone else was in the store. I turned around and saw nothing but shadow.
step:0.cnHint: 停电后店里一片黑暗，我听到身后传来一声陌生的____。
step:0.hook: A cold draft followed, though every door was shut.
step:0.line: 'I heard a *step* — someone is back there, I am sure.'

unique:0.en: Lin from the shop across the street brought over her own lantern during the blackout. It had a paper shade painted with little fish. 'It is *unique*,' I admitted. She set it on our counter without a word and the warm orange light filled the whole front room like a small sunrise.
unique:0.cnHint: 竞争对手林带来了一盏____的纸灯笼，把整个店头照得暖意融融。
unique:0.hook: She left before I could ask where she had bought it.
unique:0.line: 'My lantern is *unique* — you will not find another one like it.'

inside:0.en: The street was completely dark, but our candles gave the store a soft glow. People passing outside pressed their faces to the glass. I waved them in one by one. Soon seven strangers stood *inside*, sharing a bag of chips and talking in low, easy voices as though they had always known each other.
inside:0.cnHint: 停电的夜晚，路人们纷纷聚到店____，陌生人之间聊得很投机。
inside:0.hook: One woman in the corner had not spoken a single word yet.
inside:0.line: 'Please come *inside* — it is warmer here than on the street.'

majority:0.en: I did a quiet head-count at midnight. Seven customers, two staff, one Manager. The *majority* of them had come in only to escape the dark street, yet now nobody wanted to leave. Someone had found a deck of cards. The Manager pretended not to notice and went to make hot tea.
majority:0.cnHint: 午夜盘点，店里大____的人都是为了躲避黑暗街道而进来的。
majority:0.hook: The man with the tin box had moved closer to the candle.
majority:0.line: 'The *majority* of you came for light — but stay for the tea.'

notice:0.en: For the first hour of the blackout I was too busy handing out candles to look at faces. Then Tang nudged me. 'Did you *notice* the kid in the blue jacket?' I had not. A small boy sat alone on the step by the door, reading a comic by candlelight, completely calm.
notice:0.cnHint: 停电忙乱中，同事提醒我有没有____到角落里那个独自看书的小男孩。
notice:0.hook: No adult in the store seemed to know whose child he was.
notice:0.line: '*Notice* the boy by the door — he has been sitting there alone.'

taste:0.en: The Manager opened a box of sample chocolates that had been sitting under the counter for weeks. She passed them around. I took one and was surprised — it had a faint smoky *taste*, warm and a little strange, perfectly right for a night of candles and shadows. Nobody said a word.
taste:0.cnHint: 停电的夜里，店长拿出一盒样品巧克力，我尝出了一种奇特的____。
taste:0.hook: The Manager's expression when she ate hers was hard to read.
taste:0.line: 'The *taste* is unusual — tell me honestly what you think of it.'

differ:0.en: The power cut turned the store into a cave of shadows. I lit two candles and watched the light dance. Tang grabbed a torch and walked the aisles slowly. 'Every blackout *differs*,' he said, 'but they all make customers hungry.' Sure enough, the snack shelf emptied in minutes.
differ:0.cnHint: 停电让店里变暗，阿糖说每次停电都____，但顾客总会变得很饿。
differ:0.hook: One hungry customer kept staring at the back door.
differ:0.line: Every blackout *differs*, but they all make customers hungry.

shape:0.en: The power died at midnight. I held up my phone torch and saw strange shadows on the wall. One shadow had a tall, thin *shape* — almost like a person standing very still. I turned around fast. It was only Tang hanging his coat on a hook. I laughed, alone and nervous.
shape:0.cnHint: 停电后我看到墙上有个奇怪的____，吓了一跳，原来只是阿糖挂着的外套。
shape:0.hook: But Tang said he had not brought his coat tonight.
shape:0.line: That *shape* on the wall really scared me just now.

twice:0.en: The lights came back on, then died again. That happened *twice* in one hour. Every time the store went dark, the same old man near the window stood up and looked outside. He never bought anything. He just watched the street. By midnight, I was more curious about him than about the broken power.
twice:0.cnHint: 停电____发生，每次一停电，窗边的老人就会站起来往外看。
twice:0.hook: On the third blackout, his seat was empty.
twice:0.line: The lights have gone out *twice* already — something is wrong.

aspect:0.en: Tang walked me through every *aspect* of the blackout plan: where the torches were, which snacks to push, how to calm worried customers. He spoke quickly, like a soldier before a battle. Outside, the whole street was dark. Inside, our small store glowed like a warm island. I felt almost proud.
aspect:0.cnHint: 阿糖向我讲解了停电应对计划的每个____，让我感觉自己像个真正的店员。
aspect:0.hook: Then the Manager called — and Tang's face went pale.
aspect:0.line: I have checked every *aspect* of the plan — we are ready.

currently:0.en: 'The whole block is *currently* without power,' the Manager said over the phone, his voice very calm. I looked at the queue forming at our door — people carrying empty bowls, bags, and sad faces. Our generator hummed. We were the only lit place on the street. That felt heavy.
currently:0.cnHint: 店长打来电话说整条街____没有电，我们的小店成了黑暗中唯一的亮光。
currently:0.hook: A woman in the queue was quietly counting her coins.
currently:0.line: The whole street is *currently* dark — we must stay open.

decrease:0.en: As the blackout stretched past two hours, the crowd outside began to *decrease*. People gave up and went home. Only a few stayed — an old man, a student with a thick book, and a woman knitting by the window. The store felt quieter, softer. I made three cups of tea, just because I could.
decrease:0.cnHint: 随着停电时间变长，店外的人群开始____，只剩几个常客安静地待着。
decrease:0.hook: The knitting woman had not moved or blinked for twenty minutes.
decrease:0.line: I'm glad the crowd will *decrease* — now we can breathe.

possibility:0.en: Tang stared at the fuse box for a long time. 'There's a *possibility* it'll trip again in an hour,' he said slowly. I wrote that down. We had sold almost every candle. One small box remained. I put it behind the counter, hidden. Some things you keep just in case the night grows longer.
possibility:0.cnHint: 阿糖说还有____会再次跳闸，我悄悄把最后一盒蜡烛藏了起来。
possibility:0.hook: An hour later, Tang's watch alarm went off.
possibility:0.line: There's a *possibility* the power will fail again tonight.

crucial:0.en: Tang pulled me aside near the back shelf. '*Crucial* thing,' he whispered: never let the generator run dry. If it died, so did the chilled food — thousands of coins lost in one warm hour. He handed me a small checklist and tapped it twice. I folded it and put it in my pocket.
crucial:0.cnHint: 阿糖告诉我一件____的事：绝对不能让发电机断油，否则冷藏食品全会坏掉。
crucial:0.hook: Twenty minutes later, I heard the generator sputter.
crucial:0.line: The *crucial* thing is to keep the generator running all night.

rule:0.en: The power went out at midnight. The Manager lit a candle and pointed to a handwritten sign on the wall. 'One *rule* here,' he said quietly. 'We stay open.' Outside, the dark street was empty. I watched the small flame and decided I liked working here.
rule:0.cnHint: 停电后，店长指着墙上的告示，说明这里只有一条____。
rule:0.hook: But someone was already knocking on the locked back door.
rule:0.line: 'One *rule* here — we never, ever close early.'

plant:0.en: A woman in a raincoat came in during the blackout, carrying a small potted *plant*. She set it on the counter without a word, smiled at me, and walked back into the dark street. The little green leaves caught the candle light and seemed almost happy.
plant:0.cnHint: 停电的夜里，一位女士带着一盆____悄悄放在收银台上就离开了。
plant:0.hook: A note was buried in the soil — I could see the corner of it.
plant:0.line: 'This little *plant* needs light, just like this store does.'

national:0.en: Tang was humming a soft tune while counting coins by flashlight. 'What song is that?' I asked. 'An old *national* folk song,' she said. 'My grandfather sang it.' The melody floated through the dark store, mixing with the sound of rain, and for a moment everything felt very still.
national:0.cnHint: 停电时，同事哼着一首____民歌，让小店突然多了一种特别的气氛。
national:0.hook: Then her phone buzzed and her face went pale.
national:0.line: 'It is an old *national* folk song — my grandfather loved it most.'

doctor:0.en: A tired-looking man in a white coat came in and bought three bottles of water and a bar of chocolate. 'Long shift?' I asked. He nodded. 'I am a *doctor* at the clinic up the road,' he said. 'We are using backup lights.' He paid in coins and disappeared into the rain.
doctor:0.cnHint: 停电期间，一位附近诊所的____走进来买了水和巧克力，疲惫不堪。
doctor:0.hook: He left behind a folded paper — it looked like a patient's record.
doctor:0.line: 'I am a *doctor*, and right now I really need that chocolate.'

economy:0.en: Lin came in at two in the morning and studied every price tag with great care. 'Big purchase?' I asked. He shook his head. 'Personal *economy*,' he said with a straight face. 'I track every cent.' He bought the cheapest cup of instant noodles, sat down, and opened a thick notebook.
economy:0.cnHint: 凌晨两点，竞争对手走进来，认真研究价格，声称自己讲究个人____。
economy:0.hook: The notebook was full of tiny red circles — all around our prices.
economy:0.line: 'Personal *economy* is a serious skill — I never waste a cent.'

global:0.en: The Manager spread an old map across the counter while we waited for the power to return. He tapped a dozen cities with his finger. 'I have worked in all these places,' he said. 'But a small store at night feels more *global* than any big office. Everyone shows up here.' I believed him.
global:0.cnHint: 停电时，店长摊开地图，说这家小店比任何大办公室都更有____的感觉。
global:0.hook: One city on the map had a small key taped over it.
global:0.line: 'A quiet night store feels more *global* than any big office I know.'

leader:0.en: When the lights died, every customer looked around nervously. The Manager walked to the centre of the store, calm and slow. Someone called out, 'What do we do?' He just smiled. A good *leader*, I thought, does not need to shout. He handed out candles, and people relaxed at once.
leader:0.cnHint: 停电时大家慌乱，店长镇定分发蜡烛，让我明白了一个好____的样子。
leader:0.hook: Then he handed me a candle and whispered a single strange instruction.
leader:0.line: 'A real *leader* just keeps moving — no shouting, no fuss, just action.'

scientific:0.en: Tang pulled out a small notebook and began recording the time, temperature, and number of customers by candlelight. 'What are you doing?' I asked. 'A *scientific* study,' she said cheerfully. 'Blackouts change people's buying habits. I have three months of data already.' She clicked her pen and looked at me as a potential subject.
scientific:0.cnHint: 停电时，同事拿出笔记本，认真做关于停电期间消费习惯的____研究。
scientific:0.hook: She turned the notebook to show me — my own name was already on page one.
scientific:0.line: 'It is a *scientific* study — three months of blackout data, all mine.'

enormous:0.en: The power went out at midnight. I found one candle behind the counter and lit it. The flame was small, but on the wall it threw an *enormous* shadow — my shadow, stretched tall and strange, like a giant watching over the empty store. Tang laughed when they saw it. I did not expect that laugh to make me feel so much better.
enormous:0.cnHint: 停电后，微弱的烛光在墙上投下了一个____的影子，让同事忍不住笑了出来。
enormous:0.hook: But Tang's smile faded the moment they glanced at the door.
enormous:0.line: 'That *enormous* shadow on the wall — is that really you?'

pet:0.en: A regular came in during the blackout, guided only by the light of my candle. She carried a small box close to her chest. Inside, curled up on a soft cloth, was a tiny *pet* rabbit — grey, quiet, and very still. 'The dark scares him,' she whispered. She bought two carrot snacks and left without another word.
pet:0.cnHint: 停电时，一位常客抱着装有____的盒子走进来，说黑暗会让它害怕。
pet:0.hook: She came back ten minutes later, alone, and without the box.
pet:0.line: 'My *pet* hates the dark, so I had to bring him with me.'

restaurant:0.en: Lin from the *restaurant* across the street knocked on our glass door just after the lights died. 'Your generator — do you have one?' they asked. We did not. Lin stood there a moment, looking at our candle, then back at their own dark windows. Without a word, Lin pulled a chair up to our counter and waited with us.
restaurant:0.cnHint: 停电后，对面____的林敲门来借发电机，最后却默默坐下来陪我们等待来电。
restaurant:0.hook: Lin had never once set foot in our store before tonight.
restaurant:0.line: 'The *restaurant* is completely dark — I had to come somewhere.'

driver:0.en: A delivery *driver* rolled up on a small scooter, engine humming in the quiet street. He knocked, then held his phone screen to the glass so we could read his order. I filled it by candle light — three rice balls and a hot tea. He bowed twice before he left. I watched his tail-light shrink into the dark.
driver:0.cnHint: 停电后，一位外卖____骑车来取餐，我在烛光下替他备好了食物。
driver:0.hook: His order note said: 'For the old man at building nine — he is waiting.'
driver:0.line: 'I am a *driver*, so the dark road does not scare me much.'

dream:0.en: The store was silent and dark except for one candle. I sat on the step stool and, without meaning to, began to *dream* with my eyes open — of a warmer job, a brighter room, a full night's sleep. Tang nudged me gently. 'Still with us?' they asked. The candle had burned almost halfway down.
dream:0.cnHint: 停电的寂静中，我不知不觉开始____起来，被同事轻轻推醒后才发现蜡烛已燃了一半。
dream:0.hook: On the floor beside my foot was a note I had never seen before.
dream:0.line: 'Don't *dream* too long — the Manager checks the camera logs.'

consumer:0.en: The Manager called during the outage to check on us. 'Every *consumer* who comes in tonight,' they said, 'give them a free hot drink from the thermos. Good will costs less than a bad review.' I wrote that down. Tang read it over my shoulder and said, 'The Manager is wiser than they look.'
consumer:0.cnHint: 停电期间，店长来电说要给每位____提供免费热饮，切勿因停电损害口碑。
consumer:0.hook: The thermos, we then discovered, was completely empty.
consumer:0.line: 'Each *consumer* tonight gets a free drink — Manager's order.'

interesting:0.en: An old man came in, felt his way to the snack shelf, and chose the same item every time: one bag of spicy peas. I found that *interesting*, so I asked him why. He smiled and said, 'Young one, when you find the thing that is always good, you stop looking for something better.' He paid exact change in the dark without counting.
interesting:0.cnHint: 停电夜里，一位老先生的购物习惯让我觉得很____，他的回答更让我若有所思。
interesting:0.hook: He left a second coin on the counter that did not match any price.
interesting:0.line: 'You find that *interesting*? I have done it for twenty years.'

grade:0.en: A student came in, eyes red, holding her phone to her chest. She bought a small chocolate bar and said nothing for a long time. Then, very quietly: 'I got my *grade* back. It is not good.' I pushed another chocolate bar across the counter without charging her. She looked up, surprised. Sometimes one small thing is enough.
grade:0.cnHint: 停电夜里，一个学生来买东西，轻声说自己的____出来了，结果不太好。
grade:0.hook: She left her student card on the counter — and it had a different name on it.
grade:0.line: 'My *grade* came back tonight, and I really needed some chocolate.'

evidence:0.en: The power cut at midnight. I lit a candle and looked around the quiet store. Something felt wrong. A shelf near the door had been moved. Bags of rice were pushed aside. There was clear *evidence* that someone had been searching for something — but what?
evidence:0.cnHint: 停电后，店员发现货架被动过，留下了____。
evidence:0.hook: The footprints in the flour led straight to the back room.
evidence:0.line: 'Look at this — solid *evidence* that someone was here before us.'

prefer:0.en: Tang brought two candles from the back room during the blackout. 'We could use the emergency light,' I said. Tang shook his head with a calm smile. 'I *prefer* candles. They make the store feel like a cosy little world.' I had to admit — he was right.
prefer:0.cnHint: 停电时，同事说他____烛光而不是应急灯。
prefer:0.hook: Then Tang blew one candle out and whispered something to the dark.
prefer:0.line: 'Honestly, I *prefer* candles — they hide the messy corners nicely.'

interview:0.en: A young woman came in at two in the morning carrying a small recorder. She said she wanted to *interview* people who work night shifts for her college newspaper. The store was dark except for one candle. I said yes before I could think twice.
interview:0.cnHint: 深夜，一位大学生来____夜班工作者，恰好碰上了停电。
interview:0.hook: Her first question made me forget every answer I had prepared.
interview:0.line: 'May I *interview* you about what night shifts are really like?'

middle:0.en: The power went out right in the *middle* of the Manager's careful stock count. He froze, pencil in hand, numbers half written in his notebook. The candle Tang lit threw long shadows across the shelves. The Manager did not speak for a full minute.
middle:0.cnHint: 停电发生在店长盘点的____，他愣在原地。
middle:0.hook: When he finally spoke, the number he said made no sense at all.
middle:0.line: 'It always breaks down right in the *middle* of something important.'

standard:0.en: Lin walked in from the street, barely wet despite the heavy rain outside. I asked how. She held up a small folding umbrella and said, '*Standard* kit. Night-shift people carry one always.' She set it by the door and bought one coffee, same as every night.
standard:0.cnHint: 停电后的雨夜，竞争对手拿出了她____的夜班装备。
standard:0.hook: But tonight Lin did not leave after her coffee — she just waited.
standard:0.line: 'A small umbrella is *standard* kit — you should get one too.'

subject:0.en: During the blackout Tang lit a second candle and sat beside me. We talked softly to pass the time. The *subject* drifted from store rules to childhood food to the strange peace of an empty street at three in the morning. It felt good, that talk.
subject:0.cnHint: 停电夜里，闲聊的____从店规飘到了童年的食物。
subject:0.hook: Then Tang said one sentence that changed the whole mood completely.
subject:0.line: 'The *subject* keeps changing — what do you actually want to talk about?'

accept:0.en: The Manager asked me to stay two extra hours because the other clerk had not come. I looked at the dark street, the quiet shelves, the single candle still burning. I decided to *accept*. There was something almost peaceful about the store in the middle of a blackout.
accept:0.cnHint: 店长请店员多留两小时，店员决定____这个请求。
accept:0.hook: Ten minutes later, a knock came at the locked back door.
accept:0.line: 'I will *accept*, but only if you tell me what we are watching for.'

act:0.en: When a child separated from her mother ran in crying, Lin did not hesitate. Her whole body changed — calm voice, soft hands, a gentle *act* of kindness so smooth it looked practised. She found the mother in two minutes. Then Lin went straight back to her cold coffee.
act:0.cnHint: 与母亲走散的孩子跑进来，竞争对手立刻____起来帮忙。
act:0.hook: I realised I had never once asked Lin what she did before this street.
act:0.line: 'Just *act* natural — the kid needs to feel safe right now.'

decline:0.en: The power cut hit at midnight. Sales had been falling all week, and the Manager kept a small notebook tracking every hour. 'Look at this *decline*,' he said, tapping the page. Outside, the street lamps were dead. Inside, three candles made the shelves look warmer than usual.
decline:0.cnHint: 停电之夜，店长翻开笔记本，盯着本周营业额的____发愁。
decline:0.hook: Then a stranger walked in, carrying something wrapped in cloth.
decline:0.line: 'This *decline* started the night the old road closed.'

extra:0.en: Tang found four boxes of candles behind the storage shelf just as the lights went out. 'Perfect timing,' she said. She lit one for the counter and handed me two. The third she kept for herself. That left one *extra*, which she placed near the door for anyone coming in from the dark street.
extra:0.cnHint: 停电时，阿糖在储物架后找到了蜡烛，还多出了一根____的。
extra:0.hook: Nobody touched that candle by the door — until 2 a.m.
extra:0.line: 'Here, take this *extra* one in case yours burns out.'

income:0.en: The Manager sat behind the counter counting receipts by candlelight. He told me the store was his only *income* since he sold his old repair shop. Every coin mattered. He smoothed each receipt flat with his thumb, like he was reading a letter from someone far away.
income:0.cnHint: 停电后，店长借着烛光数收据，这家店是他唯一的____来源。
income:0.hook: One receipt, dated three years ago, made him go very quiet.
income:0.line: 'This store is my only *income* now, so every night counts.'

medicine:0.en: Just after midnight a woman knocked hard on the glass door. She looked tired and a little frightened. Her child had a fever, she said. She needed *medicine* fast. Tang went straight to the shelf without a torch, moving by memory alone, and returned in under ten seconds holding the right box.
medicine:0.cnHint: 午夜一位母亲敲门，停电中的阿糖凭记忆帮她找到了____。
medicine:0.hook: The woman paid, then whispered something to Tang that made Tang freeze.
medicine:0.line: 'Please, do you have any *medicine* for a child's high fever?'

private:0.en: During the blackout the Manager moved a small tin box from under the counter to his coat pocket. He caught me looking and gave a short smile. 'Just something *private*,' he said quietly. He asked no questions and I asked none. Some things in a convenience store are not for sale.
private:0.cnHint: 停电时，店长把一个小铁盒悄悄放进口袋，说那是____的东西。
private:0.hook: Later I noticed the tin was the same size as a photo frame.
private:0.line: 'It is something *private* — please do not ask me about it.'

side:0.en: The freezer hummed its last hum and went silent. Tang and I moved all the ice cream to a cooler box. She took the left *side*, I took the right. We worked fast and said little. When we finished, she handed me a cone from the bottom of the pile. 'Waste not,' she said.
side:0.cnHint: 停电后，阿糖和我分工合作，各守冰柜的一____，把冰淇淋转移保存。
side:0.hook: One of the ice cream tubs had a name written on the lid.
side:0.line: 'You take that *side*, I will handle this one — we must hurry.'
