air:0.en: With the fans off and the door closed, the *air* inside the store grew thick and warm, carrying the smell of candle wax and instant noodles. Lin arrived at half past twelve, looked around slowly, and said it felt like a different place entirely. She was right. Darkness changes a room.
air:0.cnHint: 停电后店内____变得闷热，隔壁咖啡店的林进门后说这里感觉像换了个地方。
air:0.hook: Lin then asked for something we had never stocked before.
air:0.line: 'The *air* in here tonight feels strange — like before a storm.'

consumption:0.en: The Manager studied the generator manual by candlelight. He pointed to a small chart. 'High *consumption*,' he said, meaning it burned fuel too fast to run all night. We agreed to use it only for the fridge. The rest of the store stayed dark, and somehow that felt right.
consumption:0.cnHint: 停电后，店长查看发电机手册，担心燃料的____太快撑不过夜。
consumption:0.hook: The fridge light flickered once, then showed something odd inside.
consumption:0.line: 'The fuel *consumption* is too high — we must turn off the lights.'

estimate:0.en: The power went out at eleven. I lit a candle and looked around the dark store. The Manager had left me a note: 'My *estimate* is two hours — keep the cold drinks closed and count the cash by hand.' I nodded at the empty room, feeling very alone.
estimate:0.cnHint: 停电后，店长留了张纸条，对停电时长做了____，让我按指示行动。
estimate:0.hook: But the note also said: 'Don't open the back room.'
estimate:0.line: 'My *estimate* is two hours, so stay calm and wait.'

explore:0.en: With the lights gone, the store felt bigger somehow. I decided to *explore* the shelves I had never really looked at — the dusty back corner full of odd snacks from places I could not name. A small tin caught my eye. Someone had written a date on it in red pen.
explore:0.cnHint: 停电让我有时间____平时没注意到的货架角落，结果发现了奇怪的东西。
explore:0.hook: The date on the tin was next week.
explore:0.line: 'Go ahead and *explore* — you might find something useful back there.'

fix:0.en: The candle kept falling over on the counter. Tang appeared from the back, took one look, and pressed the candle into a cup of uncooked rice. 'That should *fix* it,' she said, dusting off her hands. The flame stood perfectly still. I felt a little embarrassed I had not thought of that.
fix:0.cnHint: 蜡烛老倒，同事用米杯____了这个问题，让我有些不好意思。
fix:0.hook: Then Tang gave me a look that said the rice was not really for candles.
fix:0.line: 'A cup of rice will *fix* it — here, let me show you.'

general:0.en: Lin came in just after midnight, flashlight in hand. 'How are sales?' she asked, already scanning the shelves. 'In *general* the night shift is slow,' I said, 'but tonight is different — everyone wants candles.' She smiled in a way I could not quite read and picked up the last box.
general:0.cnHint: 竞争对手深夜进店问生意，我说____情况如何，但今晚有些特别。
general:0.hook: She bought the last box of candles but did not seem to need them.
general:0.line: 'In *general*, slow nights are the ones worth watching closely.'

loss:0.en: The refrigerators hummed to silence. I made a list of everything inside and felt a quiet worry. The Manager had once told me that a single night's *loss* from spoiled stock could erase a whole week of profit. I checked the time. One hour down. One more to go — maybe.
loss:0.cnHint: 冰柜停了，我担心食物损坏带来的____会抹掉一周的利润。
loss:0.hook: Then I heard one of the fridges click back on — just one.
loss:0.line: 'Any *loss* from tonight comes straight out of the weekend numbers.'

partner:0.en: Around one in the morning a man knocked on the glass door. 'Is the person who runs this place here?' he asked. I shook my head. 'I used to be his *partner*,' he said softly, looking at the dark shelves like he was remembering something. He bought nothing and left quietly.
partner:0.cnHint: 深夜有人敲门，自称是店长曾经的____，只是静静看了看就离开了。
partner:0.hook: He left a folded piece of paper under the door mat.
partner:0.line: 'I was his *partner* here, a long time ago — before things changed.'

concept:0.en: Tang tried to explain the new digital inventory system to me by candlelight. I stared at her hand-drawn diagram. 'The *concept* is simple,' she said, tapping the paper. 'Everything that comes in gets a number. Everything that goes out loses one.' I nodded, but the shadows were making the numbers dance.
concept:0.cnHint: 同事借烛光给我讲新系统，说这个____其实很简单，但我没太看明白。
concept:0.hook: One number on the diagram had been circled three times in red.
concept:0.line: 'The *concept* is simple — in gets a number, out loses one.'

history:0.en: I found an old notebook under the counter while searching for a spare pen. Page after page of tiny handwriting — dates, names, small notes about regular customers. Someone had kept a careful *history* of every person who walked through the door for years. The most recent entry was tonight's date.
history:0.cnHint: 我在柜台下发现一本旧笔记本，记录着多年来的____，最新一页竟是今晚的日期。
history:0.hook: My own name was already written on that last page.
history:0.line: 'This store has a long *history* — someone always wrote everything down.'

attack:0.en: The power cut hit at midnight. Every shelf went dark, and the old fridge began to make a low, angry sound. Then a sudden *attack* of fear swept through me — I was alone, the street was silent, and the back door was open.
attack:0.cnHint: 停电后，店员突然感到一阵____，发现后门是开着的。
attack:0.hook: A shadow moved just beyond the open door.
attack:0.line: 'That *attack* of fear — did you feel it too?' Tang whispered.

heavy:0.en: Tang dragged in a large box of emergency candles just after the lights died. It was *heavy* enough that he knocked over a display of instant noodles trying to set it down. We laughed, then got to work placing candles along every counter.
heavy:0.cnHint: 停电后，唐搬来一箱很____的应急蜡烛，差点撞翻货架。
heavy:0.hook: The last candle flickered and went out.
heavy:0.line: 'This box is *heavy* — could you hold the door open?'

thought:0.en: I sat behind the counter with a single candle and let my mind wander. My first *thought* was that the whole street must look magical from outside. Then the door chimed, and a small boy in a school uniform walked in, completely calm.
thought:0.cnHint: 停电时，店员独自坐在烛光下，脑海中突然有了一个____。
thought:0.hook: The boy asked for something we had never stocked.
thought:0.line: 'My first *thought* was to call the Manager,' I admitted to Tang.

attract:0.en: Tang lit a row of candles on the windowsill to *attract* any customer who might be nervous about stepping into a dark shop. The warm glow spread across the wet pavement outside. Within minutes, three people pushed through the door, looking relieved.
attract:0.cnHint: 唐在橱窗摆上蜡烛，想用灯光____路过的顾客进店。
attract:0.hook: One of the three never said a single word all night.
attract:0.line: 'We need something to *attract* people — candles in the window should work.'

define:0.en: The Manager called from home to check on us. 'How would you *define* the situation?' she asked, sounding both worried and businesslike. I looked at Tang, who was balancing a candle on top of the coffee machine, and said, 'Cosy, I think.'
define:0.cnHint: 店长打来电话，想让店员____一下当前停电的状况。
define:0.hook: The Manager went quiet for just a little too long.
define:0.line: 'Can you *define* the problem before I drive over?'

executive:0.en: A man in a neat coat came in just before one in the morning and bought four bottles of water without a word. Tang nudged me later. 'That is the *executive* who owns the building across the street,' he said. 'He comes here every blackout.'
executive:0.cnHint: 一位衣着整洁的____在停电期间悄悄来买水，唐认出了他。
executive:0.hook: No one knew why he always came alone.
executive:0.line: 'That *executive* buys the same four bottles every time,' Tang said.

expectation:0.en: My *expectation* had been that a blackout night would be slow and dull. Instead, the candle-lit store drew a steady stream of neighbours I had never met: an elderly painter, a night-school teacher, a man carrying a very sleepy cat.
expectation:0.cnHint: 店员原以为停电之夜会很冷清，结果完全超出了他的____。
expectation:0.hook: The man with the cat sat down and showed no sign of leaving.
expectation:0.line: 'My *expectation* was zero customers tonight — I was so wrong.'

friendly:0.en: Lin appeared at half past midnight, supposedly just to 'check the competition.' But she brought a bag of spare batteries and helped us restock the candle display without being asked. For the first time she seemed genuinely *friendly*, and that surprised me most.
friendly:0.cnHint: 停电夜里，竞争对手林出人意料地表现得非常____，还带来了备用电池。
friendly:0.hook: She left before I could ask why she really came.
friendly:0.line: 'I can be *friendly* — stop looking so surprised,' Lin said, smiling.

field:0.en: The power cut the lights at eleven. Tang lit a small candle on the counter and sighed. 'Back in my school days, I spent every evening on the *field*, running laps until the sky went dark,' he said. The flame made his face look younger, almost like a boy again.
field:0.cnHint: 停电后，阿糖在烛光中聊起自己曾在____上奔跑的青春岁月。
field:0.hook: Then he glanced at the door, as if expecting someone.
field:0.line: I used to own that *field* after sunset.

personality:0.en: The candle threw shadows across the shelves. A regular customer, a quiet woman in a grey coat, came in for warm tea. Tang leaned over to me and whispered, 'She has a strong *personality* — argued with the Manager for an hour once over a ten-cent price difference.' She smiled at us and said nothing.
personality:0.cnHint: 停电夜里，阿糖悄悄告诉我这位常客拥有鲜明的____，曾为小事与店长争论。
personality:0.hook: She picked up exactly three items — the same three every time.
personality:0.line: That quiet type always has the strongest *personality*.

size:0.en: Without power, the fridge units hummed to a stop. I checked our stock by torchlight and found only one hot-pack rice box left. A tall student ducked in, looked at it, then looked at me. 'What *size* is that portion?' he asked hopefully. I held it up. He bought it in two seconds flat.
size:0.cnHint: 停电后冰柜停转，一位高个学生进来询问剩下那份饭的____。
size:0.hook: He ate it standing outside, and then came back in.
size:0.line: Does it really matter what *size* it is right now?

schedule:0.en: The Manager called from home during the blackout. 'Follow the normal *schedule*,' he said firmly over the phone. 'Restock the front shelf at midnight, mop at one.' Tang held the candle close to the handwritten chart on the wall and nodded, even though the Manager could not see him at all.
schedule:0.cnHint: 停电时店长打来电话，要求我们严格按____继续工作。
schedule:0.hook: The chart had one strange task written in red ink.
schedule:0.line: We keep to the *schedule* no matter what happens.

towards:0.en: The street outside was completely dark. Through the glass door I watched a small figure move slowly *towards* the store, guided only by the faint candle glow in our window. Tang straightened up and smoothed his uniform. 'That walk,' he murmured, 'I know that walk.'
towards:0.cnHint: 漆黑的停电夜，一个身影朝我们店____缓缓走来，阿糖却认出了对方的步态。
towards:0.hook: The figure stopped just short of the door.
towards:0.line: She is walking *towards* us — and she looks angry.

background:0.en: While we waited for the power to return, Tang told me about Lin. 'Interesting *background*,' he said, refilling the candle dish. 'Studied business overseas, then came back to open a rival store two blocks away. Nobody really knows why she chose this quiet street.' Outside, a car passed without slowing down.
background:0.cnHint: 停电的空闲里，阿糖向我讲述了隔壁咖啡店的林不同寻常的____和回国开店的经历。
background:0.hook: Tang never finished his sentence — the lights snapped back on.
background:0.line: Her *background* explains why she always undercuts our prices.

department:0.en: The power blinked back on for one minute, then died again. In the confusion, a delivery arrived — boxes addressed to the wrong store. The label read: Lin's shop, snack *department*. Tang stared at the boxes, then at me. 'We could just... keep them until morning,' he said, not quite meeting my eyes.
department:0.cnHint: 停电混乱中，竟收到了发给隔壁咖啡店的林那家店____的货物，阿糖的提议让我有些担心。
department:0.hook: One box was already open at the corner.
department:0.line: These belong to her snack *department*, not ours.

detail:0.en: At two in the morning the power finally came back for good. The Manager appeared without warning, walking every aisle in silence. Then he stopped at the front shelf. 'One *detail*,' he said quietly, pointing to a single juice bottle facing the wrong way. Tang and I exchanged a look. He sees everything.
detail:0.cnHint: 深夜终于来电，店长悄然视察，只为指出货架上一个微小的____。
detail:0.hook: Then the Manager turned and looked straight at me.
detail:0.line: Never overlook a single *detail* on my shelf.

indeed:0.en: The lights went out at midnight. Every shelf, every corner fell into thick darkness. I grabbed a torch and swept it slowly around the store. The Manager had warned me this old building lost power sometimes. It was *indeed* as bad as he said — not a single bulb survived.
indeed:0.cnHint: 停电那一刻，店里____像店长说的那样糟糕。
indeed:0.hook: But one shadow near the back door had not moved at all.
indeed:0.line: It is *indeed* a bad night for this old building.

launch:0.en: Lin arrived just after the blackout, carrying a box of candles. 'Tonight is the *launch* of our new emergency kit sale,' she announced, setting them on the counter with a grin. She had planned this. The candles were already priced and tagged. I stared. Had she known the power would fail?
launch:0.cnHint: 停电后，隔壁咖啡店的林把这次停电当作新急救套装____的好时机。
launch:0.hook: The price tags were printed hours before the outage.
launch:0.line: Think of it as the *launch* of our emergency kit sale!

refer:0.en: Tang lit a small candle and opened a thick binder. 'When the power dies, we *refer* to this manual,' he said calmly, turning to a page titled Night-Outage Steps. He walked me through each item one by one. I had never seen anyone so prepared for darkness.
refer:0.cnHint: 停电后，阿糖翻开手册，告诉我遇到停电要____这本指南。
refer:0.hook: Page seven had a handwritten note nobody could explain.
refer:0.line: We always *refer* to this manual when the lights die.

trust:0.en: The Manager handed me the key to the back safe before he left for the night. 'I *trust* you with this,' he said quietly. It felt heavier than any key should. Outside, the street went dark as the blackout crept closer, block by block, and I held the key very tight.
trust:0.cnHint: 店长把保险箱的钥匙交给我，说他____我。
trust:0.hook: A knock on the back door came only seconds later.
trust:0.line: I *trust* you with this key tonight.

discussion:0.en: During the blackout Tang, Lin and I sat on empty crates near the candle. A quiet *discussion* started about which snack would survive a week without power. Lin insisted on crackers; Tang argued for canned peaches. I said nothing — I was too busy counting how many candles we had left.
discussion:0.cnHint: 停电时，三人围着蜡烛展开了一场关于零食的____。
discussion:0.hook: Then Lin mentioned she had a full year of canned goods at home.
discussion:0.line: This *discussion* about snacks is more serious than it looks.

extremely:0.en: The freezer hummed to a stop and the whole store fell silent. It was *extremely* hot without the fans, and sweat ran down my neck. I fanned myself with a paper bag. Tang passed me a cold bottle from a cooler he had quietly filled with ice an hour earlier. I could have cried.
extremely:0.cnHint: 风扇停转后，店里____热，阿糖悄悄拿出了冰块。
extremely:0.hook: That cooler had just enough ice for one more hour.
extremely:0.line: It is *extremely* hot in here without the fans.

organize:0.en: Lin decided someone had to *organize* the torches, candles and matches into one clear spot near the counter. She sorted them by size, labelled each group with a sticky note, and stepped back to admire her work. Tang and I exchanged a glance. Even a blackout could not slow her down.
organize:0.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林决定____手电筒和蜡烛，把它们整齐摆放在柜台旁。
organize:0.hook: One torch in her neat row was somehow already empty.
organize:0.line: Let me *organize* these torches before the next outage.

pattern:0.en: I noticed a strange *pattern* on the wall — small circles of light dancing in a slow loop. Tang explained it was the candle flame reflected through an old glass jar left on the shelf. We all watched for a moment. The store felt almost magical until the jar tipped and Tang caught it just in time.
pattern:0.cnHint: 我发现墙上有奇怪的光____，原来是烛光透过玻璃瓶折射出来的。
pattern:0.hook: Tang's hand was shaking long after he set the jar down.
pattern:0.line: Look at that *pattern* on the wall — beautiful, right?

transform:0.en: The power cut at midnight. I lit every candle we sold and placed them along the shelves. The soft glow seemed to *transform* the store into something out of an old painting — warm gold on every tin and bottle. A woman I had never seen before stepped in, looked around slowly, and smiled as if she had been here a thousand times.
transform:0.cnHint: 停电后，烛光把便利店____成了一幅温暖的画，一位陌生女士走了进来。
transform:0.hook: She went straight to the back shelf without looking at the signs.
transform:0.line: 'A little candlelight can *transform* even a sad night, don't you think?'

additional:0.en: Tang found two boxes of candles under the counter and lit them all. I asked if we should save some for later. He shook his head and pulled out an *additional* box from a bag he had brought from home. 'I always keep a spare,' he said, looking almost too proud of himself.
additional:0.cnHint: 停电时，阿糖拿出了____的蜡烛，说自己早有准备。
additional:0.hook: But his face fell when he checked what else was in the bag.
additional:0.line: 'I brought an *additional* box — Tang is always ready for trouble.'

journal:0.en: With no screens working, an old man sat at the corner stool and opened a small notebook. 'My power *journal*,' he said, tapping it. Every page listed what he had done during each past blackout — dates, candles used, snacks eaten. He had forty-three entries. I counted while he ordered warm tea.
journal:0.cnHint: 停电夜里，一位老先生拿出专门记录停电经历的____。
journal:0.hook: Entry forty-four had tonight's date already written at the top.
journal:0.line: 'I call this my power *journal* — forty-three blackouts and counting.'

understanding:0.en: Lin came in from the store across the street, carrying her own candles. I expected some argument over customers. Instead she set the candles on our counter without a word. We stood in the warm dark for a while, and a quiet *understanding* passed between us — on a night like this, the street only had one store.
understanding:0.cnHint: 停电之夜，隔壁咖啡店的林来帮忙，我们之间产生了一种无声的____。
understanding:0.hook: Before she left, she wrote something on a receipt and slid it across the counter.
understanding:0.line: 'No need to talk — I think we have an *understanding* tonight, yes?'

citizen:0.en: A man in a yellow rain jacket came in and bought six bottles of water, then asked if he could leave them by the door for anyone who needed them. 'Just a small thing,' he said. Tang whispered to me that the man did this every blackout — a quiet *citizen* of this corner who showed up whenever the lights went out.
citizen:0.cnHint: 停电时，一位热心的街区____来到店里，把水留给有需要的人。
citizen:0.hook: The man had already gone before I thought to ask his name.
citizen:0.line: 'A good *citizen* of this street looks after the people around them.'

contrast:0.en: Outside, the whole block was dark. Inside, our candles made the shelves glow orange and yellow. The *contrast* was sharp — step through our door and the night changed completely. A teenage boy stopped on the pavement, stared in, and then slowly pushed the door open as if entering somewhere magical.
contrast:0.cnHint: 店外漆黑一片，店内烛光摇曳，这种____吸引了一个路过的少年。
contrast:0.hook: He asked, very quietly, if he could just stand inside for a while.
contrast:0.line: 'Look at that *contrast* — pure dark outside, pure warmth in here.'

establish:0.en: By two in the morning Tang had moved a small table near the door and set out hot water and cups. Nobody asked him to. He just did it, and people started gathering around it as if it had always been there. In one quiet hour he managed to *establish* a kind of neighbourhood meeting point that the store had never had before.
establish:0.cnHint: 停电夜里，阿糖自发____了一个让街坊聚集取暖的小角落。
establish:0.hook: One of the regulars stayed until sunrise and nobody minded at all.
establish:0.line: 'Let's *establish* one rule tonight: everyone gets a free cup of hot water.'

difficulty:1.en: The power cut hit our street just after midnight. I grabbed a torch and checked the door — still locked, good. The *difficulty* was that half our electronic price tags had gone dark, so customers could not tell what anything cost. I wrote prices on paper by torchlight, one sticky note at a time.
difficulty:1.cnHint: 停电后，店员在手电筒光下用纸条标价，克服了一个小小的____。
difficulty:1.hook: Then a customer outside pressed her face against the glass and mouthed something urgent.
difficulty:1.line: 'The real *difficulty* is explaining to sixty customers why the register won't open.'

full:1.en: The street was *full* of people the moment the lights went out. They spilled off the pavement, phones raised like little moons, faces lit from below. I stood in the shop doorway and counted at least thirty neighbours I had never seen before. A power cut, it turns out, is the fastest way to meet everyone on the block.
full:1.cnHint: 停电那一刻，街道上____是人，邻居们纷纷走出家门。
full:1.hook: One of them was staring not at the dark sky but directly at our store window.
full:1.line: 'The street is *full* of people — should we open the side door for them?'

range:1.en: Tang appeared from the back room carrying a *range* of candles — tall white ones, short red ones, little tea-lights in silver cups. She lined them up along the counter without a word, struck a match, and suddenly the whole shop glowed orange. Outside, a small crowd pressed against the glass and pointed.
range:1.cnHint: 阿糖从后屋拿出各种各样的蜡烛，点亮了整间小店，吸引了一____好奇的路人。
range:1.hook: The last candle she lit had a label none of us could read in the dim light.
range:1.line: 'We keep a *range* of candles for exactly this kind of night — lucky, right?'

region:1.en: The Manager called from home to say the whole *region* around the old bridge had lost power — not just our street. He told me to keep the fridge doors shut, sell only shelf goods, and stay calm. I could hear him eating noodles while he talked, which somehow made his advice easier to follow.
region:1.cnHint: 店长电话说，整个____都停电了，叮嘱店员沉着应对。
region:1.hook: He then mentioned one regular customer I should watch out for tonight.
region:1.line: 'This *region* loses power every summer — you will get used to it, trust me.'

material:1.en: A student crouched outside under our awning, spreading damp notes across the pavement. She told me the *material* for her exam tomorrow was soaked when she cycled through a puddle, and she needed light to let it dry. I moved a candle to the window ledge closest to her and said nothing else.
material:1.cnHint: 一位女生把被雨水打湿的复习____摊在店外借光晾干。
material:1.hook: An hour later she was still there, and she was no longer alone.
material:1.line: 'All my study *material* is wet — can I borrow your window light for a while?'

pressure:1.en: The queue at our counter grew long and impatient. I could feel the *pressure* rising like water — everyone wanted cold drinks, and the fridge was off. I handed out room-temperature juice, smiled at each person, and kept moving. By the time I reached the last customer the mood had softened completely.
pressure:1.cnHint: 停电后队伍越来越长，店员感受到巨大的____，但一直微笑着应对。
pressure:1.hook: The last person in the queue slid a folded note across the counter without a word.
pressure:1.line: 'Don't let the *pressure* get to you — you are doing great for a first night.'

thus:1.en: The traffic lights at the corner were dark, and cars had stopped moving. Drivers got out, chatted across bonnets, shared cigarettes. A small dog escaped from one car and ran straight into our shop. Its owner followed, *thus* becoming our first customer of the night who paid in coins shaken from a cup holder.
thus:1.cnHint: 红绿灯停了，一只小狗跑进了店里，它的主人____成了当晚第一位顾客。
thus:1.hook: The dog sat down behind the counter and refused to leave with its owner.
thus:1.line: 'My dog ran in, and I followed — I am *thus* forced to buy something, I suppose.'

tool:1.en: Lin arrived from the store two blocks away carrying a *tool* bag and a big grin. He said his shop had a generator and offered to lend us an extension lead. I was not sure if this was kindness or a chance to look at our stock. Either way, the lights came back on in our freezer, and the ice cream was saved.
tool:1.cnHint: 竞争对手隔壁咖啡店的林带着____过来帮忙，顺便也打量了一番我们的店。
tool:1.hook: Before he left, Lin took a very long look at our new shelf of imported snacks.
tool:1.line: 'Every good shopkeeper keeps one *tool* for emergencies — tonight it is this cable.'

responsibility:1.en: The street outside the store went dark all at once. Every light on the block died. The Manager stepped out first, looking up and down the quiet road. 'Someone has to check the fuse box,' he said. 'That *responsibility* falls on the person who knows this building best.' He looked right at me.
responsibility:1.cnHint: 停电了，店长说处理保险丝盒是____最清楚这栋楼的人的。
responsibility:1.hook: He was already walking back inside, keys in hand.
responsibility:1.line: 'That *responsibility* falls on the person who knows this building best.'

soon:1.en: Outside, the whole street sat in thick darkness. I stood at the door watching neighbours open their windows and look out. A few candles appeared on windowsills, one by one, like small orange stars. I thought power would return *soon*, but the silence just grew deeper and the candles kept multiplying.
soon:1.cnHint: 街道一片漆黑，我以为停电____会结束，但蜡烛却越来越多。
soon:1.hook: Then one window went dark again, very suddenly.
soon:1.line: 'Don't worry, the power will come back *soon*.'

center:1.en: A large power box stood at the *center* of the crossroads, its little red warning light now completely dead. Tang walked up to it with a torch and tapped the metal cover twice. Neighbours gathered in a loose circle around her, their faces pale in the torchlight, all waiting for some kind of answer.
center:1.cnHint: 路口____的配电箱红灯熄灭了，唐拿着手电筒走上前查看。
center:1.hook: Tang's torch flickered once, then went out too.
center:1.line: 'The box at the *center* of the crossroads is completely dead.'

arrive:1.en: I called the power company from the store's landline. A calm voice told me a repair team would *arrive* within the hour. I relayed the news through the open doorway to the small crowd outside. A few people nodded. One old man simply sat down on the kerb and opened a bag of snacks, perfectly content to wait.
arrive:1.cnHint: 我打电话给电力公司，对方说维修人员会____，我把消息告诉了门外的街坊。
arrive:1.hook: The old man offered me a snack without saying a word.
arrive:1.line: 'The repair team will *arrive* within the hour, everyone.'

boost:1.en: Tang found a box of emergency candles under the counter and set them along the store window ledge. The warm glow gave the whole street a small *boost* of calm — people stopped shouting across balconies and started drifting toward the light instead, the way moths do on an ordinary summer night.
boost:1.cnHint: 唐摆出应急蜡烛，那点温暖的光给街上的气氛带来了小小的____。
boost:1.hook: Among the drifting neighbours was someone none of us recognised.
boost:1.line: 'A few candles can give everyone a real *boost* of calm.'

conflict:1.en: Lin arrived from the competing store down the road carrying a crate of bottled water to share. Two neighbours immediately began to argue — one said Lin was only doing it for attention, the other said that was unfair. Their voices started to *conflict* sharply in the dark, rising above the sound of the distant repair van.
conflict:1.cnHint: 两位街坊对林的动机看法不同，言辞开始激烈____起来。
conflict:1.hook: Lin said nothing, just set the crate down and smiled.
conflict:1.line: 'Our views *conflict*, but let's not argue in the dark.'

demand:1.en: A woman in a bright yellow coat pushed to the front of the small crowd and *demanded* to know exactly when the lights would return. Her voice was sharp and loud. The Manager answered her politely, twice. She asked a third time anyway. Behind her, the old man with the snacks looked up at the sky, unbothered.
demand:1.cnHint: 一位穿黄色外套的女士强烈____知道何时来电，店长礼貌地回答了两次。
demand:1.hook: The old man quietly offered her a snack too.
demand:1.line: 'I *demand* to know exactly when the power is coming back.'

emotion:1.en: When the street lights finally buzzed back on, a small cheer went up from the neighbours still gathered outside. I felt a sudden rush of *emotion* — not about the electricity, but about the sight of all these strangers standing together in the warm light, eating the old man's snacks and laughing at nothing in particular.
emotion:1.cnHint: 灯光亮起时，我心里涌上一股____，不是因为来电，而是因为眼前这幅温暖的景象。
emotion:1.hook: Then I noticed Lin was already gone.
emotion:1.line: 'I don't know why, but I'm full of *emotion* right now.'

international:1.en: The power cut hit at midnight. Outside, the street went dark and silent. A traveller rushed in with a large backpack, speaking fast in three languages. She spread an *international* flight map on the counter, pointing at a city I had never heard of. 'My phone is dead,' she said. 'Can I charge it here?'
international:1.cnHint: 一位手持____航班地图的旅行者在停电时冲进店里，请求给手机充电。
international:1.hook: Her map showed a city the Manager said had not existed for ten years.
international:1.line: 'This is an *international* flight — I cannot miss it, please help me!'

manage:1.en: Every torch in the store sold out in three minutes. I could not find the fuse box, the radio was dead, and six customers were all talking at once. Somehow I *managed* to keep everyone calm by handing out free candy and telling bad jokes in the dark. Tang watched from the corner, looking impressed.
manage:1.cnHint: 停电时店里乱成一团，叙述者设法____让顾客们冷静下来。
manage:1.hook: Tang said afterwards that the Manager had been testing me all along.
manage:1.line: 'I don't know how you *managed* that — I would have just hidden in the back.'

outside:1.en: The blackout swallowed the whole block. I stepped to the door and looked at the *outside*: every lamppost was off, and the road was a river of phone-torch lights as people felt their way home. One old man moved against the flow, walking calmly toward the store, carrying a candle in a glass jar.
outside:1.cnHint: 停电后，叙述者望向____，看到街上满是手机灯光，还有一位拿着蜡烛的老人走来。
outside:1.hook: The old man said the candle had once belonged to someone who never came back for it.
outside:1.line: 'The *outside* is pitch black — do you have any torches left?'

fun:1.en: Tang lit three candles on the counter and put on a shadow-puppet show using her hands and a torch. Customers gathered around, laughing at her rabbit and dragon shapes on the wall. 'Blackouts can be *fun*,' she said, grinning. A little boy in pyjamas clapped the loudest. His mother looked grateful and a little surprised.
fun:1.cnHint: 停电中，阿糖用手影表演给大家带来了____，一个穿睡衣的小男孩笑得最开心。
fun:1.hook: The little boy whispered something to Tang that made her face go very still.
fun:1.line: 'Come on, a little *fun* never hurt anyone — stop looking so worried!'

reality:1.en: Lin from the store across the street walked in holding a battery lamp. She had always seemed cold to me, but in the candlelight she looked just tired. 'In *reality*,' she said quietly, 'I hate the dark. Always have.' She sat on the step and did not say anything else for a while. I made her a cup of hot instant soup.
reality:1.cnHint: 平时冷淡的隔壁咖啡店的林在停电时走进店里，说出了____中自己其实很怕黑。
reality:1.hook: Lin left without her lamp, and I am still not sure if that was an accident.
reality:1.line: 'In *reality*, I only came over because I did not want to be alone in the dark.'

beyond:1.en: The blackout spread *beyond* our street, reaching all the way to the river, according to a cyclist who stopped for water. He said the whole district was out and repair crews were hours away. Then he bought every energy bar on the shelf, nodded once, and rode off into the dark like he had somewhere important to be.
beyond:1.cnHint: 一位骑车人告诉叙述者，这次停电范围____了我们这条街，延伸到了很远的地方。
beyond:1.hook: The cyclist left a handwritten note under his money that none of us could read.
beyond:1.line: 'The blackout goes *beyond* this block — the whole district is dark tonight.'

completely:1.en: By two in the morning the store was *completely* full. People sat on the floor between the shelves, sharing snacks and telling stories. I had not planned any of this. The Manager arrived at half past two, stopped in the doorway, and stared. I waited for him to be angry. He was not angry.
completely:1.cnHint: 凌晨两点，店里____坐满了避暗的顾客，店长到来时的反应出乎叙述者意料。
completely:1.hook: The Manager took out his phone and made a call he did not explain to anyone.
completely:1.line: 'The power is *completely* out on this side of town — can we stay a little while?'

advise:1.en: A woman in a nurse's uniform asked me what snacks were good for staying awake on a long shift. I did not really know, but I did my best. 'I *advise* the salted nuts,' I said, trying to sound confident. She studied me for a moment, then bought the nuts and a small chocolate bar. 'Good choice,' she said. 'For you, I mean.'
advise:1.cnHint: 一位护士请叙述者____她选择适合熬夜的零食，叙述者的回答得到了意外的评价。
advise:1.hook: The nurse comes in every Thursday night, but she has never once bought the nuts again.
advise:1.line: 'I *advise* you to take the salted nuts — they really help you stay awake.'

describe:1.en: The street outside went dark all at once. A woman knocked on our glass door and asked if she could wait inside. 'Of course,' I said. She stood by the window, watching the blackout spread block by block. I asked her to *describe* what she saw, thinking it might calm her. She smiled and said every dark street looked like a secret.
describe:1.cnHint: 停电时，一位女士进店避暗，她用____形容窗外的街道。
describe:1.hook: She knew exactly which block would lose power last.
describe:1.line: 'Can you *describe* the street from your side? I can only see shadows.'

rest:1.en: Tang and I dragged two plastic chairs to the doorway when the power cut out. We had nothing to do — the register was dark, the fridge hummed once and stopped. Tang called it a forced *rest*. I called it the longest ten minutes of my shift. Then a man in slippers shuffled up, carrying a candle in a paper cup.
rest:1.cnHint: 停电让阿糖和我被迫____，一位穿拖鞋的男人随后出现了。
rest:1.hook: The man said the candle was not really his to give.
rest:1.line: 'Think of it as a *rest*. The store needed one anyway.'

employer:1.en: Lin showed up outside during the blackout, leaning against the wall of the store across the street. I had not seen her this close before. She told me her *employer* had locked up early and sent everyone home. She did not sound upset — just tired. She looked at our dark store and laughed softly.
employer:1.cnHint: 停电后，隔壁咖啡店的林出现在街角，说她的____提前关门让她回家了。
employer:1.hook: Lin had a key in her pocket that did not match any lock nearby.
employer:1.line: 'My *employer* sent us home. Funny — I walked straight here anyway.'

owner:1.en: A cat sat on the low wall outside, calm in the dark. A boy of about ten ran up and checked its collar, then looked around the empty street, worried. He told me he was looking for the *owner*, who had stepped out just before the lights went off. I held my torch up so he could read the tag better.
owner:1.cnHint: 停电后，一个男孩在街边寻找那只猫的____。
owner:1.hook: The name on the collar matched no one on this street.
owner:1.line: 'The *owner* was right here a minute ago — did you see anyone leave?'

gender:1.en: Two students came in from the dark street to charge their phones on our backup socket. They were filling out a form by torchlight and asked me how to answer a question about *gender* in English. I spelled it out letter by letter. They thanked me, finished the form, and then just sat quietly, watching the street.
gender:1.cnHint: 两位学生借用备用电源，顺便问我一个表格上关于____的英文词怎么写。
gender:1.hook: The form they were filling out was due in three hours.
gender:1.line: 'We need the English word for 性别 — is it really spelled *gender*?'

website:1.en: The power was out but the Manager had a printed list taped behind the counter — every supplier's phone number. 'No *website* works now,' he said, tapping the paper proudly. I had never thought a printed list could feel so useful. He called the third number, got an answer, and nodded slowly at whatever he heard.
website:1.cnHint: 停电时，店长拿出纸质联系表，说现在任何____都没法用了。
website:1.hook: Whatever he heard on that call made him unlock the back room.
website:1.line: 'Every *website* is down. Good thing I never threw this list away.'

emotional:1.en: An old man stopped under our awning to get out of the wind. He said blackouts always made him *emotional* — they reminded him of a small village and a grandmother who kept oil lamps just in case. He did not seem sad, exactly. More like someone handling a snow globe, very gently. He bought one box of matches and left.
emotional:1.cnHint: 一位老人说停电总让他感到____，因为会想起小时候的事。
emotional:1.hook: He had bought matches here every week for a year.
emotional:1.line: 'I get a little *emotional* in the dark — old habits from a different life.'

training:1.en: Tang handled the whole blackout without any notes or panic. Torches, safety check, customer log — done in two minutes. I asked if there was a guide somewhere. He said there was no book, just *training* the Manager gave him last winter, one slow night at a time. Then he handed me a torch and told me my turn starts now.
training:1.cnHint: 阿糖镇定地应对停电，说这都是店长给他的____，而现在轮到我了。
training:1.hook: The Manager was watching us from the back door the whole time.
training:1.line: 'It is all from *training*. The Manager does not believe in written rules.'

consume:1.en: The power went out at midnight. I lit a candle on the counter and watched it *consume* the darkness inch by inch, turning shadow into a warm orange glow. Outside, the street was totally black. Then a figure appeared at the glass door, pressing their face against it with wide, hopeful eyes.
consume:1.cnHint: 停电后我点起蜡烛，它____着黑暗，这时门外出现了一个人影。
consume:1.hook: The figure outside mouthed a single word I could not read.
consume:1.line: 'A candle can *consume* the dark, but not the cold — do you sell blankets?'

desire:1.en: During the blackout, I sorted the snack shelf by candlelight. An old man knocked softly and stepped in, blinking. He walked straight past the chips and the drinks and stopped at the last warm meat bun under the glass. His face showed a quiet *desire* so honest it made me smile. I bagged it for him without a word.
desire:1.cnHint: 停电夜里，一位老人走进来，眼神中流露出对那个肉包子深深的____。
desire:1.hook: He paid, then asked if he could sit a while — just until the lights came back.
desire:1.line: 'I don't *desire* much at my age — just one warm bun and a little light.'

meal:1.en: The power cut hit just as Tang finished heating a boxed rice on the back burner. She carried it to the counter and sat beside me, and we shared that simple *meal* by the glow of two phone screens propped against the register. It was quiet and a little funny and surprisingly nice. Neither of us talked much.
meal:1.cnHint: 停电时，我和阿糖就着手机屏幕的光，一起吃了一顿简单的____。
meal:1.hook: Then Tang said, very quietly, that this reminded her of someone she had not seen in years.
meal:1.line: 'A *meal* tastes better when the lights are out and someone sits with you.'

vegetable:1.en: A woman rushed in during the blackout, her bag dripping rain. She grabbed every *vegetable* left on the small fresh shelf — two bundles of green onion, a bag of spinach, one pale carrot — and stacked them on the counter like they were treasure. I scanned them by flashlight. She seemed almost relieved.
vegetable:1.cnHint: 停电夜里，一位女士冲进来，把货架上剩下的所有____都买走了。
vegetable:1.hook: Before she left she said the vegetables were not for herself, and she glanced up at the building across the street.
vegetable:1.line: 'Every *vegetable* on that shelf, please — someone upstairs needs a real dinner tonight.'

adopt:1.en: When the power died, the Manager called from home. His voice was calm. 'Just *adopt* the candle-and-flashlight rule,' he said. 'We used it in the old store twenty years ago. Customers will stay if they feel safe.' I lit every candle we had and lined them along the window. He was right — three people came in within the next ten minutes.
adopt:1.cnHint: 停电后店长打来电话，建议我____烛光应急方案，这个办法果然奏效了。
adopt:1.hook: The Manager added, almost to himself, that he missed the old store very much.
adopt:1.line: 'Just *adopt* the old candle rule — it never once let us down.'

miss:1.en: A young woman ran to the door at 1 a.m., pulling it open with both hands. She had *missed* the last bus, her phone was nearly dead, and the rain had started again. She stood inside dripping, looking around as though she still could not quite believe a lit shop existed at this hour. I handed her a paper towel without being asked.
miss:1.cnHint: 一位____错过末班车的年轻女性，在停电的雨夜跑进了便利店。
miss:1.hook: While she charged her phone she kept checking the door, as if waiting for someone who might still show up.
miss:1.line: 'I *missed* the last bus and now I have nowhere dry to wait — is that okay?'

yourself:1.en: Lin from the store up the road slipped in just after the blackout started, a small torch in hand. I raised an eyebrow. He grinned. 'Don't worry,' he said, 'I'm not here to spy on your prices. When the power is out, you stop being rivals.' He bought two coffees. 'Get one for *yourself*,' he said, sliding a cup across the counter.
yourself:1.cnHint: 停电后，竞争对手隔壁咖啡店的林走进来，还请我为____买了一杯咖啡。
yourself:1.hook: Just before Lin left, he mentioned that his store had been losing customers for reasons he could not explain.
yourself:1.line: 'Buy one for *yourself* too — rivals can share a coffee in the dark.'

century:1.en: An elderly woman came in slowly, leaning on a cane. She looked around at the candles with a soft laugh. 'Half a *century* ago,' she said, 'every shop on this street looked just like this after dark.' She bought a bar of soap and a small notebook, the same things, she told me, that she had bought every week since she moved to this street.
century:1.cnHint: 一位老奶奶看着烛光笑着说，半个____前这条街上的每家店都是这副模样。
century:1.hook: She paused at the door and said she hoped the new clerk would still be here next winter.
century:1.line: 'Half a *century* of night shifts on this street, and candles still feel like home.'

model:1.en: The street outside the store went dark the moment the power cut hit. I stepped out and found old Mr. Chen arranging tiny clay figures on a folding table. Each one was a perfect *model* of a local building — the clock tower, the noodle shop, the store itself. A small crowd gathered, phones lighting up their faces.
model:1.cnHint: 停电后，一位老人在街边摆出城市建筑的____，吸引了一小群人围观。
model:1.hook: Then someone in the crowd pointed at the last figure and whispered.
model:1.line: 'This *model* of the store — did someone ask you to make it?'

spot:1.en: During the blackout I stood at the door, watching the dark street. A bicycle wobbled past with no light. Then I managed to *spot* a familiar red scarf in the shadows — it was Tang, late for the handover, weaving between parked cars and muttering to herself.
spot:1.cnHint: 停电的黑暗中，我费力地____了骑车赶来的同事。
spot:1.hook: She was carrying something wrapped in newspaper that she refused to put down.
spot:1.line: 'Hard to *spot* anyone out here — why are all the street lights gone?'

achievement:1.en: Lin from the rival store across the street appeared under our awning, sheltering from the sudden dark. She looked up at our hand-painted sales chart still visible by torchlight. 'Not bad,' she said quietly. Reaching that number felt like a real *achievement*, even if I had only been here a week.
achievement:1.cnHint: 停电时，对面的竞争对手看到我们的销售图，承认这是一项____。
achievement:1.hook: Lin's next words, however, did not sound like a compliment at all.
achievement:1.line: 'I'll admit — that sales record is quite an *achievement* for a new branch.'

enter:1.en: The power went out just as a delivery rider tried to *enter* the store. He pushed the glass door but the automatic sensor was dead. He stood there, helmet still on, box balanced on one arm, knocking with two fingers. I hurried over and held the door open for him by hand.
enter:1.cnHint: 停电后自动门失灵，送货员无法____店里，我只好手动开门。
enter:1.hook: The box he carried was addressed to someone who had never shopped here before.
enter:1.line: 'I just need to *enter* for one second — the address says this store.'

eye:1.en: Outside, a neighbour's cat sat perfectly still on the wall opposite, watching the blackout street. Its green *eye* caught what little moonlight there was and glowed like a small lamp. A child nearby stopped crying, pointed, and laughed. For a moment the whole dark street felt a little less lonely.
eye:1.cnHint: 停电的街上，一只猫的____在月光中发光，让紧张气氛缓和了下来。
eye:1.hook: But the cat was staring past the child at something further down the street.
eye:1.line: 'Look at that *eye* — it is the only light on this whole street right now.'

shift:1.en: The blackout hit ten minutes before the end of my first night *shift*. I was counting the till when everything went dark. I found a torch under the counter — the Manager had taped a note to it: 'Always here. Always charged.' I decided I liked him a little more after that.
shift:1.cnHint: 停电发生在我第一个夜班____结束前，我在黑暗中找到了店长留下的手电筒。
shift:1.hook: The note had a second line I had not noticed at first.
shift:1.line: 'Your *shift* is not over until the lights come back on — store rule.'

agree:1.en: Lin sheltered under the awning and I stood beside her in the dark. We did not speak at first. Then she said the blackout made every store equal, and I had to *agree* — no bright signs, no advantage. She almost smiled. Outside, a dog barked somewhere and we both jumped at the same time.
agree:1.cnHint: 停电让两家店站在同一起跑线上，我不得不____竞争对手说的话。
agree:1.hook: A second later Lin's phone lit up with a message that made her expression change.
agree:1.line: 'No power, no edge — I *agree*, tonight we are just two people in the dark.'

aware:1.en: I had been so busy hunting for candles that I was not *aware* of the small crowd forming just beyond the door. By the time I looked up, at least a dozen people stood outside — neighbours, cyclists, a woman with a sleeping baby. They all seemed to expect the convenience store to fix everything.
aware:1.cnHint: 忙着找蜡烛的我没有____到门外已经聚集了一群等待帮助的邻居。
aware:1.hook: Among them stood one person who was watching me, not the store.
aware:1.line: 'Were you even *aware* that half the street has been outside for ten minutes?'

land:1.en: Outside the store, old Mr. Chen spread a hand-drawn map on the hood of a parked car. 'This *land* once had a great market,' he told me, tracing the street corner with one finger. The power was out, but his eyes were bright with memory.
land:1.cnHint: 停电的夜晚，一位老人在店外指着街角的____，讲起这里昔日的热闹。
land:1.hook: He folded the map and said one name I recognised.
land:1.line: 'This *land* used to feed half the people on this street.'

promote:1.en: Tang rushed out of the store just as the lights died. She was carrying a stack of paper flyers into the dark street, undeterred. 'Even a blackout will not stop me,' she said, pinning one to a lamp post. The flyers were meant to *promote* the store's new late-night menu.
promote:1.cnHint: 停电了，同事还跑到街上张贴海报，努力____新的深夜菜单。
promote:1.hook: One flyer blew off and landed at a stranger's feet.
promote:1.line: 'We *promote* the new menu tonight, blackout or not.'

purchase:1.en: A woman in a yellow raincoat stood under the dead street light, holding a small paper bag close to her chest. She said her *purchase* from earlier in the evening — a single candle — had turned out to be exactly what her whole building needed tonight.
purchase:1.cnHint: 一位女士庆幸自己之前的____派上了大用场，那根蜡烛点亮了整栋楼。
purchase:1.hook: She smiled, then asked if we had any more candles left.
purchase:1.line: 'That *purchase* was the luckiest thing I did today.'

rely:1.en: The street was nearly black. A young delivery rider stopped his bicycle by the store window, using the faint glow of his phone to read an address. 'Normally I *rely* on the street lamps,' he said with a tired laugh, squinting at his screen in the warm dark.
rely:1.cnHint: 停电后，一个送餐骑手站在店外说，他平时都____路灯来认路。
rely:1.hook: His phone battery showed three percent.
rely:1.line: 'I *rely* on those lamps every single night, you know.'

connect:1.en: I ran an extension cord from the store's back-up socket out to the pavement, where a small group of neighbours had gathered. The cord was just long enough to *connect* a single lamp to the outlet. Weak orange light spilled onto the street, and people moved toward it like moths.
connect:1.cnHint: 我把延长线拉到街上，用它____备用电源和一盏灯，邻居们纷纷围拢过来。
connect:1.hook: Among the faces in the lamplight, I saw one I did not expect.
connect:1.line: 'Can you *connect* that lamp a little closer to the bench?'

indicate:1.en: Lin appeared from around the corner, flashlight in hand, pointing at the electricity box on the wall. 'The red light still on there,' she said, 'might *indicate* that only part of the street lost power.' She sounded calm, almost pleased, as if she had been waiting for exactly this kind of problem.
indicate:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林指着墙上的电箱，说那盏红灯可能____停电的范围并不像大家以为的那么大。
indicate:1.hook: She then pulled out a small notebook and began writing.
indicate:1.line: 'That red light could *indicate* power is still on next block.'

period:1.en: The Manager stood in the store doorway, arms folded, watching the dark street with a patient expression. 'Every old neighbourhood goes through a *period* like this,' he said quietly, more to himself than to me. 'No lights, people outside, everyone suddenly remembering they have neighbours.'
period:1.cnHint: 店长站在门口，说每个老街区都会经历这样一段____，停电反而让邻里关系更近了。
period:1.hook: Then he went inside and came back with a tray of free coffee cups.
period:1.line: 'This *period* will pass, but the stories will stay.'

picture:1.en: A little girl sat on the steps of the building across the street, drawing by the light of a candle her mother held steady. I crossed over to look: it was a *picture* of our store, its sign dark but its window glowing faintly from somewhere inside. She had even drawn me standing in the doorway.
picture:1.cnHint: 街对面，一个小女孩借着烛光画了一幅____，画的正是停电中的便利店和站在门口的我。
picture:1.hook: She held it up and asked if she could give it to the Manager.
picture:1.line: 'I drew a *picture* of your store because it looks like a star tonight.'

management:1.en: The power cut hit at midnight. Every candle in the store was lit within two minutes. I looked around at the neat rows of goods still visible by soft flame and realised the *management* of this little shop was better than I had given it credit for. Even the emergency torch had fresh batteries.
management:1.cnHint: 停电后，店里的____让我刮目相看——每根蜡烛都有备份，手电筒也有新电池。
management:1.hook: Then I noticed one shelf had been quietly emptied while the lights were out.
management:1.line: 'Good *management* means being ready before the crisis, not during it,' the Manager said calmly.

perfect:1.en: Outside, the street was completely dark except for our window glowing with candle light. A couple walking past stopped and stared. One of them said it looked like a *perfect* little painting. I waved. They waved back and then kept walking, but slowly, as if they did not want the picture to end.
perfect:1.cnHint: 停电的街道上，我们小店的烛光在路人眼中成了一幅____的画面。
perfect:1.hook: The second person glanced back one more time before the darkness swallowed them.
perfect:1.line: 'It looks *perfect* from out here,' the taller one said softly to their friend.

along:1.en: I stepped outside to check the street. The whole block was dark. A cat walked *along* the centre of the road, calm and unhurried, as if it owned the night. A man with a small lantern followed a few metres behind, also unhurried. Neither of them seemed to think the blackout was any trouble at all.
along:1.cnHint: 停电后我走到门外，看见一只猫____街道中央散步，身后还跟着一个提灯笼的人。
along:1.hook: The man with the lantern paused right in front of our door and looked up at the sign.
along:1.line: 'I just walked *along* the whole street and you are the only ones still open,' he said.

harm:1.en: A small boy stood at the door, holding a broken torch. He looked worried. I told him a power cut could not *harm* the store and that we had plenty of candles left to sell. His face relaxed at once. He picked out one yellow candle very carefully, paid with exact coins, and ran back into the dark street.
harm:1.cnHint: 一个小男孩担心停电会____小店，我安慰他之后，他认真挑了一根蜡烛跑回了夜色中。
harm:1.hook: I never saw which building he ran into, but a warm light appeared in a high window shortly after.
harm:1.line: 'Will the dark *harm* your shop?' he asked, eyes wide at the door.

increasingly:1.en: As the blackout stretched on, the candle-lit store became *increasingly* busy. People came in not just to buy things but to stand in the warm light for a while. By one in the morning the little space felt almost like a village square. Tang leaned over and whispered that this never happened on normal nights.
increasingly:1.cnHint: 随着停电时间延长，小店变得____热闹，人们来这里不只是买东西，更像是聚在村头一样取暖。
increasingly:1.hook: One woman in the corner had not bought anything and showed no sign of leaving.
increasingly:1.line: 'It gets *increasingly* strange,' Tang whispered, 'the longer the lights stay off.'

opinion:1.en: Tang and I disagreed about the candles. I thought we should save half for the store. Tang's *opinion* was that we should sell every last one while people needed them and just sit in the dark ourselves afterward. We argued in low voices across the counter while a line of customers waited, each one quietly amused.
opinion:1.cnHint: 停电时，我和阿糖为蜡烛该留着还是全卖掉起了争论，客人们在一旁默默看戏。
opinion:1.hook: The last customer in line was already holding the exact number of candles we had been arguing about.
opinion:1.line: 'My *opinion* is that customers come first, even in the dark,' Tang said firmly.

previous:1.en: The Manager arrived at the store just after one in the morning, calm and unsurprised. She said a blackout had hit this same street two winters ago. Her *previous* experience meant she had kept a full box of candles and a gas burner in the back room ever since. She put the burner on the counter and made hot water for everyone.
previous:1.cnHint: 店长来了，她说____的停电经历让她早就在库房备好了蜡烛和燃气炉。
previous:1.hook: She mentioned, almost too quietly to hear, that the last blackout had lasted three days.
previous:1.line: 'My *previous* experience taught me to always keep a spare box,' the Manager said, setting down the candles.

aim:1.en: Lin appeared at the door around two, carrying a small battery lamp. I had heard Lin ran the shop on the next block and I half-expected trouble. But Lin just set the lamp on our counter without a word. The *aim*, Lin said after a pause, was simply to help out a neighbour. I did not know what to say, so I said thank you.
aim:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林提着一盏电池灯来到门口，说____只是想帮帮邻居，让我一时语塞。
aim:1.hook: Lin left without taking any payment, but paused once at the corner and looked back.
aim:1.line: 'The *aim* was never to compete tonight,' Lin said quietly, 'just to help.'

meanwhile:1.en: The power went out at midnight. I lit two candles behind the counter and waited. Outside, the whole street went dark and quiet. *Meanwhile*, Tang was somewhere in the back room, calmly counting the canned goods by phone-light, humming a little tune as if nothing unusual had happened at all.
meanwhile:1.cnHint: 停电后，我在柜台点蜡烛，____唐在后室借手机灯光清点库存。
meanwhile:1.hook: Then Tang called out something odd about a can with no label.
meanwhile:1.line: '*Meanwhile*, I found twelve cans back here that nobody can identify.'

damage:1.en: When the lights came back on, I walked the whole store checking shelves. One freezer door had been left open in the dark for an hour. The ice cream inside was soft and weeping. The Manager arrived at six, looked at the freezer, and quietly said the *damage* was worse than last month's broken window.
damage:1.cnHint: 来电后店长查看冰柜，发现这次的____比上个月那扇破窗还要严重。
damage:1.hook: He then pulled out a small notebook and added something to a very long list.
damage:1.line: 'The *damage* to the freezer stock alone will cost us three days of profit.'

police:1.en: A loud knock came at the glass door around two in the morning. I jumped. It was only an officer doing rounds, uniform dark against the unlit street outside. She asked for a warm cup of instant noodles and paid in exact change. *Police* work on quiet nights, she said, was mostly hunger and waiting.
police:1.cnHint: 凌晨两点一位女警敲门，说____在平静的夜里值班主要就是饿和等。
police:1.hook: She left a small card on the counter without explaining why.
police:1.line: '*Police* work sounds exciting, but mostly you just wait and eat noodles.'

race:1.en: Lin arrived breathless, holding a big torch and a bag of batteries. He said the shop across the road had lost power too, so every customer on the street would come to whoever opened first. 'It is a *race*,' he said, grinning, already stacking the batteries on the counter before I could even say hello.
race:1.cnHint: 林气喘吁吁地跑来说，谁先开门谁就赢得这场____，并开始摆电池。
race:1.hook: But Lin had forgotten that our door had been open the entire time.
race:1.line: 'This is a *race*, and we are already winning — look at the line outside!'

medical:1.en: A young man came in shaking, holding his left hand wrapped in a cloth. He said he had cut it on something in the dark outside. I found our first-aid box under the counter. Tang, calm as ever, said his father had been a *medical* worker and had taught him how to clean a small cut properly.
medical:1.cnHint: 一个年轻人手受伤了，唐说他父亲是____工作者，知道如何正确处理小伤口。
medical:1.hook: The young man smiled and asked if Tang came to the store every night.
medical:1.line: 'My father was a *medical* worker, so cleaning cuts is easy for me.'

wear:1.en: The Manager had walked over in the dark without a torch and arrived with muddy shoes. He stood at the door looking tired, a coat thrown over his pyjamas. That kind of *wear* on a person's face — the mix of worry and sleepiness — told me he had been awake since the first power cut hours ago.
wear:1.cnHint: 店长深夜赶来，脸上那种____让我知道他从第一次停电起就没睡着。
wear:1.hook: He stared at the melted ice cream and let out one very long, slow breath.
wear:1.line: 'You can see the *wear* on his face — he has not slept since midnight.'

climate:1.en: Two students sat on the step outside, sharing a bag of crackers and talking loudly. One said the summer blackouts were getting worse every year. The other nodded and said the *climate* in this city had shifted — hotter summers, stranger storms, longer nights without power. I listened through the open door and felt they were probably right.
climate:1.cnHint: 两个学生在门口聊天，说这座城市的____已经改变，停电会越来越频繁。
climate:1.hook: One of them then looked up and asked me how old the store's wiring was.
climate:1.line: 'The *climate* here has really changed — summers are hotter and blackouts are longer.'

head:1.en: Tang appeared from the back room holding a torch above his *head* like a tiny beacon. He had found the store's emergency light, fixed the loose wire with a rubber band, and got it working. The whole shop glowed softly yellow. A small cheer came from the two students still sitting on the front step outside.
head:1.cnHint: 唐高举手电筒走出来，原来他已经修好了应急灯，____上方光芒像灯塔一样。
head:1.hook: He then said he had also found something strange taped behind the emergency light.
head:1.line: 'I held the torch above my *head* so I could see the wire clearly.'

relate:1.en: The street outside went dark all at once. A woman stood under our one working lamp, trying to *relate* the whole story to her phone — something about a cat, a ladder, and a lost key. I caught only pieces, but every piece was better than the last. She spoke fast, laughed faster, and ended with a long sigh.
relate:1.cnHint: 停电后，一位女士站在店门口的灯下，向手机里的人____着一段离奇的经历。
relate:1.hook: She hung up, turned to me, and said the story was not even the strange part.
relate:1.line: 'Let me *relate* what just happened — you will not believe it.'

attitude:1.en: The power cut at midnight. A man in a long coat walked up to our door, tried the handle, and found it locked from outside by the wind. His *attitude* stayed perfectly calm — he simply folded his arms, tilted his head, and waited as if he had all the time in the world. I rushed over and pushed the door open, a little embarrassed.
attitude:1.cnHint: 停电那晚，一个男人被风关在门外，他的____却出奇地从容淡定。
attitude:1.hook: He stepped inside, smiled, and said he had been locked out of stranger places.
attitude:1.line: 'My *attitude* toward locked doors is simple — just wait and they open.'

fill:1.en: Candles lined the counter. Tang found three in the back room and lit them one by one. The soft light seemed to *fill* every corner of the store with something warmer than electricity ever managed. A tired delivery worker stepped in, looked around, and let out a long, slow breath, as if the whole night had been leading him here.
fill:1.cnHint: 停电时，蜡烛的光____了小店的每个角落，一名外卖员走进来后长舒了一口气。
fill:1.hook: He set down his bag and said he had one more stop — but maybe not yet.
fill:1.line: 'These candles *fill* the whole place with a good feeling, you know?'

ignore:1.en: Outside, the street lamps were all out. A teenager sat on the low wall across from us, staring at a dark phone screen. Passing neighbours called to her, but she seemed to *ignore* every single one, as still as a statue. Then our candle in the window flickered, and her head turned toward it like a needle finding north.
ignore:1.cnHint: 停电后，街对面有个少女____了所有路过的邻居，直到窗里的烛光吸引了她的注意。
ignore:1.hook: She crossed the street slowly and asked if we sold batteries — for something she would not name.
ignore:1.line: 'I did not mean to *ignore* everyone — I was just thinking very hard.'

necessary:1.en: The whole block lost power just after one. The Manager had told me last week that a torch behind the counter was *necessary* for exactly this kind of night. I had nodded and then forgotten completely. Standing in the dark, I found it at last — taped to the wall, right where it always was, judging me silently.
necessary:1.cnHint: 停电那晚，店长早就说过手电筒是____的，而我却险些忘了它在哪里。
necessary:1.hook: Behind me, a quiet voice asked if I needed help — and I had not heard anyone come in.
necessary:1.line: 'The Manager said a torch is *necessary* — now I finally understand why.'

definitely:1.en: Lin appeared at the glass door at half past one, face lit blue by a phone torch. She said the store across the road had closed early, so ours was *definitely* the last light on the whole street. She bought two candles, a box of crackers, and one small notebook, and she arranged everything in her bag with great care.
definitely:1.cnHint: 停电后，隔壁咖啡店的林说我们的店____是整条街最后一盏灯，然后仔细地买了几样东西。
definitely:1.hook: She paused at the door and asked if the notebook came with any sort of promise.
definitely:1.line: 'Your store is *definitely* the brightest thing on this street right now.'

forget:1.en: The power stayed off for two hours. In that time I served six customers by candlelight and began to *forget* what the usual hum of the fridges even sounded like. An old man bought a single pear, held it up to the candle to check its colour, nodded with approval, and placed the exact coins on the counter without a word.
forget:1.cnHint: 停电持续了两小时，我渐渐____了冰柜平时的嗡嗡声，一位老人举着梨子借烛光查看成色。
forget:1.hook: He left, then came back thirty seconds later to leave one extra coin he said he owed from last Tuesday.
forget:1.line: 'Do not *forget* — a good pear always shows its colour in honest light.'

particularly:1.en: The street outside was *particularly* quiet after the power went out — no hum, no buzz, no distant signs. Just wind, and the sound of my own feet on the tile. A woman in a yellow raincoat stopped outside, read our handwritten sign saying we were open, and smiled so wide I could see it clearly through the dark glass.
particularly:1.cnHint: 停电后街道____安静，一位穿黄雨衣的女士看到我们手写的营业告示后，隔着玻璃开心地笑了。
particularly:1.hook: She came in, bought nothing, and simply said she had needed to see a light.
particularly:1.line: 'Tonight feels *particularly* quiet — I am glad your light is still on.'

return:1.en: The street outside went dark all at once. Every lamp on the block died, and the store's backup light clicked on with a soft buzz. I stepped to the door and looked out. Somewhere down the road, a figure was making the slow *return* walk home, phone torch swinging like a little lantern in the black.
return:1.cnHint: 停电后街道一片黑暗，一个人提着手机灯____走回家。
return:1.hook: The figure stopped, turned, and stared straight at the store.
return:1.line: 'Every night I make the same *return* — past this corner, without fail.'

remove:1.en: The power cut killed our sign, and the Manager rushed out with a ladder to *remove* the dead bulb before it fell onto the pavement. He balanced up there in the dark, muttering softly to himself. A passing cyclist slowed, watched him, then quietly held the ladder steady without saying a single word.
remove:1.cnHint: 停电后店长爬梯子要____掉快掉落的灯泡，一位骑车人默默扶住了梯子。
remove:1.hook: The cyclist had been here before — the Manager clearly knew that face.
remove:1.line: 'Help me *remove* this bulb before it drops on someone, please.'

colleague:1.en: Tang was outside sweeping the step when the street went black. She called in to me: 'Hey, new one — torch is under the counter.' I found it, ran it out to her, and for a moment we stood side by side in the warm dark. It felt good to have a *colleague* who already knew where everything was.
colleague:1.cnHint: 停电时同事阿糖让我找手电筒，我们并肩站在黑暗中，感受着有____的踏实。
colleague:1.hook: Tang smiled, then said there was one regular I really needed to meet.
colleague:1.line: 'A good *colleague* always knows where the torch is — now you do too.'

normal:1.en: Funny thing about a blackout: people act like the world has ended. A man outside was pacing and checking his phone every five seconds. I leaned out and told him the power would be back soon. He laughed, a little embarrassed. 'Sorry,' he said. '*Normal* me would just read a book.' I wondered what had changed.
normal:1.cnHint: 停电时一个男人在外面焦急踱步，他说____的自己根本不会这么慌张。
normal:1.hook: He came back ten minutes later and left a small paper bag on the step.
normal:1.line: 'This is not *normal* for me — I am usually very calm in the dark.'

succeed:1.en: The Manager had tried twice to get the backup generator going on the pavement outside. On the third pull of the cord it finally roared to life. He punched the air. 'I knew I would *succeed*!' he called out, grinning at me through the glass door. A small crowd of neighbours actually clapped.
succeed:1.cnHint: 店长在门外拉了三次才终于让发电机启动，他高喊自己____了，邻居们鼓起掌来。
succeed:1.hook: One neighbour in the crowd had not clapped — she was watching the Manager very carefully.
succeed:1.line: 'Pull harder — if we *succeed*, the whole street gets light tonight.'

image:1.en: Without the store's bright sign, the corner looked completely different — softer, older. Tang stood in the doorway holding a candle, and the warm light caught her face just so. 'What a strange *image* we make,' she said, looking back at me. She was right: two clerks, one candle, one dark city street.
image:1.cnHint: 没有招牌灯，阿糖举着蜡烛站在门口，感叹停电创造出了多奇特的一个____。
image:1.hook: Someone across the street was photographing exactly that image.
image:1.line: 'We must look strange — what an odd *image* we make in this darkness.'

ourselves:1.en: With no power and no customers, Tang and I sat on the step outside and ate the rice balls we had each brought for our break. The street was quiet and full of stars you never normally see. 'We should lose power more often,' Tang said. 'It is nice to just enjoy *ourselves* for once.'
ourselves:1.cnHint: 停电无客时，我和阿糖坐在台阶上吃饭，难得____好好放松了一回。
ourselves:1.hook: A car slowed as it passed — the driver seemed to recognise Tang.
ourselves:1.line: 'No customers, no rush — let us just enjoy *ourselves* for a little while.'

catch:1.en: The street outside was slick after a brief rain, and I watched an old man hurrying past lose his footing on the wet pavement. He grabbed a lamp post just in time. I ran to the door. 'Are you all right?' He waved, smiling. 'Tried to *catch* myself — still got the reflexes, see!'
catch:1.cnHint: 一位老人在湿滑的路面上差点滑倒，他伸手抓住灯柱____住了自己，还笑着炫耀反应快。
catch:1.hook: He winked, then said he came here every single night for one thing.
catch:1.line: 'I always *catch* myself — forty years of walking this corner, no falls yet.'

mistake:1.en: The street outside the store went completely dark. Every lamp on the block died at once. I stepped out to check the power box and made a *mistake*: I let the door close behind me. The lock clicked. I was outside, alone, in the dark.
mistake:1.cnHint: 停电的夜晚，我出门检查配电箱，犯了一个____，被锁在门外。
mistake:1.hook: Inside, the phone was ringing — and no one could answer.
mistake:1.line: 'That was a big *mistake*, leaving your keys on the counter.'

staff:1.en: The whole block lost power just after midnight. I stood on the pavement, looking up at the dark store sign. A voice came from behind me. It was the Manager, still in his jacket. He said all *staff* were supposed to have an emergency torch. He handed me one.
staff:1.cnHint: 停电后，店长出现在街上，告诉我所有____都应该备有应急手电筒。
staff:1.hook: Then he pointed to a shadow moving slowly down the street.
staff:1.line: 'Every *staff* member gets one torch — do not lose it.'

enhance:1.en: The city repair crew set up a bright work light on the corner. It turned the dark street almost white. One worker told me the new cables would *enhance* the power supply for the whole block. For now, the light drew people out of their dark homes like moths.
enhance:1.cnHint: 停电后，街角的施工队说新电缆会____整个街区的供电。
enhance:1.hook: Among the small crowd, one face looked very familiar.
enhance:1.line: 'These new lines will *enhance* the power for everyone here.'

famous:1.en: A man sat calmly on the bench outside the store, eating a meat bun by torchlight. Someone whispered that he was *famous* — a chef whose small restaurant two streets away had a line every night. He did not look up. He just kept eating, perfectly at ease in the dark.
famous:1.cnHint: 停电夜里，一位在街角长椅上淡定吃包子的男人据说是附近____的厨师。
famous:1.hook: He slid one extra bun across the bench without a word.
famous:1.line: 'I heard his place is *famous*, but I have never been.'

project:1.en: Tang came running from the direction of the bus stop, out of breath. She explained that the power cut was linked to a city *project* to upgrade the underground cables along our street. She had read about it on the notice board outside the store. I had never noticed that board.
project:1.cnHint: 停电原来和一个城市地下电缆____有关，同事唐早就在公告栏上看到过通知。
project:1.hook: She gave me a look that said I really should read more notices.
project:1.line: 'The whole street is part of a big *project* — did you not know?'

record:1.en: Old Mr. Chen from the corner flat came outside carrying a small battery player. He set it on the steps and pressed play. A clear, warm voice filled the quiet street. He told me it was a very old *record*, one his wife had loved. Everyone nearby stopped talking.
record:1.cnHint: 停电夜里，老陈搬出电池播放器，放起一张他妻子生前珍爱的旧____。
record:1.hook: At the last note, a woman across the street began to cry softly.
record:1.line: 'This *record* is older than you — and still sounds beautiful.'

regular:1.en: I had only worked three night shifts, but I could already tell who the *regular* visitors were. One young man arrived at half past twelve on foot, even during the blackout, guided by his phone light. He bought one coffee and one bread roll, then left without a word.
regular:1.cnHint: 即使停电，那个____在半夜光顾便利店的年轻人还是准时出现了。
regular:1.hook: Tonight he paused at the door and looked back at me strangely.
regular:1.line: 'You are already a *regular* face here — I noticed you last week.'

security:1.en: The block was dark and the street felt oddly open. The Manager stood near the entrance, arms folded. He said the store's *security* light, the one above the door that ran on a small battery, would last about two hours. After that, we would have only torches and the kindness of strangers.
security:1.cnHint: 停电后，店长说门上方靠电池供电的____灯只能再撑两个小时。
security:1.hook: Across the street, someone tried a door handle — very quietly.
security:1.line: 'The *security* light gives us two hours — use them well.'

whatever:1.en: The street outside the store went dark all at once. I stepped out and looked both ways. A few people stood under the dead lamp posts, checking their phones. 'Don't worry,' said the Manager, appearing beside me with a torch. '*Whatever* happens out here tonight, we stay open.' He sounded calm, but his hand was shaking a little.
whatever:1.cnHint: 停电了，店长拿着手电筒出现在门口，告诉我无论____发生，我们都要继续营业。
whatever:1.hook: But why did he already have the torch ready?
whatever:1.line: '*Whatever* happens tonight, we keep this door open.'

predict:1.en: Tang leaned against the counter and stared at the dark road outside. 'I knew this would happen,' he said, folding his arms. 'I could *predict* it the moment the sky turned that funny yellow colour this evening.' I looked at him. He seemed very pleased with himself for a person standing in the dark.
predict:1.cnHint: 阿糖盯着停电的街道，得意地说他早就能____今晚的停电。
predict:1.hook: Then his phone died, and he went very quiet.
predict:1.line: 'Anyone with sense could *predict* this after that yellow sky.'

road:1.en: I walked to the corner to check the fuse box. The whole *road* was black from one end to the other, not a single light in any shop window. Only our generator, sputtering softly behind the store, kept our sign half-lit. A lone figure was moving slowly towards us through the dark.
road:1.cnHint: 我走到门外，发现整条____都停电了，只有我们店还亮着微弱的灯。
road:1.hook: The figure stopped, then started walking faster.
road:1.line: 'The whole *road* is out — we are the only light left.'

solution:1.en: The Manager drew a small diagram on a receipt and explained his plan for the generator. 'This is my *solution*,' he said, tapping the paper. 'We run the fridge, the register, and one lamp. Everything else stays off.' It sounded sensible. Tang immediately pointed out three reasons it would not work.
solution:1.cnHint: 店长在收据背面画图，向我们解释他对停电的____方案。
solution:1.hook: Oddly, Tang's third reason made the Manager go pale.
solution:1.line: 'Here is my *solution* — fridge, register, one lamp, nothing more.'

total:1.en: I counted the candles left in stock: four. I counted the torches: two, and one had no batteries. Tang added up the numbers on the register screen and shook his head. 'A *total* loss for tonight,' he said. Just then the door opened and six customers walked in at once, all of them wanting hot food.
total:1.cnHint: 阿糖算了算今晚的账，说是____亏损，然而就在这时门开了。
total:1.hook: Six cold and hungry people can change a night very fast.
total:1.line: 'By my count this is a *total* loss — unless something changes fast.'

fail:1.en: The small generator outside began to sputter. The single lamp above the counter flickered twice, then held. 'Please don't *fail* on us now,' I whispered, patting the wall as if the building could hear me. The Manager gave me a look. Then the lamp flickered again, and even he whispered something under his breath.
fail:1.cnHint: 发电机开始突突作响，我轻声祈祷它不要在这时候____。
fail:1.hook: What the Manager whispered, I could not quite catch.
fail:1.line: 'Old machine, please don't *fail* us on the one night we need you.'

function:1.en: Lin arrived from the store across the street, carrying a small radio. 'Mine has no power at all,' she said, setting it on our counter. 'At least your place still has some *function*.' She said it without any real meanness, more like a tired compliment. Then she asked if she could stay until the power came back.
function:1.cnHint: 对面店铺的隔壁咖啡店的林拿着收音机过来，说我们店至少还有些____，想在这里等来电。
function:1.hook: She and the Manager had clearly met before — neither said hello.
function:1.line: 'Your shop still has some *function*; mine is completely dead.'

method:1.en: Tang tried three ways to reset the breaker on the outside wall. Each one failed. 'You have no *method*,' Lin said, watching from the doorway with her arms crossed. Tang turned around, looking offended. The Manager stepped between them and tried a fourth way without a word. The lights on the street blinked, and one came back on.
method:1.cnHint: 阿糖想重置断路器却屡屡失败，隔壁咖啡店的林说他没有____，店长默默上前试了第四种方式。
method:1.hook: Only one street light came on — the one right above Lin's store.
method:1.line: 'You need a proper *method*, not just pushing things and hoping.'

differ:1.en: The street outside our store looks completely different after dark. The neon light above the door throws orange shadows that *differ* from anything I saw during the day shift. Tang leans on the counter and says the night crowd is a whole other world. I am starting to believe him.
differ:1.cnHint: 夜班时，店外的街道和白天____很大，唐告诉我夜间的顾客完全是另一个世界。
differ:1.hook: Then a man in a yellow raincoat stopped and stared at our door.
differ:1.line: 'The night people *differ* from the day crowd — you will see.'

shape:1.en: The power cut hit at midnight. I grabbed a torch and swept the beam across the shelves. Outside the window, a strange *shape* moved slowly past — too tall for a person, too quiet for a car. Tang did not even look up from his phone. 'Just Old Mr Chen and his umbrella,' he said.
shape:1.cnHint: 停电后，我用手电筒照向窗外，看到一个奇怪的____缓缓走过。
shape:1.hook: But Old Mr Chen, I would later learn, had been out of town for a week.
shape:1.line: 'There is a *shape* by the window — do you see it?'

twice:1.en: The lights went out, came back, then went out again. I reached for the emergency torch *twice* before I finally found it under the counter. Tang laughed quietly in the dark. 'First blackout?' he asked. I nodded, even though he could not see me. Outside, someone knocked on the glass door.
twice:1.cnHint: 停电时，我____找手电筒才摸到，唐在黑暗中轻声笑了。
twice:1.hook: Whoever knocked did not wait — they had already slipped inside.
twice:1.line: 'I have dropped this torch *twice* tonight — my hands are shaking.'

aspect:1.en: Tang told me that every *aspect* of the night shift is different from what the Manager describes in training. The silence, the strange orders, the way the street seems to hold its breath at 2 a.m. — none of it is in the handbook. He tapped the dark window. 'You just have to feel it,' he said.
aspect:1.cnHint: 唐告诉我，夜班的每个____都和店长培训时说的不一样。
aspect:1.hook: He never told me which aspect scared him most.
aspect:1.line: 'Every *aspect* of this shift surprises new clerks — trust me.'

currently:1.en: The Manager called to check on us during the blackout. 'How is the generator?' he asked. 'It is *currently* making a very unhappy noise,' I told him. There was a long pause. 'That noise is normal,' he said, and hung up. I was not convinced. Neither, from her face, was Tang.
currently:1.cnHint: 停电时店长打电话询问发电机，我告诉他它____发出很奇怪的声音。
currently:1.hook: Two seconds later the generator stopped completely.
currently:1.line: 'The backup power is *currently* doing something I cannot explain.'

decrease:1.en: As the blackout stretched past an hour, the number of customers began to *decrease* until the street was completely empty. Only one person remained outside — standing very still under the broken lamp post. I asked Tang if we should check on them. He shook his head slowly. 'We wait,' he said.
decrease:1.cnHint: 停电超过一小时后，顾客数量开始____，最后街上只剩一个一动不动的人。
decrease:1.hook: The figure outside had not moved in twenty minutes.
decrease:1.line: 'Sales always *decrease* during a blackout, but tonight feels different.'

possibility:1.en: I listed every *possibility* I could think of for why the lights were still off: unpaid bill, storm damage, something chewing the cables behind the building. Tang listened politely, then pointed to the corner. A small cat sat proudly beside a very chewed power strip. Case closed.
possibility:1.cnHint: 我列举了停电的各种____，唐默默指向角落——一只猫坐在一根被咬坏的插线板旁边。
possibility:1.hook: The cat, Tang whispered, had been here longer than the Manager.
possibility:1.line: 'There is one more *possibility* you have not considered,' Tang said softly.
