forget:2.cnHint: 停电时我习惯性地盘点货架，阿糖却说我一定会____那些数字的。
forget:2.hook: When the lights finally came back on, one shelf was completely empty and neither of us remembered selling anything from it.
forget:2.line: 'Do not *forget* to count the candles — they have a habit of walking off on their own.'

particularly:2.en: The blackout lasted two hours. Afterward, Tang made two cups of warm tea and handed me one without a word. The night had been strange, but not bad — *particularly* the part when a small child in pyjamas wandered in, looked at the candles, and whispered 'pretty' before a tired parent appeared and carried them away.
particularly:2.cnHint: 漫长的停电夜并不难熬，____是那个穿着睡衣闯进来的小孩带来了温暖。
particularly:2.hook: The parent paused at the door, glanced back at me, and looked like they wanted to say something important.
particularly:2.line: 'I liked tonight, *particularly* the part where we just sat and listened to the rain.'

meanwhile:2.en: The power cut hit at two in the morning. I found a box of candles under the counter and lit three in a row. *Meanwhile*, Tang was in the back room, counting the cash drawer by phone-light and humming a little song as if nothing at all had happened. The warm glow made the whole store feel like a secret den.
meanwhile:2.cnHint: 停电时，我点燃蜡烛，____阿糖在后屋借着手机灯光数钱。
meanwhile:2.hook: Then Tang called out — the cash drawer was one note short.
meanwhile:2.line: '*Meanwhile*, I found the spare key taped inside the drawer — did you know about that?'

damage:2.en: A shelf fell during the blackout. Cans rolled everywhere and one jar of pickles cracked on the floor. I swept it up fast, but the smell was strong. The Manager arrived at six, looked at the wet patch, and clicked his tongue. 'Let me check the *damage*,' he said, pulling out a small notebook and writing things down very carefully.
damage:2.cnHint: 停电时货架倒下，店长天亮后来查看____情况。
damage:2.hook: The last line in his notebook was not about the shelf at all.
damage:2.line: 'The *damage* is not too bad — but don't tell the owner just yet.'

police:2.en: At three in the morning a knock came at the locked glass door. A woman in a rain coat held up a small card. *Police*, it read. She asked if anyone had come in acting strangely in the last hour. I thought of the man who had bought six lighters and said nothing. I told her yes.
police:2.cnHint: 深夜停电后，____来店里询问是否有可疑人员进入。
police:2.hook: She nodded slowly and wrote down the lighter count.
police:2.line: 'The *police* say the power cut was not an accident — please keep that quiet.'

race:2.en: The emergency lights ran on a small battery that was dying fast. Tang and I had maybe ten minutes before total darkness. We began a quiet *race* through the store — grabbing torches, candles, and the first-aid box — moving in opposite directions around the shelves like two fish in a round tank. Tang won by one item.
race:2.cnHint: 备用电池快耗尽，我和阿糖展开了一场找手电筒的____。
race:2.hook: The item Tang found last was not on any shelf — it was taped behind the mirror.
race:2.line: 'This is a *race* — first one to the torch cupboard gets the last warm bun.'

medical:2.en: A young man rushed in just after the power died. He was calm but his hands were shaking. He asked for the *medical* kit behind the counter — his friend outside had cut her hand on a fence in the dark. I handed it over without a word. Tang watched from the door as he ran back out into the black street.
medical:2.cnHint: 停电后一位年轻人冲进来取____急救包，说朋友在黑暗中受伤了。
medical:2.hook: He never came back to return the kit — or to explain.
medical:2.line: 'The *medical* kit is almost empty — who used the last bandage and said nothing?'

wear:2.en: Old Mr Chen came in at four, the same time every night. Even in the blackout he found his shelf by touch. Tonight, though, I noticed the *wear* on his coat — the elbows were thin as paper and one button was gone. He bought his usual tea and a meat bun, counted the coins twice, and gave me a small nod.
wear:2.cnHint: 停电的夜晚，常客陈老先生来买东西，我第一次注意到他外套的____痕迹。
wear:2.hook: On the back of his receipt he had written a name and a phone number.
wear:2.line: 'The *wear* on these shelves tells me this store is older than it looks.'

climate:2.en: Tang leaned against the dark fridge and sighed. 'The *climate* in this store has changed,' she said, meaning the mood, not the air — two clerks had quit last month and everyone was tired. I handed her a warm canned drink from the non-cold shelf. She held it with both hands and looked a little less tired. A little.
climate:2.cnHint: 阿糖感叹店里的____变了，言下之意是近来人心惶惶、士气低落。
climate:2.hook: Then she said something about the Manager that I was not ready to hear.
climate:2.line: 'The *climate* here used to be warmer — something changed after that new rule came in.'

head:2.en: The Manager sent a voice message at five in the morning. I held the phone to my ear in the candlelit store. 'Use your *head*,' his voice said, a little sharp. 'If the fridge alarm goes off, write down the time and call me. Do not open the fridge door.' I wrote the rule on my hand in pen so I would not forget.
head:2.cnHint: 停电期间，店长发来语音消息，叮嘱我用____想清楚，冰箱报警要记录时间。
head:2.hook: The fridge alarm went off thirty seconds later.
head:2.line: 'Use your *head*, not just the manual — the manual was written before this store existed.'

land:2.en: The power cut at midnight. I lit two candles and stared at the old map the Manager had taped above the register. It showed a stretch of *land* far to the north, full of rivers and green hills. He had circled one small village in red ink. I never thought to ask him why — until tonight, when I found a letter tucked behind it.
land:2.cnHint: 停电后，店员发现地图背后藏着一封信，地图上圈着某片____。
land:2.hook: The letter was sealed, but the name on the front was not the Manager's.
land:2.line: 'That *land* in the north is where I was born,' he once told Tang softly.

promote:2.en: Tang slid a handwritten sign across the counter. 'The Manager wants to *promote* the new hot drinks,' she whispered, 'but the machine is dead without power.' We laughed quietly. Outside, rain tapped the window. We propped the sign up anyway, facing the dark street, more out of habit than hope.
promote:2.cnHint: 停电期间，同事拿出一张手写告示，想____新推出的热饮，结果却闹了个笑话。
promote:2.hook: Then someone outside actually tried the door, reading that sign in the dark.
promote:2.line: 'Help me *promote* this before the Manager checks on us,' Tang said with a grin.

purchase:2.en: A woman in a yellow raincoat came in holding a candle of her own. She set three items on the counter slowly, like a quiet ritual. 'One *purchase* before the lights come back,' she said, half to herself. I bagged them carefully. She looked at each item as if saying goodbye to something.
purchase:2.cnHint: 停电中，一位穿黄色雨衣的女士来店里完成了一次____，举止神秘而若有所思。
purchase:2.hook: She left without taking her change, and did not look back once.
purchase:2.line: 'Just one small *purchase* — I always do this when the power goes out,' she said.

rely:2.en: The emergency torch kept cutting out. 'You can't *rely* on that old thing,' Tang said, shaking it until a thin beam returned. We had already used every candle on the shelf. I kept the cash drawer open by hand and wrote totals on a paper bag. It was slow, but it worked fine.
rely:2.cnHint: 停电时手电筒频繁熄灭，同事说不能____这个老家伙，两人只好用纸袋记账。
rely:2.hook: Then Tang went quiet — she was reading something on that paper bag.
rely:2.line: 'Never *rely* on anything with batteries older than my shoes,' Tang muttered firmly.

connect:2.en: My phone had no signal. I tried to *connect* to the store's small backup router, but only one bar appeared and then vanished. Tang wrote a note on card and taped it to the door: 'We are open. Cash only. Come in.' It felt oddly warm, like the whole street was suddenly smaller.
connect:2.cnHint: 停电后手机无法____网络，同事在门上贴了张手写告示，街道反而显得温馨起来。
connect:2.hook: A boy outside read the note, then stood still for a long moment before entering.
connect:2.line: 'If you can *connect* to anything at all, tell the Manager we are fine,' Tang said.

indicate:2.en: Tang pointed to the small thermostat on the wall. 'The needle will *indicate* if it gets too cold for the drinks in the back,' she said. I watched it all night like a nervous student watching a clock. Around three in the morning, the needle moved. I called Tang over at once.
indicate:2.cnHint: 停电夜里，同事说墙上的温度计会____后仓饮料是否受冻，结果凌晨三点指针真的动了。
indicate:2.hook: What Tang saw behind the back-room door made her go very still.
indicate:2.line: 'That needle will *indicate* trouble long before we smell anything wrong,' Tang said.

period:2.en: Lin appeared just after two o'clock, leaning on the counter with a coffee cup from somewhere else. 'Rough *period* for your little shop, huh?' he said, nodding at the candles. I smiled politely. Tang, stacking cups nearby, did not look up — but her jaw tightened just a little.
period:2.cnHint: 停电____里，竞争对手隔壁咖啡店的林拿着别家的咖啡来串门，同事阿糖听了他的话悄悄攥紧了拳头。
period:2.hook: Lin left a folded receipt on the counter, and I wish I had not opened it.
period:2.line: 'Every shop goes through a hard *period* — the question is what you do next,' Lin said.

picture:2.en: Behind the register I found a faded *picture* tucked under a roll of tape. It showed four young people standing outside this same store, laughing, in what looked like summer. The sign above them was different — older letters. I recognised the Manager's eyes immediately, but not the others.
picture:2.cnHint: 店员在收银台后面发现了一张旧____，照片里的年轻人们站在这家店门口，店长的眼神一眼就认出来了。
picture:2.hook: One of the four people in the photo was wearing Lin's old team jacket.
picture:2.line: 'That *picture* has been there since before I started,' Tang said, her voice going soft.

return:2.en: The power cut at eleven. I found a small notebook near the back shelf — someone had left it the week before. There was a name inside: Lin. I set it by the counter, ready for her *return*. The store felt very quiet without the hum of the lights.
return:2.cnHint: 停电后，我在货架附近发现了一本笔记本，等待失主____。
return:2.hook: But the notebook was gone by midnight, and no one had come in.
return:2.line: 'I am here for the *return* of my notebook,' she said softly.

remove:2.en: Tang lit a small candle from under the counter. The flame made long shadows on the wall. I tried to *remove* a fallen display stand, but it was heavier than it looked. Tang watched me struggle for a moment, then walked over without a word and lifted one end.
remove:2.cnHint: 停电时，我努力____倒下的展示架，同事默默走来帮忙。
remove:2.hook: Under the stand was an envelope none of us had ever seen before.
remove:2.line: 'Let me help you *remove* that,' Tang said quietly.

colleague:2.en: The candles threw warm light across the shelves. I had only worked one week, so I did not know everyone yet. Tang was the first *colleague* who actually talked to me — not about work, but about the street outside, the old cat that slept by the bins, small things.
colleague:2.cnHint: 停电的夜晚，我才真正开始认识这位____。
colleague:2.hook: Then Tang said something strange: 'Don't trust the morning staff.'
colleague:2.line: 'You are a good *colleague* to have on a dark night,' Tang said.

normal:2.en: At midnight the power came back. The lights buzzed on, the fridge hummed, and everything looked *normal* again. But I noticed one shelf was different — three cans of soup, stacked in a careful triangle. Nobody had been in the back room. I had been at the counter the whole time.
normal:2.cnHint: 来电后一切看起来____，但货架上有些东西悄悄变了。
normal:2.hook: The security camera, I then realised, had been facing the wrong way all night.
normal:2.line: 'Everything looks *normal* to me,' Tang said, frowning at the shelf.

succeed:2.en: The Manager had left a note before going home: 'Try to *succeed* in keeping the cold drinks stocked — the delivery box is in the back.' I found the box, but it was already half empty. Someone had taken drinks during the blackout without paying. I checked every corner of the store.
succeed:2.cnHint: 店长留了张便条，希望我能____完成备货任务，但箱子已经少了一半。
succeed:2.hook: The receipt on top of the box was signed with only one initial: L.
succeed:2.line: 'Did you *succeed* in finding the stock?' the Manager asked the next morning.

image:2.en: When the lights died, my phone screen was the only light. I used it to check the shelf labels. Then I noticed something: a photo was stuck to the inside of the stock-room door — a faded *image* of four people smiling in front of this very store, years ago. One of the faces looked like Lin.
image:2.cnHint: 库房门上贴着一张旧____，其中一张脸让我感到熟悉。
image:2.hook: In the photo, the store sign behind them showed a completely different name.
image:2.line: 'That old *image* has been there for years,' Tang said, looking away.

ourselves:2.en: The blackout lasted nearly two hours. Tang made tea on a small gas ring, and we sat on the step behind the counter. 'We should enjoy *ourselves*,' Tang said. 'The Manager never lets us rest like this.' It was the most peaceful the store had ever felt. Then the door opened.
ourselves:2.cnHint: 停电期间，我和同事难得清闲，决定好好让____放松一下。
ourselves:2.hook: The person who walked in was not a regular, and they were soaking wet.
ourselves:2.line: 'Let's enjoy *ourselves* while it is quiet,' Tang said with a small smile.

catch:2.en: I heard a sound from the back aisle — a soft knock, like something falling. I took a candle and went to look. A tin had rolled off the shelf. I bent down to *catch* it before it reached the drain at the floor's edge. When I stood up, I saw light under the stock-room door.
catch:2.cnHint: 我去查看声音，弯腰____滚落的罐头，却发现库房门下透着光。
catch:2.hook: The stock-room had been locked all night, and I had the only key.
catch:2.line: 'Quick, *catch* it before it falls,' Tang said from behind me.

mistake:2.en: The power cut had lasted ten minutes. I checked the safe by phone-light and found the drawer open. The cash inside was untouched, but a handwritten note sat on top: 'This is not a *mistake* — you left this unlocked three nights in a row. Fix it.' No name, no date.
mistake:2.cnHint: 停电时，我发现保险箱抽屉大开，里面压着一张神秘纸条，提醒我犯了____。
mistake:2.hook: The handwriting looked exactly like the Manager's.
mistake:2.line: 'Leaving the safe open every night is not a small *mistake*,' the note said.

staff:2.en: The backup lights clicked on at last. I stood behind the counter and looked around. In the pale yellow glow I counted four people still inside: Tang restocking chips, a security guard by the door, a delivery man waiting for a signature, and me. Four *staff* members, no customers, one shared sigh of relief.
staff:2.cnHint: 停电后备用灯亮起，店里四名____各就各位，场面意外地温馨。
staff:2.hook: Then the delivery man whispered something to Tang that wiped the smile off her face.
staff:2.line: 'How many *staff* are still on duty tonight?' the guard asked quietly.

enhance:2.en: Tang lit three small candles and placed them along the front shelf. The soft light made the rows of snacks look almost beautiful. 'Candlelight can *enhance* even a convenience store,' she said with a straight face. A regular customer walked in just then, stopped at the door, and slowly began to clap.
enhance:2.cnHint: 停电时，阿阿糖点起蜡烛，说烛光能____便利店的氛围，没想到引来掌声。
enhance:2.hook: The clapping customer then asked for something we definitely did not sell.
enhance:2.line: 'A little candlelight can *enhance* the whole mood in here,' Tang said.

famous:2.en: An old man shuffled in out of the dark street and set a dusty tin on the counter. 'I used to sell these biscuits,' he said. 'Twenty years ago this corner shop was *famous* for them. Is the Manager still the same person?' He tapped the tin twice and waited, eyes bright behind thick glasses.
famous:2.cnHint: 一位老人在停电夜走进来，说这家店曾因一种饼干而____，想找当年的店长。
famous:2.hook: The tin was still sealed, and the date on the lid read twenty-two years ago.
famous:2.line: 'This little shop was once *famous* all along this street,' the old man said.

project:2.en: I found a folder wedged behind the back-room shelf while searching for candles. On the cover, in red pen: 'Night Shift Improvement *Project* — Phase 2.' Inside were charts, timed observations, and staff notes — all about me, dated from my very first week. Someone had been watching carefully from the start.
project:2.cnHint: 停电摸黑找蜡烛时，我在储物架后发现一个关于我的神秘____文件夹。
project:2.hook: The most recent note was dated just this morning.
project:2.line: 'This *project* has been running since your first night here,' Tang said calmly.

record:2.en: The old radio behind the counter crackled back to life on battery power. A slow, warm song filled the dark shop. Tang froze mid-step. 'That's from a *record* my father owned,' she said softly. 'I haven't heard it in fifteen years.' She stood very still, a bag of chips held against her chest.
record:2.cnHint: 停电时收音机突然播出一首老歌，阿阿糖说这首歌来自父亲珍藏的一张____。
record:2.hook: When the song ended, someone outside began humming the same tune.
record:2.line: 'My father had every *record* that singer ever made,' Tang said quietly.

regular:2.en: The power had been off for half an hour. Most customers left, but one man stayed on his usual stool at the window counter, reading by phone-light. Tang leaned over and told me he was a *regular* — here every night from eleven to one, same stool, same instant noodles, same silence. Tonight he had not ordered anything.
regular:2.cnHint: 停电后大多数顾客离开，只有一位____客人坐在老位置，今晚却一直没点任何东西。
regular:2.hook: Then I noticed his bowl from last night was still sitting there, untouched.
regular:2.line: 'He is our most *regular* customer — never misses a single night,' Tang said.

security:2.en: I noticed the small camera above the door had a red light still blinking — battery-powered. Tang saw me looking. 'The *security* system stays on even in a blackout,' she said. 'The Manager had it upgraded after something happened two winters ago.' She paused, then turned away before I could ask what that something was.
security:2.cnHint: 停电后摄像头红灯仍在闪烁，阿阿糖说____系统有备用电源，原因与两年前的一件事有关。
security:2.hook: The footage from two winters ago was apparently still saved somewhere.
security:2.line: 'Our *security* system never goes down, no matter what,' Tang said firmly.

whatever:2.en: The lights went out at eleven. The Manager grabbed a torch and said we would keep serving *whatever* customers came in, rain or not. I found candles under the counter and lit them one by one. The store glowed like a small lantern on the dark street.
whatever:2.cnHint: 停电后，店长说无论____顾客都要继续服务。
whatever:2.hook: Then someone knocked on the locked back door.
whatever:2.line: '*Whatever* you need tonight, we are open.'

predict:2.en: Tang checked the weather app before the power cut and tried to *predict* how long the outage would last. 'Two hours, maybe three,' she said, counting the candles. She was wrong. By midnight the fridge hummed back to life, and Tang looked almost disappointed her guess had failed.
predict:2.cnHint: 唐试图____停电会持续多久，结果并不准确。
predict:2.hook: But the security camera footage from that hour was gone.
predict:2.line: 'I can *predict* the end time — about two hours from now.'

road:2.en: A cyclist appeared at the glass door, soaked through. He said every light on the *road* outside had gone dark, and our candles were the only warm glow for three blocks. He bought two hot drinks and stood dripping by the counter, in no hurry to leave.
road:2.cnHint: 一位骑车人说外面____上的路灯全灭了，只有我们的店还亮着。
road:2.hook: He kept glancing back at something parked across the road.
road:2.line: 'The whole *road* is dark — yours is the only light left.'

solution:2.en: The fridge alarm beeped without power, and Tang could not find the off switch. The Manager tried every button. I suggested pulling the plug from the wall. It worked. 'Simple *solution*,' the Manager said, patting my shoulder, and I felt quietly proud for the first time that night.
solution:2.cnHint: 冰柜警报响个不停，我找到了一个简单的____。
solution:2.hook: Then the alarm in the back room started.
solution:2.line: 'That is the best *solution* I have seen all week.'

total:2.en: I counted the candles: twelve. Tang counted the customers still inside: four. The Manager added up the cash in the drawer and announced a *total* of exactly zero extra coins. 'Perfect chaos,' he said cheerfully, writing the number in his small notebook with a steady hand.
total:2.cnHint: 店长把收银机里的钱加了个____，结果是整数。
total:2.hook: The notebook, I noticed, had someone else's name on the cover.
total:2.line: 'The *total* comes to zero — how does that even happen?'

fail:2.en: The backup torch began to *fail* halfway through the outage, its light shrinking to a thin yellow thread. Tang shook it twice, then set it on the counter like a patient. The Manager lit another candle from his pocket without comment, as if he had expected this all along.
fail:2.cnHint: 备用手电筒开始____，光线越来越弱。
fail:2.hook: The Manager's spare candle smelled oddly of something sweet.
fail:2.line: 'If this torch starts to *fail*, we still have six candles left.'

function:2.en: Without electricity the card reader lost its *function*, and every sale became cash only. Most customers nodded and dug through their pockets. One young woman froze — no coins, no notes. Tang quietly handed her a warm rice ball and waved her off, saying tonight had different rules.
function:2.cnHint: 停电后，刷卡机失去了____，只能用现金结账。
function:2.hook: The woman left a folded note on the counter instead of money.
function:2.line: 'The card reader has no *function* right now — cash only, sorry.'

method:2.en: Lin arrived just before midnight with a portable lamp and a very confident look. His *method* for dealing with power cuts: arrive late, bring your own light, buy the last hot noodles. It was annoying and also perfect. He winked at me and took the corner seat like a king.
method:2.cnHint: 林有一套应对停电的____，而且每次都管用。
method:2.hook: He seemed to have known about the outage before it happened.
method:2.line: 'My *method* is simple — always bring your own light source.'

review:2.en: The power cut came at midnight. I found a notebook on the back shelf, left by the last clerk. Every page was filled with neat notes — a *review* of every regular customer: their usual drinks, their quiet habits, their late-night moods. Someone had studied this store like an exam.
review:2.cnHint: 我在货架后找到一本笔记，里面是前任店员对每位常客的____。
review:2.hook: The last entry had no name — only a question mark.
review:2.line: 'This *review* tells you everything you need to survive the night shift.'

ahead:2.en: The emergency lights flickered on, casting long shadows. I checked the small clock above the door: three hours still *ahead* before dawn. The street outside was silent except for one pair of shoes clicking slowly toward the glass. Whoever it was, they were in no hurry.
ahead:2.cnHint: 停电后，天亮前还有三个小时____，店外却有脚步声慢慢靠近。
ahead:2.hook: The footsteps stopped right outside the door.
ahead:2.line: 'Three hours *ahead* of us — anything could walk in.'

cheap:2.en: Tang pulled two instant noodle cups from the shelf and set them on the counter with a tired grin. 'Power is out, hot water is still working, and these are the least *cheap* thing I could find,' she said. We ate standing up, listening to the dark street hum softly outside.
cheap:2.cnHint: 停电中，阿糖从货架上选了两杯泡面，说这已经不算____了。
cheap:2.hook: Then we heard a knock from inside the stock room.
cheap:2.line: 'Don't call it *cheap* — it's the best meal this shift has.

critical:2.en: The store refrigerator made a loud crack and went silent. Tang looked at me with wide eyes. 'That unit is *critical*,' she said quietly. 'Everything inside will spoil before morning.' I grabbed the torch and we walked slowly toward the humming dark at the back of the store.
critical:2.cnHint: 冰柜突然停转，阿糖说这台机器在停电之夜____至极。
critical:2.hook: Inside the fridge, something had already started to move.
critical:2.line: 'Keeping that fridge running is *critical* — don't touch the switch.'

motivate:2.en: I almost sat down and did nothing. Then I remembered what the Manager had written on a small card taped to the register: 'A quiet store is not a sleeping store.' Those nine words were enough to *motivate* me to walk every aisle, check every shelf, and stay alert until sunrise.
motivate:2.cnHint: 店长留在收银台的一张小卡片足以____我在停电之夜坚持下去。
motivate:2.hook: But the card was signed with a name I did not recognise.
motivate:2.line: 'Let those words *motivate* you when the night feels too long.'

charge:2.en: A man in a raincoat stepped in and asked if we still had a working socket. 'My phone is dead,' he said. I pointed to the one socket still powered by the backup line. Tang whispered to me, 'Should we *charge* him?' I shook my head. He plugged in and stood there, staring at nothing.
charge:2.cnHint: 一个陌生男人进店要求手机充电，阿糖小声问我要不要____他费用。
charge:2.hook: When his screen lit up, his face went pale.
charge:2.line: 'We won't *charge* you — just stay where we can see you.'

complex:2.en: Lin arrived just before two in the morning, carrying a thick folder. She spread papers across the small corner table without a word. The diagrams inside were *complex*, full of tiny arrows and numbers I could not follow. She caught me staring and covered the pages with her arm, very slowly.
complex:2.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林深夜带来一个文件夹，里面的图表____得让人看不懂。
complex:2.hook: One diagram had our store's address printed at the centre.
complex:2.line: 'It looks *complex*, but every answer is hidden somewhere inside.'

itself:2.en: At half past two the power came back. The store blinked to life: lights, the soft music, the hum of the fridge. Everything looked the same, yet the night had changed the place somehow. The store *itself* felt different now — smaller, warmer, and full of secrets I had only just begun to find.
itself:2.cnHint: 来电之后，这家店____感觉变了，仿佛藏着许多秘密。
itself:2.hook: Then I noticed one shelf had been quietly rearranged.
itself:2.line: 'The store *itself* will teach you more than any training day.'

join:2.en: The power cut turned the store dim. I found a short cable under the counter and used it to *join* two emergency lights together, doubling their glow. Customers relaxed when the soft light spread across the shelves. In the quiet, Tang handed me a warm can of corn soup.
join:2.cnHint: 停电后，我用一根电线把两盏应急灯____在一起，让店里亮了许多。
join:2.hook: But Tang's hands were shaking long before the lights went out.
join:2.line: 'Can you *join* these two wires? My hands won't stop shaking.'

significant:2.en: During the blackout I sorted through a box of lost items behind the counter. Most were ordinary — pens, an umbrella, one glove. But one envelope felt *significant*: it was sealed, addressed to 'the night clerk,' and had been sitting there for three weeks.
significant:2.cnHint: 我在柜台后面整理失物，发现一个____的信封，上面写着"夜班店员收"。
significant:2.hook: Someone knew a night clerk would come. They just had to wait.
significant:2.line: 'That envelope is *significant* — don't throw it away, please.'

step:2.en: The store was pitch dark. I moved slowly, one careful *step* at a time, using the faint glow of the drinks fridge as my guide. Near the magazine rack I bumped into something soft — a schoolbag left on the floor, zipper open, homework spilling out.
step:2.cnHint: 停电后我一____一步地在黑暗中走动，在杂志架旁踩到了一个没人认领的书包。
step:2.hook: Inside the bag was a name tag, but the name belonged to no regular.
step:2.line: 'Watch your *step* — someone left a bag right there in the dark.'

unique:2.en: Lin came in during the outage carrying a small lantern with a paper shade painted with tiny fish. The warm orange light made the whole store look like something from an old painting. 'My grandmother made it,' she said quietly. Every fish on it was *unique*, no two the same.
unique:2.cnHint: 林带来了一盏祖母亲手做的纸灯笼，每条鱼的图案都____，没有两条是相同的。
unique:2.hook: Lin's smile faded the moment she saw what was on the top shelf.
unique:2.line: 'Each fish is *unique* — Grandmother painted them one by one, late at night.'

inside:2.en: The Manager left a handwritten note taped to the stockroom door before he went home. I read it by torchlight: 'Emergency candles are *inside* the blue box, bottom shelf, left wall.' I found the box easily, but beside it was a second box with no label at all.
inside:2.cnHint: 店长留了张纸条，说应急蜡烛就在蓝色箱子____，但旁边还有一个没有标签的箱子。
inside:2.hook: The unlabelled box was warm to the touch.
inside:2.line: 'Everything you need is *inside* the blue box — do not open the other one.'

majority:2.en: I did a quick head count during the blackout. Eight customers were in the store. The *majority* chose to stay rather than walk home in the dark — they sat on stacked water bottles near the window, sharing snacks and talking in low voices. One person stood alone by the door.
majority:2.cnHint: 停电时店里有八位顾客，____选择留下来，只有一个人独自站在门口。
majority:2.hook: The person at the door kept checking a phone that never lit up.
majority:2.line: 'The *majority* want to stay — should I lock the front door or leave it open?'

notice:2.en: A small yellow *notice* was pinned to the community board beside the door — I had walked past it a hundred times without reading it. By candlelight I finally stopped and read: 'If the lights go out, check the grey box above the fridge.' I had never seen any grey box.
notice:2.cnHint: 蜡烛光下我终于看清了门边布告栏上的一张____，上面说停电时要检查冰箱上方的灰色箱子。
notice:2.hook: There was indeed a grey box, and it was already open.
notice:2.line: 'Did you *notice* that sign by the door? It mentions a grey box upstairs.'

taste:2.en: Tang lit a candle and heated two cups of instant noodles on the small back-room stove. He passed one to me without a word. After a long cold hour in the dark, the salty broth had a *taste* that felt almost like a hug. I forgot to ask where he had found the stove.
taste:2.cnHint: 唐在后屋悄悄热好了两杯面，那碗汤的____在停电的寒意中像一个拥抱。
taste:2.hook: The back room had no stove on my first day — I was certain of it.
taste:2.line: 'The *taste* is nothing special, but it's hot — drink it before it gets cold.'

differ:2.en: The storage room smelled of old cardboard. I found two boxes of emergency candles, but they *differed* in size — one set thin and tall, the other short and fat. I lit the short ones first. Good thing I checked: the tall ones belonged to Lin, labelled in neat handwriting.
differ:2.cnHint: 停电后，我在储藏室发现两盒蜡烛，但它们的尺寸____。
differ:2.hook: Why did Lin keep personal candles hidden in the store?
differ:2.line: 'These *differ* from the store's stock — please don't touch them.'

shape:2.en: A customer slid a note under the back door. I picked it up and held my candle close. Drawn on the paper was a rough *shape* — a circle with a smaller circle inside. No words. The Manager, standing behind me, went very quiet when I showed it to him.
shape:2.cnHint: 停电时，有人从后门递进一张纸条，上面画着一个____。
shape:2.hook: The Manager had seen that shape before — somewhere he clearly regretted.
shape:2.line: 'That *shape* means someone outside knows where the safe is.'

twice:2.en: The old fridge beeped *twice* as the power died, then fell silent. I walked the dark aisles, counting shelves by touch. On my second pass I bumped into Tang, who was already holding a flashlight. 'I keep spares,' she whispered, handing me one with a small, satisfied smile.
twice:2.cnHint: 停电时冰箱____响了，唐早已准备好了手电筒。
twice:2.hook: Tang's flashlight had a name written on the handle — not hers.
twice:2.line: 'It beeped *twice*; that means the temperature is rising fast.'

aspect:2.en: Tang walked me through every *aspect* of closing the register by candlelight: counting coins, checking the receipt roll, locking the drawer. She was calm and exact. I tried to keep up. Outside, someone pressed their face against the dark glass, watching us work.
aspect:2.cnHint: 停电期间，唐仔细教我收银台工作的每个____。
aspect:2.hook: The face at the glass was gone before I could look up properly.
aspect:2.line: 'Every *aspect* of the close must be done correctly, even in the dark.'

currently:2.en: I picked up the store's old wall phone — it still worked without power. A recorded voice said the repair team was *currently* working on the street outside. I felt relieved. Then I noticed the street through the window was completely empty. No truck. No workers. No lights.
currently:2.cnHint: 停电后我打电话询问，语音提示维修队____正在工作，但窗外空无一人。
currently:2.hook: Someone had changed that recorded message very recently.
currently:2.line: 'They say the crew is *currently* on-site, but I see nobody out there.'

decrease:2.en: Tang watched the candle on the counter and frowned. 'As the flame gets lower, my good mood will *decrease* at the same rate,' she said. I laughed. Then she pointed at the back shelf: the emergency battery lamp we relied on had a crack running straight through its case.
decrease:2.cnHint: 唐看着蜡烛，担心心情会随烛光____，而备用灯也出了问题。
decrease:2.hook: That crack was fresh — something had hit the lamp tonight.
decrease:2.line: 'My patience will *decrease* fast if we have no backup light.'

possibility:2.en: The Manager spread a small hand-drawn floor plan on the counter. 'There is a *possibility*,' he said slowly, 'that the fuse box is behind the noodle shelf.' I moved twelve packs of instant noodles by candlelight. Behind them was a wall. Just a wall. The Manager stared at it for a long time.
possibility:2.cnHint: 停电后，店长认为有____保险丝盒就在面条架后面，但结果让人意外。
possibility:2.hook: Then the wall made a soft, hollow knock all by itself.
possibility:2.line: 'There is a *possibility* I remembered this floor plan wrong.'

crucial:2.en: Tang grabbed my arm. 'The ice-cream freezer — that is the *crucial* one. If it melts, the Manager will make us pay.' We dragged a big cooler box from storage and began moving the ice cream by hand, candle balanced on a shelf above us. It was messy, cold, and somehow fun.
crucial:2.cnHint: 唐告诉我，停电期间保住冰淇淋柜是____的，于是我们紧急转移冰淇淋。
crucial:2.hook: At the bottom of the freezer lay a small sealed envelope addressed to Lin.
crucial:2.line: 'Saving the ice cream is *crucial* — the Manager checks every single one.'

enormous:2.en: The power cut left the store lit only by two small candles. I opened the storage room to look for torches and stopped at the door. An *enormous* shadow stretched across the wall — big enough to belong to a bear. My heart jumped. Then the shadow moved, and I heard a familiar cough.
enormous:2.cnHint: 停电后我去储藏室找手电筒，墙上出现了一个____的影子。
enormous:2.hook: The shadow belonged to someone who was not supposed to be here.
enormous:2.line: 'That is an *enormous* box — did the Manager really order all of this?'

pet:2.en: A regular customer came in just before midnight carrying a small cage. Inside sat a tiny rabbit with one torn ear. She set the cage on the counter while she paid, and the rabbit pressed its nose to the bars and stared at me. 'He is my good-luck *pet*,' she said softly.
pet:2.cnHint: 一位客人深夜带着她的____来买东西，那只兔子一直盯着我看。
pet:2.hook: She had visited every night this week, always with the same worried look.
pet:2.line: 'My *pet* has not eaten since the lights went out — is it too warm in here?'

restaurant:2.en: During the blackout a delivery rider rushed in, soaking wet. He pulled a crumpled paper from his bag — a receipt from the *restaurant* two streets away. 'Wrong address again,' he said, dropping into a chair. The order was for someone in our store, yet nobody here had placed it.
restaurant:2.cnHint: 停电时一名外卖骑手冲进来，带着一张来自附近____的收据。
restaurant:2.hook: The name on the receipt matched the one on our lost-and-found notebook.
restaurant:2.line: 'The *restaurant* called and said someone here ordered forty dumplings — really?'

driver:2.en: A taxi stopped outside and the *driver* climbed out slowly, holding a small notebook. He knocked on the glass door and asked whether anyone had left it in his car around nine. The cover had our store's sticker on it. I checked the lost-and-found box: empty. My hands felt cold.
driver:2.cnHint: 一名出租车____带着一本小笔记本来到店里，想找失主。
driver:2.hook: The last page of the notebook held a hand-drawn map of our storage room.
driver:2.line: 'I am just the *driver* — but I think the owner really needs this back tonight.'

dream:2.en: The candles burned low and the store went very quiet. Tang sat on the step stool, eyes half shut. 'I had a strange *dream* last week,' he said without looking up. 'The fridge was full of light even though the power was off, and someone was reading a letter inside it.' He smiled oddly.
dream:2.cnHint: 停电的安静里，阿糖说起了他上周做的一个奇怪的____。
dream:2.hook: Tonight, the fridge door was open — and a folded letter sat on the top shelf.
dream:2.line: 'In my *dream* the letter had your name on it — is that not a little strange?'

consumer:2.en: I found a printed survey tucked under the counter — the Manager had left it before going home. It was a feedback form asking every *consumer* to rate the store's night service. Someone had already filled one in and left it on the pile. The score was zero, and there was one short note at the bottom.
consumer:2.cnHint: 我在柜台下找到一份调查问卷，有____已经填完并留下了一张评分。
consumer:2.hook: The handwriting on the note looked exactly like the Manager's own.
consumer:2.line: 'Every *consumer* gets a form tonight — even if the lights never come back on.'

interesting:2.en: Lin appeared at the back door with a torch and a box of batteries. 'Found these in my bag,' she said, looking too calm. I thought it was *interesting* that she had batteries on a night when every shelf in our store had sold out within an hour of the blackout starting. She met my eyes and smiled.
interesting:2.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林带着电池出现，我觉得这件事很____，因为店里的电池早就卖光了。
interesting:2.hook: She had been two hours off shift — yet her jacket was still damp from our storeroom.
interesting:2.line: 'Do you not find it *interesting* that I had exactly the right number of batteries?'

grade:2.en: A student sat on the floor near the window, reading by candlelight. She had opened her exam paper — the kind teachers return with a red mark at the top. I could not help looking. The *grade* circled in red was so low that she had drawn a tiny face next to it. It was smiling bravely.
grade:2.cnHint: 一名学生借着烛光看老师发回的试卷，试卷上那个____让人心疼。
grade:2.hook: She turned the paper over, pulled out a pen, and began writing something new.
grade:2.line: 'A bad *grade* is just the beginning of the story, right — that is what my mum says.'

rule:2.en: The power cut out just after midnight. I grabbed the flashlight from under the counter, then noticed a handwritten note taped to the register: 'Night-shift *rule* number one — candles are in the blue box, always.' The Manager had thought of everything. The blue box was exactly where the note promised.
rule:2.cnHint: 停电后，店员发现收银台上贴着店长留下的夜班____，里面写明了蜡烛的存放位置。
rule:2.hook: But the note had a second line, and someone had crossed it out.
rule:2.line: 'Night-shift *rule* number one — candles are in the blue box, always.'

plant:2.en: During the blackout I swept the floor by candlelight. Near the back shelf I found a small *plant* in a clay pot, tucked between the instant noodles. A sticky note on the pot read: 'Please water me on Tuesdays. — Tang.' I had no idea Tang kept living things here.
plant:2.cnHint: 停电时，店员在货架角落发现了同事阿糖偷偷养的一盆____，上面还留着便条。
plant:2.hook: The pot was warm, as if someone had just moved it there.
plant:2.line: 'I keep this little *plant* here because it makes the night shift feel less lonely.'

national:2.en: A customer came in during the outage, phone torch blazing. She bought four candles and a notebook, then pointed at the dark TV screen on the wall. 'I was watching the *national* chess finals,' she sighed. 'Third set. My favourite player was about to win.' She paid and left quickly.
national:2.cnHint: 一位顾客在停电时走进来，遗憾地说自己正在看转播全____象棋决赛。
national:2.hook: She came back ten minutes later, out of breath, holding a small radio.
national:2.line: 'I was right in the middle of the *national* chess finals when everything went dark.'

doctor:2.en: By candlelight I sorted the first-aid shelf. I found an old business card wedged behind the bandages: 'Dr. Chen, *doctor* of general medicine, available nights.' The card was dated three years ago. The Manager had never mentioned a house doctor. Or had he, and I simply forgot?
doctor:2.cnHint: 停电整理货架时，店员在绷带后面发现了一张多年前留下的____名片。
doctor:2.hook: The phone number on the card was the same as the store's landline.
doctor:2.line: 'A *doctor* who visits a convenience store at night — now that is a story worth knowing.'

economy:2.en: Tang arrived early for the handover, candle in hand. She set it on the counter and pulled out a small notebook. 'Power cuts cost us about forty yuan an hour in spoiled cold drinks,' she said, tapping the page. 'Simple *economy* — we should keep more ice packs in the freezer backup.' I decided then that Tang was the smartest person I knew.
economy:2.cnHint: 停电时，阿糖拿出笔记本算账，用____原则解释为什么备用冰袋很重要。
economy:2.hook: She flipped to the next page, and I saw my own name written at the top.
economy:2.line: 'Simple *economy* — ice packs cost less than the drinks we lose every blackout.'

global:2.en: Lin showed up during the outage, calm as ever, carrying a battery lamp. He set it on the counter without a word and opened his laptop. 'Checking the news,' he said. 'A *global* power grid report came out today. Blackouts like this one are up thirty percent worldwide.' He smiled. 'Not just us, then.'
global:2.cnHint: 停电期间，隔壁咖啡店的林带着电池灯来到店里，平静地告诉店员一份关于____停电趋势的报告。
global:2.hook: Lin's laptop screen showed our store's street on a live map, marked in red.
global:2.line: 'A *global* report says blackouts are up thirty percent this year — we are not alone.'

leader:2.en: Halfway through the outage, three neighbourhood kids crept in to buy snacks. The tallest one, who did all the talking, handed me exact change without being asked. 'He is our *leader*,' one of the smaller kids whispered proudly. The leader turned red. I gave them each a free biscuit for the walk home.
leader:2.cnHint: 停电期间，三个孩子来买零食，其中一个被同伴称为____，让店员忍俊不禁。
leader:2.hook: The leader paused at the door and glanced back at me, as if making a decision.
leader:2.line: 'They call me the *leader*, but I just carry the money because my pockets are bigger.'

scientific:2.en: Just before the lights came back, I found a folded paper on the floor near the door. It was a handwritten chart with columns, times, and temperatures — a *scientific* record of how quickly the ice cream freezer warmed up during past blackouts. At the bottom, in neat letters: 'Data collected over eight nights. — M.' The Manager, again.
scientific:2.cnHint: 停电快结束时，店员在地上捡到一张关于冰淇淋柜停电升温数据的____记录表。
scientific:2.hook: 'M' could stand for the Manager — or it could stand for someone else entirely.
scientific:2.line: 'A *scientific* record of every blackout we have had — the Manager misses nothing.'

evidence:2.en: The power cut left the store in darkness. I lit a candle and looked around. On the counter sat a half-eaten rice ball, a wet umbrella, and muddy boot prints leading to the back door. Enough *evidence* that someone had been here before me tonight.
evidence:2.cnHint: 停电后，我发现柜台上留下了某人到访的____。
evidence:2.hook: But the back door was locked from the inside.
evidence:2.line: 'There is clear *evidence* that someone came in through the back.'

prefer:2.en: Tang found two old torches in the supply room. She handed me the smaller one without asking. 'I *prefer* the big one,' she said simply, clicking it on and lighting up her cheerful face. Outside, the street was completely dark and very quiet.
prefer:2.cnHint: 停电时，阿糖说她____用大手电筒。
prefer:2.hook: Then we both heard a knock on the locked side door.
prefer:2.line: 'Honestly, I *prefer* working night shifts — fewer customers to argue with.'

interview:2.en: A young woman sat at the corner table, notebook open, small recorder running on batteries. She said she was here to *interview* people about life during power cuts. The Manager frowned from behind the candle. He did not look pleased to have a reporter in his store tonight.
interview:2.cnHint: 停电的夜里，有人来店里____附近居民的生活。
interview:2.hook: She smiled and turned her recorder quietly toward the Manager.
interview:2.line: 'I just want to *interview* the regulars — only five minutes, I promise.'

middle:2.en: The candles were arranged in a circle on the floor of the store. Tang placed a bowl of instant noodles right in the *middle*, steam rising in the warm light. It looked almost like a little festival. Three regulars sat around it, and nobody seemed to mind the darkness at all.
middle:2.cnHint: 停电时，大家围坐着，碗被放在圆圈____。
middle:2.hook: One of the regulars had not spoken a single word all evening.
middle:2.line: 'Put the candle in the *middle* of the table so everyone can see.'

standard:2.en: The Manager taped a handwritten sign to the door: 'Open as usual. *Standard* service, candle included.' A couple outside read it, laughed softly, and came in. I thought it was a funny sign. But the Manager looked completely serious, which somehow made it funnier.
standard:2.cnHint: 停电后店长贴出告示，宣布照____营业。
standard:2.hook: The couple ordered hot coffee, but the machine needed power.
standard:2.line: 'We keep *standard* hours no matter what — that is the rule here.'

subject:2.en: Lin came in during the blackout and leaned on the counter, ready to talk. Every time I tried to change the *subject*, she brought the conversation back to how many customers her store across the street had served today. I restocked shelves and nodded politely.
subject:2.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林来访，无论我怎么转移____，她总把话绕回来。
subject:2.hook: Then she noticed the reporter still sitting in the corner.
subject:2.line: 'Let us change the *subject* — how many people came in tonight?'

accept:2.en: A quiet old man placed a small paper bag on the counter and pushed it toward me. 'Just mooncakes,' he said. 'For the staff.' The Manager shook his head once, but I gave the man a small nod. Sometimes the right thing is to *accept* a kind gift with both hands.
accept:2.cnHint: 一位老先生送来点心，我决定____他的好意。
accept:2.hook: The Manager stared at the bag for a long moment after the man left.
accept:2.line: 'Please *accept* this — it is nothing, just a small thank-you from us.'

act:2.en: When the lights suddenly came back on, everyone in the store blinked and went quiet. Then the Manager smoothed his apron, stood straight, and gave a small nod, as if the whole blackout had been part of a planned *act*. A few customers actually clapped. Tang and I exchanged a look.
act:2.cnHint: 来电的瞬间，店长的表现像是精心安排的一场____。
act:2.hook: Nobody could tell if his calm face was real or practised.
act:2.line: 'That was quite an *act*, Manager — were you nervous at all?'

decline:2.en: The power cut hit at midnight. I found a note the Manager had left under the counter: 'Check the old sales log — look for any *decline* in snack sales after 2 a.m. If yes, cut the order.' I squinted at the numbers by torchlight. The drop was real. Someone, it seemed, had already known.
decline:2.cnHint: 停电后，店员在柜台下发现店长留下的便条，要求查看零食销售____的记录。
decline:2.hook: But the note was dated three nights ago — before the blackout was forecast.
decline:2.line: 'There's a clear *decline* in sales after two — we should cut the late order.'

extra:2.en: During the blackout, I found a small box behind the cleaning supplies. It held an *extra* set of store keys, a torch, and a folded list of emergency numbers. The Manager had packed it like a quiet gift for whoever ended up alone in the dark. I held the torch and felt oddly looked after.
extra:2.cnHint: 停电时，店员在清洁用品后面发现了一个备用箱，里面有____的钥匙和手电筒。
extra:2.hook: One number on the list was crossed out, with a new one written beside it in different ink.
extra:2.line: 'There is an *extra* torch in the box — the Manager left it there for nights like this.'

income:2.en: Tang lit a candle and pulled out a worn notebook. 'I track my *income* from every shift in here,' they said, tapping the cover. 'Night shifts pay a little more, so I always volunteer.' The candlelight made the numbers glow. I wondered what Tang was saving up for so carefully.
income:2.cnHint: 停电时，同事阿糖拿出笔记本，说自己一直记录每班的____。
income:2.hook: On the last page, Tang had written a single word that looked like a place name.
income:2.line: 'My *income* from night shifts is a bit higher, so I always sign up for them.'

medicine:2.en: A regular — a quiet older woman — knocked on the glass during the blackout. 'Do you still have cold *medicine*?' she asked through the door, her voice tired. I found two packets by torchlight and passed them through the gap. She pressed exact change into my hand without a word and walked back into the dark street.
medicine:2.cnHint: 停电时，一位老年常客敲门询问店里是否还有感冒____。
medicine:2.hook: She came back ten minutes later, not for herself, but carrying someone else.
medicine:2.line: 'Do you have any cold *medicine*? The shelves looked empty when the lights went out.'

private:2.en: I found a small envelope tucked behind the register with my name on it. Inside was a short note in the Manager's neat handwriting: '*Private* — for your eyes only. The tall man who buys green tea every Thursday night is not a customer. He is my brother. Please be kind to him.' I slipped the note into my pocket.
private:2.cnHint: 停电后，店员在收银机后发现一封写着自己名字的____信封。
private:2.hook: Thursday was tomorrow, and I had no idea what 'be kind' was supposed to mean.
private:2.line: 'This note is *private* — please do not leave it where other staff can read it.'

side:2.en: The emergency light only covered one *side* of the store, leaving the drink fridges in deep shadow. I used the Manager's torch to guide a customer to the water. He thanked me, then stood very still in the dark aisle for a long moment before leaving without buying anything.
side:2.cnHint: 停电时，应急灯只照亮了店铺的一____，店员用手电筒帮顾客找到了饮用水。
side:2.hook: He had been staring at a photo pinned to the community board, not at the drinks at all.
side:2.line: 'The light only reaches one *side* — use the torch if you need the fridges.'

air:2.en: When the power died, the hum of the fridges stopped and the whole store went silent. The *air* felt different — cooler, somehow, and very still, as if the building itself had taken a breath. Tang looked up from the candle and said, 'I actually like it better this way.' I was surprised to find I agreed.
air:2.cnHint: 停电后，店内所有机器停转，____变得格外安静清凉。
air:2.hook: Then something on the top shelf shifted and fell, though no one had touched it.
air:2.line: 'The *air* in here feels so still without the fridges — almost like being outside at night.'

consumption:2.en: I found a printout clipped to the staff board: 'Monthly power *consumption* — up 18% on last year. Please switch off display lights after midnight.' Below it, someone had added in pencil: 'Or just wait for the blackout to do it for you.' I laughed alone in the dark, then felt less alone for laughing.
consumption:2.cnHint: 停电期间，店员看到公告栏上贴着关于电力____上涨的通知，下面还有人用铅笔写了一句俏皮话。
consumption:2.hook: The pencil handwriting matched the note I had found behind the register.
consumption:2.line: 'Power *consumption* is up — please turn off the display lights after midnight.'

estimate:2.en: The power cut at midnight left the store in darkness. I found a box of candles behind the counter and lit three. The Manager called to check on us. 'My *estimate* is four hours before the grid comes back,' he said calmly. Tang and I looked at each other across the flickering light and said nothing.
estimate:2.cnHint: 停电后店长打来电话，对恢复供电的时间做出了____，小店只能靠蜡烛撑过漫漫长夜。
estimate:2.hook: But Tang's face in the candlelight said they knew something I didn't.
estimate:2.line: 'My *estimate* is four hours before the grid comes back.'

explore:2.en: With the lights out, I decided to *explore* the back room I had never entered before. My phone torch swept across stacked boxes, old receipts, and one small window that faced the alley. Something was taped to the inside of the door — a hand-drawn map of the whole block, with three shops circled in red ink.
explore:2.cnHint: 停电期间，店员借手机电筒____了平时从未进入的储藏室，意外发现了门后贴着的一张神秘地图。
explore:2.hook: One of the circled shops was ours.
explore:2.line: 'Let's *explore* that back room while the power is out.'

fix:2.en: A candle fell and dripped wax onto the old register. Tang grabbed a cloth and tried to clean it up fast. 'I can *fix* this before the Manager sees,' Tang whispered, scraping at the wax with a coin. The register beeped once, then went silent. We both froze.
fix:2.cnHint: 蜡烛打翻后，同事慌忙想在店长发现前____收银机上的蜡迹，却意外让机器发出一声怪响后沉默了。
fix:2.hook: Then a customer walked in and asked to buy something.
fix:2.line: 'I can *fix* this before the Manager sees.'

general:2.en: A woman came in carrying a sleeping child on her back. She moved through the dark store without any surprise, as if power cuts were a *general* part of her nights. She found the water shelf by memory, left exact change on the counter, and walked back into the dark street without a word.
general:2.cnHint: 一位背着孩子的女士在黑暗中从容地找到货架取水，停电对她而言似乎是生活中____的一部分。
general:2.hook: She had left an extra coin, and a folded note underneath it.
general:2.line: 'Power cuts are a *general* part of life around here.'

loss:2.en: Tang sat on the floor counting the day's cash by candlelight, face tight with worry. 'The ice cream in the freezer is all melting,' Tang said. 'That's a real *loss* for the Manager.' I checked the freezer. Every bar was soft. Outside, the street stayed dark and perfectly quiet.
loss:2.cnHint: 停电导致冷柜里的冰淇淋全部融化，同事忧心忡忡地说这对店长来说是一笔真正的____。
loss:2.hook: Then we heard a knock from inside the freezer.
loss:2.line: 'Melting ice cream is a real *loss* for the Manager.'

partner:2.en: Lin showed up at the door, phone torch shining, holding two warm meat buns from the shop across the street. 'Consider me your *partner* tonight,' Lin said with a grin. 'You have candles, I have food. Fair deal.' Tang and I let Lin in, though none of us spoke about why Lin knew we were alone.
partner:2.cnHint: 停电夜里，竞争对手林拎着热包子出现在门口，自称愿意做我们当晚的____，以食物换蜡烛。
partner:2.hook: Lin knew our schedule without ever being told it.
partner:2.line: 'Consider me your *partner* tonight — you have candles, I have food.'

concept:2.en: The old man who came in every night for hot tea seemed unbothered by the darkness. 'Young people have lost the *concept* of sitting still,' he said, settling onto the step stool by the counter. He wrapped both hands around his warm cup and closed his eyes. I had no answer for that.
concept:2.cnHint: 每晚来买热茶的老先生在烛光下感慨，年轻人已经失去了安静独处的____，说完便闭目养神。
concept:2.hook: When I looked again, his cup was empty and he was gone.
concept:2.line: 'Young people have lost the *concept* of sitting still.'

history:2.en: Sorting old papers in the back room, I found a notebook with the store's daily sales going back eleven years. Every page was in the same careful handwriting. The Manager had never mentioned this quiet *history* of the place. I turned to the very first entry and read a name I did not expect.
history:2.cnHint: 在储藏室翻找时，店员发现了一本记录这家小店长达十一年的手账，这段无声的____从未被店长提起过。
history:2.hook: The name on the first page was not the Manager's.
history:2.line: 'This notebook holds the whole *history* of our little store.'

attack:2.en: The power cut at midnight without warning. I was counting change by torch-light when a sharp *attack* of dizziness hit me — probably hunger. I grabbed a rice ball from the rack, sat on the step stool, and ate slowly. The store hummed with the backup fan. Outside, the street was perfectly still.
attack:2.cnHint: 停电后，叙述者突然感到一阵____，只好坐下来吃东西。
attack:2.hook: Then something moved in the dark storage room.
attack:2.line: 'An *attack* of dizziness — eat something before you fall over,' Tang said.

heavy:2.en: Tang dragged a crate of bottled water from the back room, her boots squeaking on the tile. 'Why is the emergency stock always this *heavy*?' she muttered. We stacked the bottles near the door by torch-light. The air felt thick and warm without the air-con, and every sound seemed louder than usual.
heavy:2.cnHint: 停电时，唐拖着一箱____的瓶装水，两人在手电筒光下整理物资。
heavy:2.hook: One bottle at the bottom had a handwritten label no one recognised.
heavy:2.line: 'This box is *heavy* — give me a hand before I drop it.'

thought:2.en: I sat behind the counter and let my mind wander. My first *thought* was that the blackout would last five minutes. An hour later, candles lined the windowsill and three regulars were sharing instant noodles on the floor. Funny how a dark store becomes a living room so quickly.
thought:2.cnHint: 停电后，叙述者原本____停电很快就会结束，结果却截然不同。
thought:2.hook: One of the regulars had not said a single word all night.
thought:2.line: 'My first *thought* was to go home, but somehow I stayed,' said Lin.

attract:2.en: Lin set a battery lantern on the magazine rack, and its soft glow seemed to *attract* every moth on the street. They tapped at the window in small, busy crowds. A boy outside pressed his face to the glass and stared at the flickering light as though it were the most wonderful thing he had ever seen.
attract:2.cnHint: 林摆出的灯笼____了窗外许多飞蛾，还有一个好奇的小男孩。
attract:2.hook: The boy slipped inside before anyone could react.
attract:2.line: 'A warm light will always *attract* people — and moths,' Lin said with a smile.

define:2.en: The Manager called from the back office, candle in hand. 'How do we *define* an emergency here?' he asked. Tang and I looked at each other. 'No power, no hot food, no working register,' I said. He nodded slowly, then added, 'And yet everyone stayed. Interesting.' He walked back without another word.
define:2.cnHint: 停电时，店长问我们如何____"紧急情况"，叙述者给出了自己的答案。
define:2.hook: The Manager's second question was much harder to answer.
define:2.line: 'Can you *define* what counts as an emergency tonight?' the Manager asked quietly.

executive:2.en: A woman in a neat jacket arrived just after one in the morning, looking out of place among the candles and noodle cups. She introduced herself as an *executive* from a company two streets away, stuck after a late meeting. She bought three energy drinks, sat on the step stool, and stared at her dark phone screen.
executive:2.cnHint: 深夜，一位公司____走进来，在烛光下独自坐着盯着熄屏的手机。
executive:2.hook: Her quiet sigh carried more weight than any word she had spoken.
executive:2.line: 'Even an *executive* needs somewhere warm when the lights go out,' she said softly.

expectation:2.en: My *expectation* before the first night shift was simple: scan items, restock shelves, stay awake. Nobody mentioned candle-lit strangers sharing snacks on the floor, or Tang teaching a delivery man to play cards by torch-light. I wrote 'adjust expectations' in my pocket notebook and underlined it twice.
expectation:2.cnHint: 叙述者入职前对夜班的____与真实情况相差甚远。
expectation:2.hook: The delivery man won every round, and nobody knew his name.
expectation:2.line: 'My *expectation* was a quiet night — so much for that,' I told Tang.

friendly:2.en: The boy who had slipped inside sat on a box of crisps, watching us work. Tang handed him a small juice carton without a word. He gave her a *friendly* nod — serious and solemn, the way children are when they feel treated as equals. I found a spare torch and let him hold it while we restocked the cold shelf.
friendly:2.cnHint: 唐递给男孩一盒果汁，他以一个____的点头表示感谢。
friendly:2.hook: When his mother finally appeared at the door, her expression was unreadable.
friendly:2.line: 'A *friendly* nod from a child is worth more than a long thank-you,' Tang said.

field:2.en: The power cut at midnight left the store lit only by my phone torch. A man in muddy boots walked in, holding a folded paper. 'I drew a map of the *field* behind the school,' he said, spreading it on the counter. 'Every puddle, every hole. The kids need a safe place to play.'
field:2.cnHint: 停电后，一位男士走进来，展开一张他亲手画的____地图。
field:2.hook: But the map showed something else — a small X near the old wall.
field:2.line: 'This *field* has three hidden puddles — I marked them all.'

personality:2.en: During the blackout Tang lit three candles and arranged them by height. 'Each candle has a *personality*,' Tang said seriously, tilting the tallest one a little. I tried not to laugh. The middle candle dripped wax onto a sticky-note pad, and Tang treated it like a small crime.
personality:2.cnHint: 停电时，阿糖点上蜡烛，认真地说每根蜡烛都有自己的____。
personality:2.hook: Then a customer arrived who clearly knew Tang from somewhere unexpected.
personality:2.line: 'A good shop has *personality* — that is why I keep coming back.'

size:2.en: The backup torch the Manager left was the *size* of my thumb. It threw a circle of light about as wide as a teacup. I swept it across the shelves trying to find the fuse box, knocking over a row of canned fish in the dark. Someone outside pressed their face to the glass and watched.
size:2.cnHint: 停电后，我发现备用手电筒的____小得可怜，根本照不了多远。
size:2.hook: The face at the glass belonged to someone who already knew where the fuse box was.
size:2.line: 'The *size* of that torch is a joke — let me lend you mine.'

schedule:2.en: Lin arrived at 1 a.m. with a handwritten *schedule* taped to a clipboard. Every column was filled with neat numbers. 'I track every power cut on this street,' Lin said, setting the clipboard on the dark counter. 'Tonight was late by four minutes.' I stared. Lin looked pleased.
schedule:2.cnHint: 停电那晚，隔壁咖啡店的林带着一份手写的____走进来，上面记录了这条街所有的停电情况。
schedule:2.hook: The last entry on the schedule was dated tomorrow night.
schedule:2.line: 'According to my *schedule*, the power comes back in twelve minutes.'

towards:2.en: I was edging *towards* the back room, torch in hand, when I heard a soft knock at the floor-level vent. A folded note slid through the gap, landed face-up on the tile, and read: 'Do not open the store room tonight.' The handwriting was very neat. The vent faced the alley.
towards:2.cnHint: 停电时，我正朝储藏室方向走去，一张纸条从通风口悄悄滑了进来。
towards:2.hook: The note used the same pen color as the Manager's training manual.
towards:2.line: 'Walk slowly *towards* the candles — the floor is wet near the fridge.'

background:2.en: A woman in a paint-stained coat bought one candle and stood reading its label for a long time. 'I use candles for *background* light when I paint at night,' she said. She paid in exact coins, all warm from her pocket. On her way out she paused, looked at the dark ceiling, and smiled at something I could not see.
background:2.cnHint: 一位女士买了一根蜡烛，说她画画时喜欢用烛光做____。
background:2.hook: The smile was aimed at the old photograph pinned above the door.
background:2.line: 'I need soft *background* light — bright light ruins the colors.'

department:2.en: A man in a rumpled shirt said he worked in the city records *department* and had come to check whether our address was listed correctly after last month's road works. He pulled out a damp form, smoothed it on the counter, and asked for a pen. The torch beam caught his badge. The name on it was not his.
department:2.cnHint: 停电中，一个自称在某政府____工作的男士来查我们店铺的地址信息。
department:2.hook: The badge photo matched someone who had been in the store two nights before.
department:2.line: 'The roads *department* sent me — I just need one signature here.'

detail:2.en: Tang had memorized every *detail* of the store layout and walked the dark aisles without bumping anything. 'Left shelf, third row, the tuna cans end here,' Tang murmured, placing my hand on cold metal. I was impressed until Tang walked straight into the mop bucket. The clang echoed all down the quiet street.
detail:2.cnHint: 停电后，阿糖凭记忆说出了货架的每一个____，却还是撞上了拖把桶。
detail:2.hook: Outside, someone had been waiting for exactly that sound.
detail:2.line: 'Every *detail* of this store is in my head — I have worked here three years.'

transform:2.en: The power cut at midnight. Within minutes, the dark store began to *transform*: Tang lit a row of small candles along the counter, the Manager arranged them in a careful line, and suddenly the cold, bright shop became something warmer and stranger, like a room from an old dream.
transform:2.cnHint: 停电后，店里的气氛被蜡烛彻底____了。
transform:2.hook: Then someone knocked on the locked door from outside.

additional:2.en: During the blackout I found a second till drawer nobody had mentioned. Inside were *additional* coins, a rubber band, and a folded note in the Manager's handwriting. Tang glanced over, saw my face, and quietly went back to counting stock as if the drawer did not exist.
additional:2.cnHint: 停电时，我发现了一个装有____物品的抽屉。
additional:2.hook: The note had today's date on it.
additional:2.line: 'There is one *additional* drawer — but ask the Manager first.'

journal:2.en: Tucked behind the back-room shelf I found a thin notebook. It was a *journal*, filled with short daily entries in neat handwriting — stock counts, odd customer remarks, small worries. The last entry stopped mid-sentence. The date was three weeks ago, the night of the previous blackout.
journal:2.cnHint: 我在储藏室发现了一本停电前留下的____。
journal:2.hook: The handwriting looked exactly like Tang's.
journal:2.line: 'Somebody left their *journal* here — should we tell the Manager?'

sort:2.en: The candles threw odd shadows and I could not tell one shelf from another. Tang showed me a *sort* of trick: group items by shape, not by label, so your hands find them in the dark. It worked. By two in the morning I could fill a bag without a single light.
sort:2.cnHint: 停电时，唐教我一种特别的____方法来摸黑找东西。
sort:2.hook: She learned that trick from someone who no longer worked here.
sort:2.line: 'This *sort* of skill takes one blackout to learn.'

understanding:2.en: Lin arrived just after the lights died, carrying a small torch. She said nothing about the rivalry between her store and ours. We shared the torch, checked the fridges together, and by the time the power came back I had a quiet *understanding* that competition looked different at two in the morning.
understanding:2.cnHint: 停电期间，我对林和我们店关系有了新的____。
understanding:2.hook: Before she left, Lin slipped a business card under the counter.
understanding:2.line: 'I think we have reached a small *understanding*, yes?'

citizen:2.en: An older man came in during the blackout holding a candle stub. He set it on the counter, bought nothing, and told me he had been a *citizen* of this street for forty years, watching every shop that had ever stood on this corner. He named six. Ours was the only one still open at midnight.
citizen:2.cnHint: 一位在这条街生活了四十年的老____在停电时走进了我们店。
citizen:2.hook: He said the corner had a habit of swallowing shops whole.
citizen:2.line: 'As a *citizen* of this street, I feel I should warn you.'

contrast:2.en: Tang placed one candle beside the energy-drink shelf. The bright cans and the soft flame made a sharp *contrast* — neon colours against warm gold light. I stood there longer than I should have. The Manager tapped my shoulder and pointed at the mop. The floor still needed cleaning, blackout or not.
contrast:2.cnHint: 烛光与货架上商品的颜色形成了强烈的____，让我忘了手头的活儿。
contrast:2.hook: In that warm light, the Manager's expression was hard to read.
contrast:2.line: 'What a *contrast* — bright tins and a single candle flame.'

establish:2.en: With no till screen working, I had to *establish* a simple system fast: one scrap of paper for sales, one for returns, totals circled in red. Tang watched me set it up, nodded once, and added a column I had missed. It was the first time I felt she trusted my thinking, even a little.
establish:2.cnHint: 停电时我需要迅速____一套手写记账的方法。
establish:2.hook: The column Tang added matched a number already on the back-room shelf.
establish:2.line: 'We need to *establish* a backup system before it happens again.'

indeed:2.en: The power cut at midnight left the store lit only by candles Tang had found under the counter. Customers crowded in, not to buy anything, but just for the light. It was *indeed* the warmest the store had ever felt. A boy in the corner kept staring at one particular candle as if it reminded him of something.
indeed:2.cnHint: 停电后便利店靠蜡烛照明，顾客们聚集在这里取暖，气氛____比平时更温馨。
indeed:2.hook: The boy had not moved for twenty minutes, and the candle was almost out.
indeed:2.line: 'It is *indeed* strange — he comes every blackout night, always alone.'

launch:2.en: During the blackout, Tang discovered an old radio behind the noodle shelf. After some fiddling, it crackled to life just in time to catch a broadcast about a rocket *launch* scheduled for dawn. Every customer in the store went quiet, tilting their heads toward the small speaker. One old woman smiled as if she already knew how the story ended.
launch:2.cnHint: 停电时，唐在货架后找到一台旧收音机，正好播报了一次火箭____的消息，所有人都静了下来。
launch:2.hook: The old woman whispered something to the radio that nobody else could hear.
launch:2.line: 'The *launch* is at five — if the power stays off, this radio is our only window.'

refer:2.en: The Manager had left a handwritten note taped to the register before the blackout. It said to *refer* to the blue folder under the counter if anything went wrong. Tang found the folder by phone-light. Inside was a single page — a hand-drawn map of the store with every fuse box marked. Someone had clearly been through this before.
refer:2.cnHint: 停电前，店长留下一张便条，让我们____蓝色文件夹来处理突发情况，里面藏着一张手绘地图。
refer:2.hook: The map had a note in the corner that said 'do not open the back room alone.'
refer:2.line: 'Always *refer* to the blue folder first — the Manager said it covers everything.'

trust:2.en: Lin appeared at the door just after the lights died, carrying a small battery lamp without being asked. 'I heard the grid went down,' Lin said simply, setting the lamp on the counter. There was a quiet kind of *trust* in that gesture — no rivalry, just a neighbor showing up. I made a note to think differently about Lin after that night.
trust:2.cnHint: 停电后，林主动带着电池灯赶来帮忙，这份不需要解释的____让我对他刮目相看。
trust:2.hook: Lin glanced once at the back shelf and then quickly looked away.
trust:2.line: '*Trust* me, I know where every spare battery in this block is kept.'

discussion:2.en: A small group of regulars gathered near the magazine rack during the blackout, sharing phone light and snacks. Their *discussion* started with how long the power might stay off and slowly drifted to childhood memories of storms and candles. I listened from behind the counter, learning more about the neighborhood in one hour than in all my shifts combined. One man had not spoken to his neighbor in three years — until tonight.
discussion:2.cnHint: 停电期间，几位老顾客聚在一起，从停电聊到了童年往事，这场____让陌生的邻居们突然熟络起来。
discussion:2.hook: The two neighbors exchanged numbers, but neither looked quite comfortable about it.
discussion:2.line: 'This *discussion* should have happened years ago — funny it took a blackout.'

extremely:2.en: The backup torch I found in the storage room was *extremely* dim — barely enough to light one shelf at a time. Still, a little girl visiting with her father thought it was the best torch she had ever seen and asked if she could hold it while her dad chose his snacks. She walked those aisles like she was leading an expedition. Her father watched her with the kind of tired, happy look that says everything.
extremely:2.cnHint: 备用手电筒____暗，但一个小女孩却把它当宝贝，像探险家一样照着货架走来走去。
extremely:2.hook: Before leaving, she pressed something small and folded into my hand.
extremely:2.line: 'It is *extremely* kind of you — she has been afraid of the dark for months.'

organize:2.en: When it became clear the power would not return quickly, Tang decided to *organize* all the candles, torches and snack items by the counter so customers could find things without wandering. It took ten minutes and turned the store from a confused huddle into something almost pleasant. A regular named nobody-yet — a quiet man in a grey coat — helped without being asked and then sat down in the corner as if he belonged there.
organize:2.cnHint: 停电后，唐开始____蜡烛和零食，让店里变得井然有序；一个灰衣男人默默帮了忙，然后就坐在角落里不走了。
organize:2.hook: The man in the grey coat had been here before — I just could not remember when.
organize:2.line: 'Let me help you *organize* this — I used to run a stall, I know the drill.'

pattern:2.en: By two in the morning I noticed a *pattern*: every ten minutes or so, the same young woman walked past the window, looked in, and walked on without entering. She never stopped, never waved, just looked. Tang said nothing but slid a warm meat bun to the edge of the counter, right by the door. The next time she passed, the bun was gone — and she did not come back after that.
